The author does, however, agree with Musk's broader claim that the majority of vehicle mileage will be autonomous within 5–10 years.

Notable quotes and data:
- Musk: "probably be widespread in the US by the end of this year"
- Musk (Summit): FSD on a "path" to being "at least an order of magnitude safer than humans"
- Musk (X, ~6 weeks prior): FSD is already "10X safer" than human drivers, "statistics are unequivocal"
- Unsupervised fleet: ~30 vehicles per RobotaxiTracker.com (Austin, Dallas: 5, Houston: 6)
- Q1 2026 earnings: Musk cited Q4 2026 "at the earliest" for unsupervised FSD in consumer vehicles
- January 2026: Musk raised required data milestone from 6 billion to 10 billion miles

articles.title: Elon Musk’s Inventing 'Jesus-level’ Technology ( Miracles)
articles.body:
This video features a live interview (conducted remotely from Austin, Texas, at approximately 2:30 AM local time) with Elon Musk at what appears to be a smart mobility or innovation conference in Israel. The interview covers Tesla's Full Self-Driving technology and robotaxi deployment, the future of humanoid robots, Neuralink breakthroughs, and SpaceX's Starship program, framed broadly around Musk's vision of transformative, near-miraculous technologies. The host draws out Musk's long-range predictions for autonomous mobility and the broader societal impact of AI and robotics.

## Autonomous Driving
1. **Vision-Only FSD Approach and Safety Claims:** Musk described Tesla's Full Self-Driving software as purely AI and camera-based, explicitly stating Tesla does not use radar or LiDAR. He argued this mirrors how humans drive — using vision and a biological neural net — and expects the approach to ultimately be "at least an order of magnitude safer than humans driving." He described the in-car experience as feeling like the car is "sentient" and "alive," with the sense of sentience growing as the software improves.

2. **Israel FSD Rollout:** Musk indicated that FSD approval in Israel may already be in place or forthcoming soon, saying "I think we may have or we'll get it soon hopefully," and invited the audience to experience it firsthand.

3. **10-Year Autonomous Driving Forecast:** Musk predicted that in approximately 10 years, roughly 90% of all distance driven will be handled by AI in self-driving cars, making human-driven cars a niche activity. He expressed high confidence in this trajectory, stating the path is "so obviously there" and does not keep him up at night.

## Robotaxi
1. **Unsupervised Robotaxi Operations in Three Texas Cities:** Musk confirmed that Tesla already has vehicles operating with no people inside and no safety monitors in three cities in Texas (consistent with RobotaxiTracker.com data showing unsupervised operations in Austin, Dallas, and Houston as of early May 2026). He added that widespread deployment across the US is expected by the end of this year (2026), with hopes for expansion to Israel as well.

## Humanoid Bots
1. **Humanoid Robots Predicted to Outnumber Humans:** Musk predicted that intelligent humanoid robots will far outnumber people in the future, describing Tesla's cars as effectively "four-wheeled robots" and noting a Tesla Optimus unit was on display at the conference exhibition. He referred to it jokingly as "Optimus subprime."

2. **Economic Impact — Universal High Income:** Musk argued that highly productive robots at scale could produce an economy 10 to even 100 times larger than today's. He framed this as leading to "universal high income" rather than universal basic income, where "pretty much anyone can have whatever they want." He acknowledged philosophical questions about human meaning in a world where AI and robots can outperform humans in every domain.

3. **Safety Concerns Acknowledged:** While optimistic, Musk noted the importance of never becoming complacent about robot safety, referencing the Terminator scenario as an unlikely but non-impossible outcome that warrants ongoing vigilance.

Notable quotes and data:
- "I expect this approach to ultimately be at least an order of magnitude safer than humans driving."
- "We already have some vehicles operating with no people inside and no safety monitors in three cities in Texas and probably will be widespread in the US by the end of this year."
- "If say like 10 years from now, probably 90% of all distance driven will be driven by the AI in a self-driving car."
- "My prediction is that there will be far far more robots — like intelligent robots — in the world than there will be people."
- "You can think of the output of the economy as productivity per capita times the population. If the robots are extremely productive and you have a lot of them, you're effectively going to have an economy that will be maybe 10 or even 100 times bigger than what it is today."
- On Neuralink's "blind sight" implant: "Even if somebody has lost both eyes… it will give them initially limited vision but I think over time very precise vision, perhaps superhuman vision."
- "Sort of what you might call like Jesus-level sort of technologies… miracles of science."
- The interview was conducted at approximately 2:30 AM Austin time, with Musk joining remotely while referencing a forthcoming SpaceX IPO.

articles.title: Waymo Has No Answer For FSD’s Move + 20 Top News Stories - Live 9am Pacific
articles.body:
This May 18, 2026 live stream from FutureAzA covers approximately 20 news stories spanning Tesla's robotaxi crash data release, Waymo's ongoing technical and PR struggles, Tesla FSD and vehicle updates, EV market developments, and broader automotive industry news. The host's core argument is that Tesla's autonomous driving approach (neural net-based) is fundamentally superior to Waymo's hand-coded system, and that Waymo's recent stumbles — combined with Tesla's relatively benign crash data — reinforce this thesis.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Tesla Robotaxi Crash Data Released — Less Alarming Than Portrayed:** Tesla reportedly released previously unredacted crash data for its robotaxi program, which the host suggests may have been accidental. Reviewing the 17 reported incidents, the host argues the vast majority are trivial: vehicles being rear-ended while stopped at stop signs or red lights (other drivers' fault), a mirror lightly touching a truck, a tire contacting a curb while parking, and a metro bus's bike rack making contact with the vehicle. The host also notes that one incident involved a pothole destroying a tire, which he argues should be classified as an incident rather than an accident. The host characterizes these as events that most drivers would not report to police and says none would concern him.

2. **FSD Version 14.3.2/14.3.3 Rolling Out with Spring Update:** A new FSD version — described as either 14.3.2 or 14.3.3 — has begun rolling out alongside a spring software update. The host notes one vehicle received FSD 14.3.2/14.3.3 and another received the spring update separately, calling the split deployment unusual. Smart Summon top speed has been increased from 6 mph to 8 mph. The host also notes that FSD's maximum speed is 85 mph (or 87 mph if the readout is switched to kilometers, as the cap is 140 km/h).

3. **Waymo Red Light Running Incident:** A Waymo vehicle was captured on video running a red light on a left turn, which the host describes as "terrifying" and says he doesn't know how Waymo fixes this. He contrasts this with Tesla's neural net approach, arguing that a vision-based system learns from observing other vehicles' behavior, whereas Waymo's rule-based system fails to generalize to novel edge cases.

4. **Waymo Flood/Standing Water Software Recall:** Waymo issued a software recall after vehicles in Texas were swept away by floodwaters. The host explains the underlying problem as a hand-coded rules conflict: vehicles were programmed both to avoid water and to proceed through it in certain conditions, leading to inconsistent behavior. He argues a neural net would have observed other cars safely navigating around standing water and followed suit, illustrating a structural advantage for Tesla's FSD approach.

5. **Waymo Neighborhood Training Loop Issue:** Waymo was observed sending approximately 50 cars repeatedly through a single residential cul-de-sac, apparently to collect training data. The host mocks the inefficiency and suggests it reflects a compute limitation rather than a perception limitation — noting the cars get stuck when a "slow children" sign is posted, congregating without resolution.

6. **Tesla Hiring for China FSD Road Testing:** A series of job postings attributed to Tesla in China signals significant expansion of FSD development activity there. Roles include data labelers, intelligent driving testers (with requirements for flexible domestic and international travel and on-site public road testing), and technicians for city-specific smart driving tests. The host frames this as a major signal of FSD momentum in China.

## Robotaxi

1. **Uber Publicly Criticizes Waymo's Expansion Strategy:** Uber executives have been taking direct shots at Waymo, criticizing its AVON (autonomous vehicle operations) model and warning that scaling proprietary AV technology while bypassing ride-hailing platforms is misguided. Waymo has expanded its service to five more cities without Uber. The host dismisses Uber's moral framing, pointing out Uber itself has retreated from many markets due to high costs and that Waymo's premium pricing also limits its reach to wealthier neighborhoods.

2. **Waymo Drunk Passenger Incident Raises Design Questions:** A passenger reportedly climbed into a Waymo's driver's seat while intoxicated. Waymo revoked the rider's access. The incident prompted discussion about why Waymo vehicles retain a driver's seat and steering controls at all, with the host suggesting this creates unnecessary confusion and risk. He contrasts this with a separate carjacking attempt where Waymo used remote communications to prevent the vehicle from moving until police arrived.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Tesla Model Y Price Increase:** Tesla raised prices on the Model Y: Rear-Wheel Drive and All-Wheel Drive variants each went up $1,000, while the Performance trim increased by $500. The host notes that even with this increase, the price remains lower in real terms than after the April 1, 2024 price increase when adjusted for inflation (~6% cumulative).

2. **Two New Paint Colors for Model 3 and Model Y in the US:** Tesla introduced Marine Blue and Frost Blue as new color options for Model 3 and Model Y in the United States. Canada receives only one of the two colors, which the host explains is due to differences in which factory supplies the Canadian market.

3. **California $1 Billion EV Truck Rebate Program:** California announced a billion-dollar rebate program for electric trucks. The host argues Tesla stands to capture a disproportionate share because no other manufacturer has the volume or competitive pricing to take full advantage of the program.

4. **BYD Flash Battery Demand Outpacing Supply:** BYD reported that battery supply is tight due to accelerating demand for its flash-charging EVs. The host notes an online debate in China over thermal management, referencing a live-stream test that recorded battery surface temperatures of 76°C during high-rate charging sessions. He questions whether most consumers actually need megawatt-level charging speeds.

5. **Congress Bill to Permanently Block Chinese Vehicles from US:** A bipartisan bill introduced by Michigan legislators (one Democrat, one Republican) would permanently ban vehicles from Chinese automakers if they contain China-developed software or connectivity systems. The host attributes the Michigan origin to domestic auto industry protectionism rather than genuine data-privacy concerns, and is skeptical the bill will advance.

## Market & Competition

1. **Toyota $2 Billion Texas Assembly Plant Expansion:** Toyota announced plans to invest up to $2 billion expanding its existing San Antonio facility, creating approximately 2,000 new jobs. The host notes the relatively modest job count reflects this being an expansion rather than a new greenfield factory.

2. **Volkswagen-Backed Gotion Launches Sodium-Ion Battery:** Gotion (Volkswagen-backed) launched a sodium-ion battery claiming up to 261 Wh/kg for the high-energy version and 162 Wh/kg for the low-temperature version, described as mass-production ready. The host, while generally skeptical of "miracle battery" announcements, notes Gotion is a real company with credible (non-outrageous) claims, though he flags that sodium-ion cells are bulkier than comparable lithium cells despite competitive weight.

3. **TSMC Arizona Expansion:** TSMC announced a $20 billion expansion of its Arizona semiconductor facility, though the host notes the project faces water shortages, labor shortages, and complications from visa rules.

4. **Delta Airlines Rejected Starlink, Now Behind United:** Delta rejected Starlink in-flight internet because it required branding as a "Delta portal" rather than a generic Starlink connection. United Airlines adopted Starlink and is now years ahead in connectivity. The host frames this as Delta prioritizing brand optics over customer experience, at significant competitive cost.

5. **Ethiopia EV Import Surge:** Ethiopia imported a record 19,000 Chinese EVs in 2024 and has doubled that figure to 44,000 in 2025, driven by expanding domestic hydroelectric power capacity. The host highlights this as a model for energy security through domestic electricity production.

6. **GM 2027 Chevy Bolt Production Efficiency:** GM announced a production improvement for the 2027 Bolt involving batching cars by color and trim (30 units at a time) to reduce paint shop downtime and cleaning frequency between color changes. The host jokes that GM has rediscovered basic assembly-line principles.

7. **Mazda EV Delay:** Mazda announced a two-year delay on its next EV while effectively admitting development had not yet begun. The host references the Mazda MX-30 (100 miles range, $35,000) as an example of Mazda's historically weak EV commitment.

Notable quotes and data:
- Tesla robotaxi crash data: 17 reported incidents, host argues nearly all are trivial (rear-endings by other drivers, minor contact events, pothole tire damage)
- FSD max speed: 85 mph (or 87 mph / 140 km/h depending on display units)
- Smart Summon top speed increased from 6 mph to 8 mph in the new FSD build
- New FSD version rolling out: 14.3.2 or 14.3.3 with spring update
- Model Y price increases: RWD +$1,000, AWD +$1,000, Performance +$500
- BYD battery surface temp during fast charge: 76°C
- Gotion sodium-ion battery: 261 Wh/kg (high energy), 162 Wh/kg (low temperature)
- TSMC Arizona expansion: $20 billion
- Toyota San Antonio expansion: up to $2 billion, ~2,000 jobs
- Ethiopia EV imports: 19,000 in 2024 → 44,000 in 2025
- California electric truck rebate program: $1 billion
- "Waymo has no answer for FSD's move" — host's framing of Waymo's structural inability to match Tesla's neural net adaptability

articles.title: The Market is Flashing Red Flags And Tesla Drops 5% On Friday - Do We Have A PROBLEM?
articles.body:
This video from "investingagainstthegrain" covers a range of macroeconomic and geopolitical red flags the host believes are flashing warning signs for the broader market, with a specific focus on Tesla's 5% single-day drop on Friday, May 16, 2026. The host's core thesis is that while the bull case remains intact longer-term (driven by AI, capex spending, and political incentives to resolve the Iran conflict before midterms), the near-term setup is risky enough to warrant caution and tactical positioning. Tesla is viewed as a high-conviction long-term hold, but the host expects a short-term pullback to be healthy and uses covered calls to manage the position.

## Market & Competition

1. **Geopolitical Risk and Oil Prices:** The host opens by flagging a significant spike in oil prices — WTI opening up approximately 2% to over $107/barrel and Brent crude over $110/barrel — driven by escalating tensions involving the U.S., Israel, and the UAE against Iran. Reports of a Tuesday White House Situation Room meeting on military options, a massive U.S. Air Force airlift of weapons to the Middle East, and Trump's public statement warning Iran that "the clock is ticking" are cited as signals that kinetic military action may be imminent. The host notes that the last time similar firepower was moved into the region, full-scale conflict began within 72 hours.

2. **Midterm Election Seasonality as a Bearish Headwind:** The host highlights historical S&P 500 performance data showing that the market has struggled from May to October during midterm election years, with only one such year being positive. With 2026 being a midterm year, the host treats this seasonal pattern as a serious risk factor, noting that the current macro environment (hot CPI, hot PPI, rising 10-year yields) makes it unlikely this year will be an exception.

3. **Tom Lee's "Painful Summer" Warning:** Tom Lee — described as the most accurate market forecaster of the last decade — is cited as predicting a painful summer for markets. His thesis involves the historical pattern that 10 out of the last 14 times a new Fed chairman takes office, the market tests that chairman with a selloff. The host partially disagrees with the framing but acknowledges Tom Lee's strong track record and treats the warning as a meaningful signal that cannot be ignored.

4. **CME Rate Expectations and Inflation Stickiness:** The CME is currently pricing in a rate *hike* in January 2027, with no rate cuts expected between now and then — even with an incoming new Fed chairman (Kevin Warsh). The host frames this as a sign the market is worried about persistent inflation, driven largely by oil supply constraints from the Strait of Hormuz situation. The 10-year Treasury yield is cited as creeping up to 4.5–4.6%, with the host asserting that sustained 4.5–5% 10-year yields are incompatible with current market valuations.

5. **Speculative Euphoria in Leveraged ETFs:** The host points to heavy retail and institutional interest in triple-leveraged semiconductor ETFs (specifically mentioning "SOX," a 3x leveraged semiconductor ETF) as a sign of late-cycle euphoria and speculative excess. Historically, the host views such instruments as indicators of market tops or near-top conditions.

6. **Gavin Baker's Semiconductor Cycle Warning:** Gavin Baker, former Fidelity fund manager and current independent fund manager, is cited from a recent interview in which he stated that historically this is the moment to sell memory companies. Baker had previously predicted Micron's strong run in a late 2025 appearance on the All-In podcast. However, Baker hedged by noting the AI revolution makes this cycle potentially different, leaving the directional call ambiguous but adding to the bull-bear tension the host is tracking.

7. **Nvidia as Potential Market Lynchpin:** With Nvidia earnings due Wednesday (approximately May 21, 2026), the host expresses strong conviction that Nvidia will deliver its best quarter ever, pointing to strong results across AMD, cloud providers (Amazon Trainium, Google TPUs), and Neoclouds as indirect evidence of insatiable Nvidia GPU demand. The host speculates Nvidia could trade at $250–$270 post-earnings and frames a strong Nvidia print — combined with a potential Iran resolution — as the catalyst that could push the S&P 500 toward 8,000.

8. **Year-to-Date Market Performance (MAG 7):** As of the video's publish date, the host reviews year-to-date performance: S&P 500 up ~1.5% (having swung from -~10% to current levels), Dow Jones up ~3%, Nasdaq up ~12.9% (swinging from approximately -12% to +12%). Among the Magnificent 7, Alphabet leads at +27%, Amazon at +14.4%, Apple at +10%, Meta at +6.9%, and Nvidia at +20%. Tesla is the laggard, down approximately 3.61% year-to-date, and was further hit by a 5% single-day drop on Friday.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Tesla's 5% Single-Day Drop — Context and Reaction:** Tesla dropped 5% on Friday, May 16, 2026, which the host attributes primarily to broader market selling pressure (Iran conflict, rising yields, NASDAQ/S&P selloff) rather than any Tesla-specific negative news. The host frames this as a healthy technical pullback on the daily chart rather than a sign of fundamental weakness, noting that Tesla's weekly and monthly charts remain "extremely healthy."

2. **Tesla's Tactical Positioning — Covered Calls Strategy:** The host describes having sold covered calls on Tesla at $560, then rolled them down to $545 to capture additional premium as the stock began pulling back. The host plans to continue rolling covered calls down as the stock declines but emphasizes not being greedy and not risking long-term share assignment. The host states that if Tesla reached $560 within the next 10–20 days, that would represent an overextension requiring a giveback before resuming higher.

3. **Tesla as Long-Term Conviction Hold:** The host distinguishes Tesla from commodity-cycle plays like Micron and SanDisk, describing Tesla as an "NF1 company" — a category-defining, one-of-a-kind business — that warrants a buy-and-hold approach rather than a trade-and-rotate strategy. The host expresses expectation that Tesla will bottom out by end of the week (approximately May 23, 2026) and resume an upward trend the following week.

Notable quotes and data:
- WTI crude oil opened up ~2% to over $107/barrel; Brent crude over $110/barrel (as of video recording).
- S&P 500 year-to-date: +~1.5%; Nasdaq: +~12.9% (swung from approximately -12% to +12%); Dow: +~3%.
- Tesla year-to-date: -3.61%; dropped 5% in a single session on Friday, May 16, 2026.
- Alphabet YTD: +27%; Amazon: +14.4%; Nvidia: +20%.
- 10-year Treasury yield cited at 4.5–4.6% and rising.
- CME pricing in a rate *hike* in January 2027; no rate cuts expected before then.
- Tom Lee: 10 out of last 14 new Fed chairman transitions saw the market test that chairman with a selloff.
- S&P 500 has historically struggled May–October in midterm election years; only one such year was positive.

articles.title: Bosch’s Hydrogen Fuel Cell Power Module | ACT Expo 2026
articles.body:
This video is an interview conducted by Armen from Munro Live at ACT Expo 2026, featuring Peter Tadros, President of Power Solutions in North America at Bosch. The conversation covers Bosch's hydrogen fuel cell power module (the C300), its applications in heavy-duty trucking and stationary power generation, as well as Bosch's battery management systems and an autonomous trucking collaboration with Kodiak. The core thesis is that Bosch embraces a "multi-energy platform" philosophy — no single silver bullet — and is developing technology-neutral solutions ready for the market at whatever pace adoption occurs.

## Market & Competition

1. **Bosch C300 Hydrogen Fuel Cell Power Module:** Bosch unveiled the C300, a second-generation hydrogen fuel cell power module rated at 300 kilowatts. This is an upgrade from the previous generation, the C190, which was rated at 190 kW. The C300 features two horizontal fuel cell stacks with a single shared power transfer unit and integrated controls, making it more efficient by using one set of components to control both stacks. Peter Tadros confirmed this is a functioning unit with Start of Production (SOP) imminent — not yet in full production. The module is designed to drop into a Class A (Class 8) truck in the same footprint as a diesel engine, fitting between the frame rails.

2. **Design Changes from C190 to C300:** The transition from 190 kW to 300 kW required the stacks to be oriented horizontally to maintain the same width envelope required for Class A trucks. The unit is slightly longer and slightly taller than the C190, but the width constraint — critical for fitting between frame rails — was preserved. The turbo pump at the rear of the unit serves a circulation function.

3. **Stationary Power / Data Center Application:** Tadros highlighted an adjacent use case for the C300 in stationary power generation, particularly for data centers facing power demand crunches. The module can serve as a primary, secondary, or backup power source. He noted that hydrogen pipelines already run through parts of the country, enabling data centers located near those pipelines to use hydrogen as a primary energy source. Because the unit was developed and validated to automotive standards — which are more demanding (vibration, corrosion, temperature swings) than stationary environments — adapting it to stationary use is relatively straightforward, requiring no new R&D from scratch.

4. **Hydrogen Sourcing and Heavy-Duty Trucking Use Case:** Tadros acknowledged that hydrogen mobility in the US has slowed but emphasized the product is ready when the market catches up. For long-haul trucking, hydrogen's key advantages over battery-electric include faster refueling (under 45 minutes per Bosch's fueling solutions on display), no battery weight penalty (which reduces payload and revenue for fleet operators), and higher uptime — a critical total cost of ownership (TCO) factor. The practical near-term model is deploying hydrogen trucks on fixed corridors where hydrogen supply is already established, building operational data, then expanding infrastructure.

5. **Battery Management System with Dual-Use Application:** Bosch also displayed a battery management system capable of monitoring, controlling, and disconnecting battery systems. Like the hydrogen module, this product has a dual-use philosophy: it serves both mobility applications (hybrid and electric vehicles) and stationary energy storage. Tadros noted the company is receiving significant customer interest and requests for the energy storage application of this system.

6. **Autonomous Trucking Collaboration with Kodiak:** Bosch showcased a sensor pod developed in collaboration with Kodiak for autonomous Class A trucks. The sensor pod — featuring radar and cameras — replaces one set of side mirrors on existing conventional trucks, enabling driverless operation without requiring a new electric or hydrogen truck platform. The stated goals are addressing driver shortages and extending operational hours. Tadros noted that extensive testing and route validation work is ongoing with Kodiak. For stationary hydrogen applications specifically, Bosch is collaborating with a company called PowerCell, which serves as Bosch's sales channel for that market segment.

Notable quotes and data:
- C300 = 300 kW hydrogen fuel cell power module; C190 (previous gen) = 190 kW
- Two horizontal fuel cell stacks with one shared power transfer unit and integrated controls
- Hydrogen refueling time: under 45 minutes per Bosch's fueling solutions
- C300 SOP: "soon" — currently a functioning pre-production sample
- Autonomous trucking sensor pod: radar + cameras, replaces primary side mirrors on existing Class A trucks
- Collaboration partners: Kodiak (autonomous trucking), PowerCell (stationary hydrogen sales)
- Peter Tadros: "There's no one silver bullet in this. We have to diversify."
- "Invented for life" — Bosch tagline closing the interview

articles.title: Daily X Summary (2026-05-18)
articles.body:
## Executive Summary
Today's posts are dominated by hands-on coverage of Tesla's FSD V14.3.3 rollout (bundled with the Spring Update), featuring several notable UI and capability improvements. A Cybercab sighting in Las Vegas adds a minor Robotaxi data point. The overall signal is mildly bullish — iterative FSD progress is visible and tangible, though no major fleet, financial, or regulatory breakthroughs were reported.

---

## Key Posts / Themes

1. **FSD V14.3.3 Rolls Out with Spring Update — Multiple Notable Changes:** The headline news is the release of FSD V14.3.3 (software version 2026.14.6.6), which began rolling out on May 17. Sawyer Merritt downloaded it on his Model Y and documented several changes firsthand. The most functionally significant is a **33% increase in Actually Smart Summon (ASS) top speed**, raised from 6 mph to 8 mph (13 km/h). Merritt noted the speed increase is perceptible in real-world use, allowing the vehicle to "flow better with traffic." Additionally, the update introduces a **live intervention counter on the main screen**, displaying miles driven on FSD since the last intervention and resetting to zero upon disengagement. The **Self-Driving App** will also track a user's longest intervention-free streak — a feature with potential implications for Tesla's data collection and safety narrative. Finally, Tesla updated the **FSD intervention popup categories**: "Preference" and "Discomfort" were replaced with "Parking" and "Other" (alongside the retained "Navigation" and "Critical" options), suggesting Tesla is refining how it classifies and learns from driver takeovers. New visualizations in the Spring Update were also highlighted as visually improved.

2. **Cybercab Spotted in Las Vegas:** A Cybercab was observed driving around Las Vegas on May 17, with Merritt sharing footage. No operational context (supervised vs. unsupervised, testing vs. public service) was provided. This is a geographically notable sighting — Las Vegas is not among the cities currently tracked by RobotaxiTracker.com — but without further detail it remains a low-signal data point, possibly indicating expanded testing geography.

3. **SpaceX Starship V3 Test Flight Scheduled Same Day as Model S/X Signature Delivery Event:** SpaceX is targeting Wednesday, May 20 at 6:30 PM ET for the first Starship V3 test flight, which coincides with Tesla's Model S/X Signature delivery event in California. This is primarily a scheduling/media note. For Tesla investors, the delivery event itself is the more relevant signal — it marks a notable moment for the refreshed Model S/X — though Merritt did not elaborate further on the delivery event details.

---

## Signal Strength: **Mildly Bullish** — FSD V14.3.3 delivers concrete, user-visible improvements to autonomy UX and data transparency, reinforcing the ongoing iteration cadence, though no step-change in capability, fleet deployment, or regulatory progress was announced.

---

## Brief

- FSD 14.33 released; Elon confirms 14.3 branch sufficient for unsupervised deployment.
- Belgium begins 5,000 km FSD supervised trial; EU vote window summer–autumn 2026.
- Tesla unredacts all 17 NHTSA robotaxi crash reports; teleoperator failures documented.
- Las Vegas Cybercab maintenance facility permitted; launch targeted within ~45 days.
- Model Y prices raised $500–$1,000 — first increase in approximately two years.
- Megapack contracts: $2.7B Georgia Power, $556M China, 1 GWh Scotland signed.
- Tesla capex guidance raised to >$25B for 2026.

## Autonomous Driving

- **FSD 14.3 confirmed sufficient for unsupervised deployment; v15 is upside, not a gate.** Elon stated 14.3 is "significantly safer than human" driving and sufficient for unsupervised FSD in legal jurisdictions. Version 15 — described as a "complete overhaul of the software architecture" running on AI4 — is targeted "hopefully later this year, certainly by early 2027," framing it as a further magnitude improvement rather than a prerequisite for rollout.

- **FSD 14.33 released mid-week**, rated "extremely positive" by the Mars Catalog. The 14.3 branch represents a full stack revamp; Bhakdi argues iteration speed on this architecture is systematically underestimated by the market. Cortex 2 came online at 250 MW (~April 2026), training both FSD and Optimus, with 500 MW targeted by mid-2026.

- **European regulatory wave accelerating.** Belgium announced a 5,000 km (~3,000 mile) FSD Supervised trial across Flemish roads, with officials stating Tesla could begin "tomorrow." Sweden's Transport Agency publicly supports FSD and flagged a consumer launch "at the earliest during summer or autumn 2026." Ireland confirmed active approval talks. The Netherlands has already issued type approval; the May 21 EU-wide one-time FSD purchase deadline is converting European markets to subscription-only ARR.

- **China FSD approval flagged as the highest-priority near-term catalyst.** Elon's primary stated objective on the Trump–Xi Beijing trip was Chinese regulatory FSD approval. Tesla posted China-specific FSD data labeling roles and robotaxi engineering positions with "urgent" language — the first time city-level China robotaxi hiring has appeared. An unverified report cited ~1,000 employee vehicles in a China employee FSD beta with NDAs required.

- **Tesla Vision airbag pre-deployment confirmed fleet-wide.** Camera-based crash prediction pre-deploys airbags and seatbelt tensioners up to 70ms earlier than impact-sensor systems — shipping standard on new vehicles and arriving via OTA to all Tesla Vision cars. Separately, a coast-to-coast FSD 14.3.2 drive completed 2,833 miles with zero disengagements, beating the prior record by 8.5 hours.

## Robotaxi

- **Zero injuries confirmed across the program's full deployment history.** Elon and Ashok both stated no accidental injuries to passengers have occurred. Elon explicitly characterized the primary scaling bottleneck as "convenience issues — the car gets paranoid and gets stuck" (routing loops, construction zone overcaution), not safety performance. Elon confirmed robotaxi revenue will be "not super material this year" but "material in a significant way" in 2027.

- **Las Vegas infrastructure being staged for imminent launch.** Tesla filed a Clark County permit for a ~36,000 sq ft automated Cybercab car wash/maintenance facility on May 12; Dillon Loomis cites a ~45-day launch target. Cybercabs were also spotted on public roads in Miami and Colorado — beyond all previously known operating markets — indicating active geographic stress-testing.

- **Cybercab production is ramping and units are moving off the lot.** Drone footage confirmed ~70 Cybercabs in the Giga Texas outbound lot; ~14 new production units were observed departing in a single session. Production rate estimates range from 5–15/day (Loomis) to 20–40/day (Tegtmeyer/brighterwithherbert). No Cybercabs have entered live passenger service; all current unsupervised rides are Model Ys.

- **Rerating threshold requires ~5,000 vehicles, per Munster.** Gene Munster (Deepwater) states the current unsupervised fleet represents "incrementally positive but likely priced in" territory. A step-function re-rating requires 5,000+ vehicles and 5–10% visible ride-hailing share — at that point, 10,000 vehicles by year-end is cited as a $700–$1,000 stock catalyst. Current Tesla robotaxi daily mileage (~80,000/day) versus Waymo (~4M/day) reflects the scale gap remaining.

- **Austin operational data reveals meaningful service gaps.** A three-week April study found rides unavailable 27% of checks, wait times over 15 minutes ~50% of the time, and effective service shutoff after 5 PM on weekdays. Dallas drew criticism for navigation errors and destination inaccuracies. Tesla operates ~50 vehicles in Austin versus Waymo's ~250+ there. Per Loomis, Houston's and Dallas's geofences remain very small, with Houston excluding downtown entirely.

## Optimus

- **Optimus V3 design reportedly signed off**, per an unverified but cited source on X. Supply chain signals remain the most concrete data: Chinese suppliers confirmed 70,000-unit supply chain readiness for 2026 (per Tesla Ming, December 2025 leak), and Bhakdi interprets capital expenditure commitments by those suppliers as the credibility signal. Tesla is hiring data collection operators across ~12 facilities, consistent with Musk's target of ~5,000 internal training units.

- **Fremont line conversion confirmed underway; production not yet begun.** Model S/X manufacturing equipment is being removed and Optimus assembly infrastructure installed, with 1M units/year as the long-term Fremont target. Per brighterwithherbert, Optimus is currently being tested inside Tesla factories but has not started independent production work. No official Tesla 2026 unit production target has been issued.

- **Wall Street still assigns zero value to Optimus.** Piper Sandler (Potter) explicitly states investors are "getting Optimus for free" at $400/share and will begin modeling it only once revenue arrives. Munster agrees and adds that a third-party commercial customer taking delivery at scale — not factory deployment — is the true rerating catalyst. Munster rates meaningful scale as genuinely 5–10 years out; Elon's 1M-unit-next-year target is not credible to the market.

## Tesla Semi

- **First production-line Semi rolled off Giga Nevada in April 2026**, roughly nine years post-announcement. The Sparks facility is designed for 50,000 trucks/year. Covenant Logistics began a 3-week commercial demo on May 13 running full freight loads on the 500-mile variant in California — the most concrete commercial validation step to date. Estimated annual fuel savings of $60,000–$80,000/truck versus diesel imply a 3–5 year payback.

- **Tesla Semi E-PTO eliminates diesel auxiliary motors on refrigerated trailers**, delivering 25 kW to reefer loads. Early Covenant Transport pilot results described as positive, with ~50% cost-per-mile savings cited in California. European website listing (UK, standard range only) signals a 2027 launch cadence; Giga Berlin is the speculated manufacturing site.

## Energy

- **Multiple large Megapack contracts confirmed as executed purchase orders** this week: $2.7B with Georgia Power (3+ GW), 1 GWh in Scotland, 240 MW in France (one of the country's largest), and $556M grid battery project in China. A new Megablock product is scheduled to ramp H2 2026. The Energy backlog was flagged as a metric to watch at the next earnings call.

- **BYD surpassed Tesla as world's top BESS integrator in 2025**: 60+ GWh shipped (13% share) versus Tesla's 46.7 GWh (10%), per Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. BYD's HaoHan system offers 14.5 MWh per standard unit versus Megapack 3's 5 MWh — a structural density gap. Eight of the top 10 global integrators are Chinese.

- **Giga Berlin 4680 expansion: $250M investment targeting 18 GWh annual capacity**, up from 8 GWh, with ~1,500 new jobs. Cell production start is H1 2027. At 18 GWh, the facility would supply cells for an estimated 240,000–250,000 vehicles per year — approaching full Giga Berlin output.

## Electric Vehicles

- **Model Y prices raised for the first time in approximately two years.** Premium RWD rises to $45,990 (+$1,000), Premium AWD to $49,990 (+$1,000), Performance AWD to $57,990 (+$500); base trims unchanged. Electrek reads this as a margin-capture move on high-profitability configurations, not a broad demand signal. Panasonic simultaneously raised its US battery forecast +19% to 46 GWh for the fiscal year ending March 2027, explicitly citing Tesla market share recovery.

- **Model Y L confirmed for Southeast Asia/Singapore and expected US arrival by end of 2026.** Bay Area test sightings and a brief US website appearance cited as near-term launch signals; pricing expected ~$55,000–$60,000. Lower-cost Cybertruck (~$59,000) deliveries expected June 2026.

- **Canada's 49,000-vehicle/year Chinese EV import quota positions Tesla to dominate.** Tesla is expected to claim a disproportionate share via Giga Shanghai Model 3 exports given its existing Canadian retail and service infrastructure. BYD is planning 20 Canadian sites in 2026 but has no existing sales infrastructure; the Canadian government is reportedly debating per-manufacturer allocation caps specifically due to Tesla's likely dominance.

## Financials

- **Tesla capex guidance raised from >$20B to >$25B for 2026**, against >$30B cash on hand. Munster characterized the market's negative reaction as a "headscratcher" for a company investing in robotaxi, Optimus, and compute infrastructure that represent paradigm-level bets. Q1 2026 profit ran at approximately $63M/day; FSD subscriptions contributed ~6.9% of profit — described as higher than expected given margin profile.

- **Tesla owns ~9% of XAI and has invested ~$2B**, per brighterwithherbert compute analysis. The host argues this stake — combined with Cortex 2 training both FSD and Optimus — provides Tesla shareholders indirect AI infrastructure exposure the market is not yet pricing. Piper Sandler's full model projects ~$96B Tesla revenue in 2026, $155B by 2030, and $1.7T by 2045, with Optimus entirely excluded.

## Market & Competition

- **SpaceX IPO: ticker SPCX, pricing June 11, first trade June 12**, targeting $1.75–$2T valuation; book reportedly 4x oversubscribed in round one. Tesla–SpaceX merger assigned >50% probability within five years by Munster (~$3T combined today). Bhakdi's merger modeling shows it is net negative for Tesla shareholders in year one (~38% return vs. ~50% standalone) but a long-term winner by year two and three.

- **Legacy OEM deterioration accelerating.** Honda posted its first-ever annual loss (>$9B restructuring costs) and abandoned its 2040 full-EV target. Nissan remains in deep distress. Mazda cut EV investment from ~¥1.5T to ~¥830B through 2030. Porsche cut 500+ jobs. China BEV penetration exceeded 40% of new car sales; US EV share sits at ~9%.

- **Macro headwinds rising.** 10-year Treasury yield moved from 4.46% to 4.6% on the week; 30-year approaching 5%. Bhakdi flags yen carry trade reversal risk, rising European and Japanese bond yields, and potential Strait of Hormuz oil disruption (EIA projecting up to 10.8M barrels/day loss at peak, JP Morgan warning commercial inventory stress by early June) as structural threats to US equity positioning.

## Bear Case of the Week

- **Tesla's Austin robotaxi crash rate is ~4x worse than the human driver average.** Reuters calculated approximately one crash per 57,000 autonomous miles versus the human baseline of ~1 per 229,000 miles, using Tesla's own vehicle safety data and 15 NHTSA-reported incidents since August 2025. Tesla had been the only ADS operator to fully redact all crash narratives; the year-long redaction was characterized by Electrek's Lambert as "a self-inflicted wound" that amplified the damage when the reports were finally released.

- **Teleoperator failures caused two confirmed accidents.** In July 2025, a remote operator drove a vehicle into a metal fence at 8 mph; in January 2026, a remote operator drove a stopped vehicle into a construction barricade at ~9 mph. Both incidents occurred with no passengers aboard, but they document a systemic risk in the operations model — and Loomis flagged this as a scaling concern as Tesla moves toward removing safety monitors entirely.

- **Austin service quality remains far below commercial-grade.** Rides unavailable 27% of all daily checks over three weeks in April; wait times exceeded 15 minutes ~50% of the time and 25 minutes more than 25% of the time. Effective service shuts down after 5 PM on weekdays. Loomis stated flatly: "I'm very confident you're going to end up disappointed unless we see significant geofence expansion." Houston's geofence excludes downtown; Dallas had a 5-mile trip that took nearly two hours.

- **Waymo is operating at a scale that makes the current Tesla deployment look minimal.** Waymo delivers 500,000+ paid rides per week across 10 US cities, fully driverless, 24/7 — against Tesla's ~80,000 autonomous miles per day. Munster's formulation: "The score is 50 to zip." Waymo is simultaneously expanding to Miami and targeting Austin, Atlanta, Houston, and the Bay Area — directly overlapping Tesla's existing and planned markets.

- **Automotive gross margins have deteriorated sharply and the near-term buffer is thin.** Margins fell from above 25% (early 2023) to below 18% (mid-2025) through sustained price cuts; Q1 2026 included a ~50,000-vehicle inventory build and missed delivery expectations. The Model Y price increase is a positive signal but affects only three trims and is under 3% on each — insufficient on its own to restore the margin structure, particularly with capex guidance raised to >$25B and free cash flow guided negative for the remainder of 2026.

articles.title: What Ron Baron Just Said About the Tesla SpaceX Merger
articles.body:
This video features host Herbert and guest Jeff Lutz — a multi-decade supply chain executive and CEO of a high-tech manufacturing consulting firm — discussing the implications of the upcoming SpaceX IPO for Tesla investors, including Ron Baron's comments on a potential Tesla-SpaceX merger. The core thesis is that while SpaceX represents a compelling investment opportunity, Tesla shareholders should not panic-sell Tesla to buy SpaceX, and any merger speculation is premature pending the S1 filing and deal structure details. The conversation also touches on Tesla's underappreciated physical AI advantage and the long-term potential of robotaxi, Optimus, and broader physical AI deployment.

## Market & Competition

1. **SpaceX IPO Details:** SpaceX is scheduled to go public on June 12th on the NASDAQ under the ticker SPCX. Shareholders have approved a 5-for-1 stock split, bringing the share price down from $527 to $105. The S1 was expected to drop the Wednesday following the video's recording. Anthropic and SpaceX are described as confirmed IPOs for 2026, with OpenAI's status uncertain. Combined, these mega-IPOs (Anthropic, SpaceX, OpenAI) are projected to raise more than all US IPOs in 2025 combined, with a combined estimated valuation of $1.6 trillion — though SpaceX alone is estimated by some at $1.75 trillion, and prediction markets have it as high as $2.2–$2.4 trillion.

2. **Major Investors Lining Up for SpaceX:** Elon Musk confirmed he will not be selling any of his SpaceX shares at IPO. BlackRock has announced plans to invest $5–$10 billion. Ron Baron stated he has placed a $1 billion IPO order. Jeff Lutz noted that SpaceX IPO demand in illiquid pre-markets is oversubscribed by double-digit percentages, and that early pre-market trading implies a $2.2–$2.4 trillion valuation.

3. **Tesla Shareholders and SpaceX Allocation:** Alexandra Merz ran a poll of her predominantly Tesla-investor audience asking how they would fund SpaceX purchases. Results (from approximately 400 respondents): 15% would sell Tesla, 6% would sell many holdings including Tesla (~21% total selling Tesla), 10% would sell other holdings but not Tesla, and the vast majority said they would use available cash. Both Herbert and Jeff Lutz stated they would consider buying SpaceX but would not sell Tesla to do so, and both said they wanted to read the S1 first.

4. **Ron Baron's View on Tesla-SpaceX Merger:** Ron Baron, when asked about a potential Tesla-SpaceX merger, said he would not bet on it — clarifying that when he doesn't know something, his answer is simply "I don't know." He acknowledged there are good reasons for and against a merger, noted that Elon operates based on what's best for his broader mission rather than personal financial gain, and said whatever Elon decides will likely have good rationale. Herbert interpreted Baron's comments as more of an "I don't know" than a firm "no."

5. **Ron Baron's SpaceX and Starlink Valuation:** Baron described SpaceX as potentially the largest company on the planet, projecting Tesla could reach $2,000–$2,500 per share over the next 10 years. He stated Starlink alone could be worth $14–$15 trillion, citing approximately $1 trillion in potential annual revenues at 70–80% profit margins. He noted Starlink currently has around 15 million customers in 2026 (up from 9 million in 2025), growing at approximately 50% per year, with a potential path to 300 million customers in 10 years. Starlink currently has 10,000 satellites and is on its way to 20,000.

6. **SpaceX's Orbital Dominance:** As of 2026, SpaceX accounted for approximately 87% of total global mass sent to orbit — 841 of 969 metric tons. The rest of the world combined accounted for 13%. Starship is designed to transport over one megaton of payload to space per year. Jeff Lutz emphasized this is not a close competition, and that rivals such as Blue Origin are years behind.

7. **Terafab Chip Manufacturing:** Ron Baron discussed Elon's plan to build a chip fabrication facility called Terafab, designed to produce chips at a fraction of the cost of Nvidia's chips, aiming for 50 times the world's current compute output. Baron noted Elon currently uses only 3% of what Nvidia provides and, given Nvidia's ~80% profit margins, believes he can manufacture chips cheaper, faster, and simpler in-house. He said Elon will never stop buying Nvidia chips but sees an opportunity to supplement at massive scale.

8. **Grok and AI Market Size:** Baron drew a parallel between Grok (XAI) and Anthropic, noting Anthropic grew from $9 billion in annualized revenues to $40–$45 billion in four to five months. He put the total AI opportunity at approximately $27 trillion per year — described as the first time a specific number of that magnitude had been publicly cited on the show.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Tesla's Physical AI as an Underappreciated Moat:** Both Herbert and Jeff Lutz argued that Tesla's real-world physical AI is significantly undervalued relative to LLM-based AI companies. They cited a quote from a senior Tesla AI executive (identified as "Yantasai" in the transcript) who stated: "Making seamless real-world agents is a lot harder than digital world agents, especially since the compute and energy budgets are extremely frugal compared to an H200. I have great respect for Tesla AI engineers pulling rabbits out of the hat over and over again. It may not be considered a frontier lab, but it is truly frontier." Jeff Lutz added that he knows of no company doing physical real-world AI at Tesla's scale.

2. **FSD Fleet Scale:** Jeff Lutz cited 1.3 million cars currently running Tesla Full Self-Driving, with customers paying a monthly subscription. He contrasted FSD's requirement for near-perfect decision-making (described as needing to be right 99.9999% of the time) with LLMs, which can hallucinate or produce wrong answers without consequence.

## Robotaxi

1. **Robotaxi Deployment Philosophy vs. Competitors:** Jeff Lutz argued that Tesla's slower-than-announced robotaxi rollout reflects a deliberate strategy to build the best cost structure and most scalable system, rather than rushing to deploy a few hundred or few thousand vehicles unprofitably as competitors might. He suggested critics who wanted Tesla to meet its original timeline would have gotten a robotaxi service that was likely not profitable. He framed this as a longer-term competitive advantage.

2. **Tesla Robotaxi as a Near-Term Value Catalyst:** Herbert noted that Tesla shareholders are anticipating a potential 10x value increase from the robotaxi business alone, and that any merger speculation is premature because Tesla is "just now about to get our robotaxi due." Jeff Lutz agreed that both robotaxi and Optimus represent unmet demand "for many years if not measured in decades," framing them as non-zero-sum opportunities.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus and the Broader Physical AI Opportunity:** Herbert argued that Tesla's physical AI will not be limited to cars and humanoid robots — it extends to any physical device with a chip and a camera, including smart home devices, agricultural machinery, factory equipment, and more. Jeff Lutz agreed, noting that any machine in any factory or farm could be given a chip and camera and become intelligent, posing the rhetorical question of what TAM one would assign to all factory and industrial equipment globally. He referenced Jeff Bezos's startup Prometheus as pursuing a similar concept of AI-enabling existing factories.

## Financials

1. **Tesla Price Target from Ron Baron:** Ron Baron projected Tesla stock could reach $2,000–$2,500 per share over the next 10 years, with the company potentially worth $10–$30 trillion or more. He stated: "Now is the time for Tesla."

2. **Merger Timeline and Deal Structure Uncertainty:** Herbert noted that according to a source named Larry Goldberg, boards of both Tesla and SpaceX could announce an intention to merge without immediately disclosing deal structure terms, meaning the actual deal terms may not be known for 8 months to a year after any such announcement. He added that neither Tesla nor SpaceX reportedly knows yet what the relative valuations or deal structure would look like.

Notable quotes and data:
- Ron Baron: "Tesla is going to be 2,000 or 2,500 over the next 10 years."
- Ron Baron: "Starlink alone I think can be worth 14–15 trillion dollars."
- Ron Baron on Starlink: "9 million customers last year. 15 million this year. They're going to grow 50% a year. They could have 300 million customers in 10 years."
- Ron Baron: "The opportunity is somewhere around $1 trillion of annual revenues for him, maybe making 70–80% profit margin — that could be worth 14–15 trillion alone."
- Ron Baron: "You never bet against the guy with superpowers who would never give up."
- Ron Baron on Terafab: "He needs to have 50 times the number of chips, the number of compute that's available right now."
- Ron Baron: "The chips he buys from Nvidia, he uses 3% of what Nvidia provides. 3%."
- Ron Baron: "Grok is like Anthropic. Anthropic grew from $9 billion of annualized revenues to $40–$45 billion in four or five months."
- Ron Baron on the AI market: "$27 trillion a year."
- Tesla AI exec ("Yantasai"): "Making seamless real-world agents is a lot harder than digital world agents… It may not be considered a frontier lab, but it is truly frontier."
- Jeff Lutz: "We have now 1.3 million cars running Tesla FSD."
- SpaceX orbital share (2026): 87% of total global mass to orbit (841 of 969 metric tons)
- SpaceX IPO date: June 12th, NASDAQ, ticker SPCX
- SpaceX stock split: 5-for-1, from $527 to $105
- BlackRock investing: $5–$10 billion in SpaceX IPO
- Ron Baron IPO order: $1 billion
- Alexandra Merz poll (~400 respondents): ~21% would sell Tesla to fund SpaceX purchase; majority would use available cash
- Woodline Partners added 68,000 Tesla shares

articles.title: Elon Just Dropped Huge SpaceXAI Updates
articles.body:
This video from the "brighterwithherbert" channel features host Herbert and guest Jo Bhakdi — an economist, investor, and tech entrepreneur — discussing Elon Musk's Forbes interview, the dismissal of his OpenAI lawsuit, SpaceX's AI computing ambitions, the anticipated SpaceX IPO, and the upcoming Starship V3 test flight. The core thesis is that Elon is strategically positioning SpaceX/XAI as the dominant provider of space-based AI compute infrastructure, while forming pragmatic alliances with Anthropic and Nvidia rather than treating them as adversaries.

## Market & Competition

1. **OpenAI Lawsuit Dismissed on Statute of Limitations:** A California court dismissed Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI, ruling that the five-year filing window exceeded the three-year statute of limitations. Elon announced he will file an appeal with the Ninth Circuit, arguing the ruling sets a dangerous precedent allowing individuals to "loot charities" by keeping enrichment quiet for a few years. He maintains that Sam Altman and Greg Brockman did in fact enrich themselves by converting a charity, and that the judge and jury never ruled on the merits of the case.

2. **Lawsuit as Strategic Aggression, Not Just Legal Action:** Jo Bhakdi frames the lawsuit as a calculated political move rather than a genuine legal effort. He argues Elon's team almost certainly knew the statute of limitations would be a problem, but the real objectives were achieved regardless: massive distraction for OpenAI through depositions, public exposure of damaging internal emails, reputational damage to the OpenAI leadership team, and likely delay of OpenAI's IPO. Bhakdi characterizes this as a "win" for Elon's broader strategic goals even in legal defeat, with SpaceX now positioned to IPO ahead of OpenAI and Anthropic potentially second.

3. **Elon's Alliance Strategy — Anthropic and Nvidia as Partners, Not Rivals:** Rather than positioning XAI as a head-to-head competitor with Anthropic or Nvidia, Elon publicly defended Anthropic when a social media post claimed Cursor's Composer 2.5 model would "destroy" them. Elon stated: "Anthropic will not be destroyed. The AI plus the harness goes far beyond coding and Opus 4.7 is still better than Composer 2.5, albeit a lot more expensive. Cursor is however an important piece of the puzzle to make Grok much better." Jo Bhakdi interprets this as Elon recognizing Anthropic's formidable lead in AI models and Jensen Huang's dominance in chips, and choosing to build a strategic alliance — owning the compute and physical AI stack — rather than attacking competitors in their areas of strength.

4. **XAI Positioning as "EWS" — Elon's AWS Equivalent:** The hosts describe Elon's evolving strategy for XAI and SpaceX as building something analogous to Amazon Web Services — renting out space-based data centers and compute to customers including Google (already in talks to rent orbital data centers) and, they predict, Microsoft next. The argument is that what began as internal compute for Tesla cars and Optimus robots is now being commercialized as a vendor business. Cursor recently began using XAI's data centers, and Bhakdi notes they "haven't even used all of it yet."

5. **Nvidia Delivers First Vera CPU to SpaceX/XAI:** Nvidia Vice President of Hyperscale Ian Buck hand-delivered the first Vera CPU servers to a select group of launch customers: Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX, and Oracle. Vera is described as Nvidia's first custom CPU purpose-built for the age of agentic AI — a shift beyond LLMs toward AI agents that need significantly more CPU power (88 CPU cores) to execute tasks outside the LLM itself. The hosts note that SpaceX/XAI being on this short list confirms Elon's priority standing with Nvidia, and that this milestone is reminiscent of Jensen Huang's first GPU gift to OpenAI that "kicked off AI."

6. **Space-Based AI Data Centers — Elon's Core Thesis:** In his Forbes interview, Elon argued that data centers in space are "much easier than people may think," citing SpaceX's current 10,000 satellites in orbit and projecting launches of over 10,000 communication satellites per year with Starship in the future — each significantly more capable than current satellites. He stated that AI satellite tonnage will dwarf communication satellite tonnage. Bhakdi frames this as Elon's decisive strategic domain: owning the space compute layer of the AI stack while letting Anthropic and Nvidia lead on models and chips respectively.

## Financials

1. **SpaceX IPO Expected Imminently — S1 Filing Anticipated:** The hosts report that the SpaceX IPO prospectus S1 filing is expected to drop the following day (2026-05-20) on the SEC's EDGAR database. The IPO date is rumored to be June 12, 2026. Rumored underwriters are four equal co-leads — JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Bank of America — with an unusual 30% retail allocation (versus a typical ~10%). Broker access varies: Vanguard reportedly gets no allocation with limit-only day-one orders; Robinhood reportedly gets allocation as a "likely lot type"; Fidelity reportedly considers IPO allocation for accounts holding $100,000 or more.

2. **Starship V3 Test Flight Stakes for IPO Valuation:** A Starship V3 test flight was scheduled for the day after the video's publication (approximately 2026-05-20). V3 incorporates improvements from V1 and V2, including a reduced-mass Raptor engine (1,500 kg), fewer grid fins, and a new launchpad. While Elon publicly downplayed the stakes — noting SpaceX has roughly 10 more ships and about half that number of boosters in production this year — Jo Bhakdi argues the flight is enormously consequential for the IPO. He notes that if Starship is carrying 150 tons of GPUs as cargo, the insured value could approach $1 billion, and a 20% failure rate would add approximately $200 million of risk cost per launch on top of the ~$90–100 million base launch cost. A successful flight, by contrast, could send the stock "to three trillion."

Notable quotes and data:
- Elon on appeal: "This will become precedent which people can then essentially loot charities and use this case as a basis for doing so."
- Elon on Anthropic: "Anthropic will not be destroyed. The AI plus the harness goes far beyond coding and Opus 4.7 is still better than Composer 2.5, albeit a lot more expensive. Cursor is however an important piece of the puzzle to make Grok much better."
- Elon on space data centers: "SpaceX at this point has 10,000 satellites in orbit right now… in the future with Starship, we'll be launching over 10,000 communication satellites per year… that will pale in comparison to the tonnage of AI satellites."
- Elon on Starship: "The Starship production pipeline is full and will complete roughly 10 more ships and about half that number of boosters this year."
- SpaceX IPO rumored date: June 12, 2026; 30% retail allocation; four equal underwriters (JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America)
- Nvidia Vera CPU: 88 CPU cores; purpose-built for agentic AI; hand-delivered to Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX, and Oracle
- Bhakdi on Starship failure rate economics: A 20% failure rate on a $1 billion cargo manifest would add ~$200 million to effective launch cost (i.e., ~$290 million total vs. ~$90 million base)
- Bhakdi on AGI timeline: "Economic AGI is already here in the next two to three months in my opinion"

articles.title: Exclusive: Tesla (TSLA) is building its giant solar panel factory in Houston
articles.body:
Tesla is building a large-scale, vertically integrated solar panel manufacturing operation at its Brookshire, Texas facility (Empire West Business Park, ~35 miles west of Houston), co-located with the Megapack Megafactory already under construction there. This is the first confirmed location for Tesla's stated 100 GW annual solar manufacturing ambition.

## Energy

1. **Brookshire facility details:** Tesla leases Buildings 9 and 10 at the site, totaling 1.65 million square feet, with plans for an additional 600,000-square-foot building. The entire site is 100% leased to Tesla under a long-term agreement. Capital expenditure across multiple simultaneous facility builds exceeds $250 million, with cleanroom-grade manufacturing environments under construction.

2. **Full vertical integration planned:** Unlike simple panel assembly, Tesla is building the complete production chain at Brookshire: ingot growth, wafer slicing, photovoltaic cell production, and finished panel assembly. This is consistent with the previously reported $2.9 billion deal (reported by CNBC in March 2026) to purchase Chinese solar manufacturing equipment from suppliers including Suzhou Maxwell Technologies, with equipment destined for Texas.

3. **Context and scale:** Tesla currently produces its TSP-420 panel at Gigafactory New York (Buffalo) at roughly 300 MW/year capacity, launched commercially in January 2026. The Houston operation represents a stated 300x scale-up. For comparison, First Solar — the largest domestic solar manufacturer — projects 17.7 GW of capacity by 2027; total U.S. solar installations in 2023 were ~32 GW. Elon Musk announced the 100 GW target at Davos in January 2026. Co-location with the $200 million Megapack Megafactory offers logistics advantages, and Houston's port infrastructure is critical for receiving the Chinese equipment imports.

## Editorial Stance
Author Fred Lambert expresses cautious optimism: the $250M+ construction commitment and $2.9B equipment deal represent real capital behind what had been rhetoric, distinguishing this from the Buffalo subsidy-driven playbook — but the 100 GW by 2028 target is characterized as "wildly ambitious to completely delusional," with Chinese export approvals and construction timelines as key risks.

Notable quotes and data:
- Tesla capex at Brookshire: **$250M+** across multiple simultaneous facility builds
- Chinese equipment deal: **$2.9 billion**, supplier includes Suzhou Maxwell Technologies (reported by CNBC, March 2026)
- Buffalo current capacity: **~300 MW/year**
- 100 GW target = **300x** increase from Buffalo, on a sub-three-year timeline

- U.S. total solar installations in 2023: **~32 GW**

articles.title: Tesla Cybertruck owner believed Elon Musk when he said it could cross a lake — now he’s in jail
articles.body:
A Tesla Cybertruck owner drove his vehicle into Grapevine Lake in Texas to test the "Wade Mode" feature, became stranded, and was arrested on multiple charges. The incident is the latest in a pattern of similar events tied to Elon Musk's past claims about the Cybertruck's water capabilities.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Grapevine Lake incident:** On Monday evening around 8 PM, Grapevine police and fire were dispatched to Katie's Woods Park Boat Ramp, where a Cybertruck had been intentionally driven into the lake to test Wade Mode. The vehicle became disabled and took on water; passengers self-evacuated and the fire department's Water Rescue Team recovered the truck. The driver was charged with operating a vehicle in a closed section of park/lake, having no valid boat registration, and multiple water safety equipment violations, and remains in jail as of the article's publication.

2. **What Wade Mode actually does:** Despite Musk's 2022 claim that the Cybertruck would be "waterproof enough" to serve as a boat and cross rivers, lakes, and even seas — with a stated goal of crossing the ~360-meter gap between SpaceX's Starbase and South Padre Island — the production vehicle's Wade Mode only pressurizes the battery pack and raises ride height to support a maximum wade depth of approximately 32 inches from the bottom of the tire, intended for shallow creek crossings.

3. **Pattern of similar incidents:** Prior incidents include a Cybertruck stuck in water in Truckee, California (prompting the CHP to note "Wade Mode isn't Submarine Mode"), a Cybertruck that sank in Ventura harbor during a jet ski launch requiring Coast Guard involvement, and a European-imported Cybertruck stuck in a lake in Slovakia. Tesla's warranty does not cover off-roading or water damage.

## Editorial Stance
The author squarely blames Musk's repeated public claims for giving owners false confidence, but also states bluntly that owners who take Musk at his word on such claims "probably deserve a night in jail and whatever fine that comes with it."

Notable quotes and data:
- Musk in 2022: Cybertruck would be "waterproof enough" to serve as a boat and cross rivers, lakes, and seas
- Target crossing: ~360 meters between SpaceX's Starbase and South Padre Island
- Actual Wade Mode limit: ~32 inches maximum wade depth from bottom of tire
- CHP quote from Truckee incident: "Wade Mode isn't Submarine Mode"
- Tesla's warranty does not cover off-roading or water damage

articles.title: Elon promises FSD by year’s end, but Einride has L4 autonomy for big trucks TODAY
articles.body:
This Electrek "Quick Charge" podcast episode contrasts Elon Musk's repeated promises about Tesla FSD reaching widespread unsupervised deployment by year-end against Einride's claim of already operating Level 4 autonomous electric semi trucks commercially today.

## Autonomous Driving
1. **Musk's FSD promise vs. Einride's L4 reality:** Musk has again stated that Tesla's unsupervised FSD will be "widespread" in the US by year-end (2026). The episode frames this skeptically, noting it is a recurring commitment. By contrast, Einride — whose CEO Roozbeh Charli is interviewed — has already begun public L4 autonomous electric semi operations and secured a multimillion-dollar middle-mile deal with Amazon.

2. **Tesla Smart Summon speed increase:** A new FSD update increases Actually Smart Summon speed by 33%, flagged in the episode as noteworthy (and described as "concerning" in tone).

## Electric Vehicles
1. **Affordable EV pipeline from legacy OEMs:** The episode references upcoming affordable EVs from BMW, Stellantis (including a potential sub-$18,000 Jeep EV and a Dodge Neon revival candidate), and Volvo, as well as a Costco stackable discount on the 2027 Chevy Bolt.

## Editorial Stance
The author frames Tesla's FSD timeline as a repeated, undelivered promise ("tenth time a charm?") and positions Einride's operational L4 autonomy as a substantive counterpoint to Tesla's hype — favoring demonstrated deployment over announced roadmaps.

Notable quotes and data:
- Musk says unsupervised FSD will be "widespread" in the US by year-end (2026) — described as a recurring promise
- Einride has begun **public L4 autonomous electric semi operations** and signed an Amazon middle-mile deal
- Tesla Smart Summon speed increased **33%** in a new FSD update
- Stellantis EV referenced at a starting price of **under $18,000**

articles.title: This Is My Last Electrified Video ⚡️
articles.body:
This video, hosted by Dillon Loomis, is primarily a channel transition announcement in which he explains his intention to rebrand "Electrified" to "Demystify" and broaden its scope beyond Tesla to include AI, SpaceX, and adjacent topics — while keeping Tesla as the core focus for the foreseeable future. Alongside the announcement, he runs through a set of Tesla and broader tech news items at an accelerated pace. The video covers Tesla's solar factory plans, FSD 14.3 early rollout impressions, Tesla Semi demand, EV road fees, Cybercab developments, and Elon Musk's public statements on robotaxis, humanoid robots, and AI.

## Autonomous Driving
1. **FSD 14.3 Early Rollout — Mixed Initial Reports:** FSD 14.3 is in very early rollout phases, with fewer than approximately 50 vehicles on the software based on trackers at the time of the video. Elon Musk described the update as "a banger" and stated it "nags less," with some users reporting going up to a minute without a nag prompt. However, early user feedback is mixed: Chris's wife reported phantom braking getting "out of hand" on 14.3, and DJ reported a critical disengagement within the first 30 seconds of the update (though he later noted performance improved after the rough start). Devon Olsen shared a video showing the car backing up unusually far during a destination park and hitting a curb, raising concerns about parking regressions — a concern echoed by Dirty Tesla's video. Mike P also reported continued left-lane camping in standard mode on 14.3.

2. **UI Changes in FSD 14.3:** The intervention feedback screen has been updated and now categorizes disengagements as navigation, parking, critical, or other. Users can reportedly dismiss this screen by double-clicking the voice activation button on the steering wheel. A new streak feature has been added to the UI, tracking how long a driver goes without disengaging FSD. Dillon Loomis expressed a preference for a total-miles-on-FSD leaderboard instead, arguing it would encourage safe engagement without penalizing necessary disengagements.

3. **Smart Summon Speed Increase:** The actually smart summon speed has been increased to 8 mph, up from 6 mph previously.

4. **FSD Regulatory Expansion — Israel:** In an interview at the Samson Smart Mobility Summit, Elon Musk said he is hoping FSD will receive regulatory approval in Israel sometime in 2026, "hopefully soon."

## Robotaxi
1. **Elon Musk on Robotaxi Deployment Timeline:** At the Samson Smart Mobility Summit, Elon Musk stated he expects widespread deployment of robotaxis in the US by the end of 2026. Dillon Loomis was notably skeptical, pointing out that Musk has been "a literal yo-yo" in his public statements about robotaxi rollout timelines, and cautioned viewers against putting too much stock in any specific prediction.

2. **Cybercab Spotted with License Plate in Houston:** A user named Sloak reported spotting a production-version Cybercab in Houston that now has a license plate. Dillon Loomis noted that the Texas Transportation Code requires all vehicles driven on public roads to have a license plate, framing it as a required — but not conclusive — step toward eventual Cybercab deployment. He cautioned against reading too much into the sighting.

3. **India Factory Plans Reportedly Abandoned — Implications for Cybercab Global Rollout:** A Chinese financial outlet reported that Tesla has decided to abandon plans to build a factory in India, citing shortcomings in India's domestic supply chain, a long-running negotiation deadlock over tariff sequencing, insufficient infrastructure, a mismatch between Tesla's high-end positioning and India's auto market buying power, and policy uncertainty. Dillon Loomis suggested this could be a negotiating tactic and speculated that once the Cybercab is in production and globally deployable, India could re-enter the conversation.

## Humanoid Bots
1. **Elon Musk's 5-Year Humanoid Robot Forecast:** In an interview at the Forbes Innovator Summit, Elon Musk projected that by approximately 2031, there could be "at least 100 million humanoid robots, but maybe a billion." He also stated that digital intelligence will exceed the sum of all human intelligence within five years. Dillon Loomis offered no specific endorsement or pushback on these projections, presenting them as Musk's stated views.

## Energy
1. **Tesla Solar Panel Factory in Houston (Brookshire):** Electric reported exclusively that Tesla is building a solar panel factory in Houston, specifically in Brookshire, co-located with the Megafactory Tesla is constructing at the same site. The Brookshire site consists of two buildings Tesla leases totaling 1.65 million square feet, with plans for an additional 600,000 square foot building, bringing the total to over 2 million square feet. The site is 100% leased to Tesla under a long-term agreement. The factory is described as a fully integrated facility, taking raw silicon inputs through ingots, wafers, and PV cells all the way to final panel assembly. Tesla is reportedly building "highly complex clean room-grade manufacturing environments" with more than $250 million in capex across multiple simultaneous facility builds. Chinese solar manufacturing equipment was reported to be shipping to Texas.

2. **Scale of Tesla's Solar Ambitions:** Tesla's existing solar capacity at Giga New York (Buffalo) is approximately 300 megawatts per year. Elon Musk has stated that both Tesla and SpaceX will each build out 100 gigawatts of solar manufacturing capacity in the years ahead — representing more than a 300x increase from the Buffalo facility. For context, First Solar, currently the largest domestic solar manufacturer in the US, is expecting under 18 gigawatts of capacity by 2027, meaning Tesla's target would be roughly six times that. The US solar industry installed 43 gigawatts in 2025, a 14% decrease from 2024; Tesla's 100-gigawatt target would be more than double the entire US installation capacity added in 2025.

3. **Capex Context and Solar Equipment Orders:** On the Q1 2026 earnings call, Tesla CFO Vaibhav Taneja stated Tesla's capex expectation for 2026 is over $25 billion, up from a prior $20 billion figure. He cited solar manufacturing equipment as part of the incremental $5 billion increase. Tesla was also reported earlier in 2026 to be in talks to buy $2.9 billion of Chinese solar manufacturing equipment. Dillon Loomis suggested the extra $5 billion in capex likely includes the Houston facility, though he noted it was not officially confirmed. Tesla also bundles Megapacks with utility-scale solar and Powerwalls with rooftop solar, making co-location of manufacturing operationally logical. Houston's access to a major port for equipment imports was cited as an advantage over Austin.

## Electric Vehicles
1. **Tesla Semi Demand and Early Performance:** The New York Times published a positive article on the Tesla Semi, describing early reviews as suggesting it "could be a much-needed hit for Tesla." The owner of King Theot Trucking in California, which has ordered 20 Tesla Semis, described it as addressing key problems with current electric trucks — limited range, heavy weight, and high cost. California trucking firms have applied for state subsidies to purchase more than 1,200 Tesla Semis — more than all applications for other electric trucks combined since the incentive program began in 2019. A truck driver quoted noted the Semi is quieter than diesel rigs and allows air conditioning while waiting to unload, which is restricted for diesel trucks in California due to idling regulations. Diesel prices have reportedly risen approximately 50% since what the transcript refers to as "the war with Iran," making electric alternatives more attractive.

2. **Tesla Semi Operational Metrics:** In 2025, Tesla's early Semi fleet achieved over 95% uptime, and 75% of service visits were completed in under 24 hours.

3. **Competitor Responses to Tesla Semi:** The president of Volvo Trucks North America stated he does not think the Semi is disruptive and cited Volvo's planned longer-range model for next year and its service reliability track record. The president of Daimler Truck North America cited insufficient high-powered charging infrastructure as a barrier to electric truck practicality for long trips.

4. **Proposed EV Road Fee Legislation:** House lawmakers proposed bipartisan legislation requiring EV owners to pay a $130 annual fee for road maintenance (in lieu of fuel taxes), and $35 for plug-in hybrid owners. Starting in 2029, fees would rise $5 per year, up to a maximum of $150 for EVs and $50 for plug-in hybrids. These fees would be in addition to existing state registration fees. Dillon Loomis noted he personally pays $250 per EV in state fees where he lives, and flagged the fairness concern that low-mileage EV drivers would pay the same flat fee as high-mileage drivers.

## Market & Competition
1. **Elon Musk Joins Forbes Innovator Summit — Electric Aircraft Comments:** In addition to his humanoid robot forecast, Elon Musk mentioned he sees electric aircraft as "probably an opportunity," noting there are startups in that field.

2. **Andrej Karpathy Joins Anthropic:** Andrej Karpathy announced he has joined Anthropic, stating the next few years at the frontier of large language models will be "especially formative." He also said he plans to resume his work in education in time. Earlier in May 2026, SpaceX signed an agreement with Anthropic to provide access to Colossus 1. Dillon Loomis highlighted this as an example of the deepening overlap between Tesla, SpaceX, and leading AI organizations.

3. **Grok's Role in Tesla Ecosystem:** Elon Musk noted that Anthropic's AI and Claude (specifically Opus 4.7) remains better than Composer 2.5, though at higher cost. He stated Cursor is an important piece of making Grok better. Dillon Loomis noted that Grok is already integrated into Tesla vehicles and will play a significant role in Optimus development, framing AI ecosystem developments as directly material to Tesla's future.

Notable quotes and data:
- Elon Musk (Forbes Innovator Summit): "I think digital intelligence will exceed the sum of all human intelligence [within five years, i.e., by approximately 2031]."
- Elon Musk (Forbes Innovator Summit): "There might be at least 100 million humanoid robots, but maybe a billion" within five years.
- Elon Musk (Samson Smart Mobility Summit): Expects widespread robotaxi deployment in the US by end of 2026; hopes FSD approval in Israel comes "sometime this year."
- Elon Musk: "In 10 years, around 90% of all miles traveled will be autonomous vehicles."
- Tesla solar capex: Over $250 million across multiple simultaneous facility builds in Brookshire, Houston.
