(2) Safety monitor presence — every Austin incident to date had a human safety monitor in the vehicle, meaning the current "safer than humans" claim still includes a human backstop; the fully driverless test at scale is still ahead. (3) No clean disclosed unsupervised mileage or fleet count from Tesla, placing an asterisk on any Tesla vs. Waymo ratio. (4) Teleoperation cuts both ways — while it exonerates the autonomous driving model in two incidents, it confirms a human is still sometimes in the loop and can make mistakes.

## Robotaxi

1. **Austin Unsupervised Fleet Approaching Majority:** The video notes that over 50% of all robotaxi cars operating in Austin are now unsupervised (driverless), and that percentage is continuing to increase. This is framed as a near-term milestone, with the transition to a fully monitor-free operation at scale described as the critical next test for the safety thesis.

2. **Investment Thesis Framing — Safety Data as the Regulatory Gate:** The video argues that robotaxi safety data is the single gate behind which the entire Tesla valuation thesis waits. Regulators require both evidence (readable safety data) and political cover (credible third-party voices) before permitting monitor-free scaling. The video contends that both arrived simultaneously in May 2026: unredacted crash narratives providing the evidence, and the New York Times doctor essay providing the political cover. The shift from redacted incident counts to readable narratives plus a mileage-based safety estimate is characterized as the moment the story moved from "trust me" to "here, read it yourself."

## Market & Competition

1. **Neurosurgeons and Doctors Make Public Health Case for AVs:** A guest essay in The New York Times, written by neurosurgeon Dr. Jonathan Slotkin and co-signed by other doctors and nurses, called for the government to clear a faster regulatory path for self-driving cars, describing it as a "public health imperative." The essay cited a peer-reviewed Waymo study across more than 56 million driverless miles showing 91% fewer serious injury or worse crashes than human drivers on the same roads, and 80% fewer crashes causing any injury at all. It also cited a projection that if just 30% of cars were fully automated, 40% of crashes could be prevented. The video frames this medical community endorsement as a meaningful shift — moving the autonomous vehicle safety argument from enthusiast debate to clinical and regulatory legitimacy.

---

**Notable quotes and data:**

- Analyst Reigns estimates Tesla robotaxi in Austin is ~1.8x safer than average human drivers as of April 2026
- Human driver baseline (NHTSA-derived): ~1 accident per 249,000 miles
- Austin robotaxi mileage estimated with under 5% error using fleet size and reported mileage relationship
- 17 total incidents since Austin launch on June 22, 2025
- 7 incidents attributed to Tesla; of those, only 3 involved the car's autonomous driving system
- 2 at-fault incidents caused by remote teleoperators, not the car
- Average speed across all incidents: ~5.9 mph (per EV Wire); no major injuries
- Blown tire response: car autonomously slowed to ~18 mph and pulled over without human input
- Teleoperator drove car into a fence after taking control; separate teleoperator ran car into construction barricade at ~9 mph
- Waymo monthly federal incident counts (2026): January 100, February 73, March 50, first half of April 2
- Mayhof tracker: Waymo all-time total >1,800 incidents; Tesla total 17
- Waymo peer-reviewed study: 91% fewer serious injury crashes, 80% fewer injury crashes vs. humans, across 56M+ driverless miles
- Projection cited by doctors: 30% AV adoption could prevent 40% of crashes
- Over 50% of Austin robotaxi fleet is now operating unsupervised
- "The conversation just changed from *can it* to *how fast*."

articles.title: Tesla now calls FSD ‘Tesla Assisted Driving’ in China – a more truthful name
articles.body:
Tesla has rebranded its FSD system in mainland China to "Tesla Assisted Driving" (特斯拉辅助驾驶), dropping the word "Intelligent" from its previous Chinese name "FSD Intelligent Assisted Driving." The article frames this as a concession to stricter Chinese regulatory standards and a tacit acknowledgment that the "Full Self-Driving" name is misleading.

## Autonomous Driving
1. **FSD remains a Level 2 ADAS system:** Despite being marketed as "Full Self-Driving" and priced at up to $15,000 (or via subscription), Tesla's system is classified as Level 2 under standardized self-driving taxonomy — meaning the human driver remains legally responsible. The article notes Tesla has added "(Supervised)" to the name in the US following pressure from California regulators, but no substantive capability change accompanied this.

2. **China-specific naming history:** In China, the system has gone through multiple name iterations: originally "FSD Intelligent Assisted Driving," then dropping "FSD," and now "Tesla Assisted Driving." Notably, Tesla still uses "Full Self-Driving" on its Hong Kong English-language site and "fully automatic driving function" in Hong Kong Chinese — reflecting Hong Kong's distinct regulatory status as a special administrative region.

3. **FSD availability in China remains unclear:** Tesla stated in an English-language tweet this week that FSD is available in China, but the article notes it is unclear whether this included any new capabilities, given Tesla has previously launched and then rolled back FSD in China.

## Market & Competition
1. **Fierce Chinese ADAS competition:** Multiple Chinese automakers offer competing ADAS systems, some at no cost to consumers. A large-scale Chinese media real-world test covering both highway and city driving found Tesla's system ranked first — but by a narrow margin, not a commanding lead. The article notes Chinese automakers are deploying ADAS capabilities faster than Western competitors overall.

## Editorial Stance
The author argues that "Full Self-Driving" has always been a misleading name for a Level 2 system, and that Tesla's repeated renaming in China reflects the difficulty of building a brand around a claim the product cannot fulfill. The author criticizes CEO Elon Musk for a decade of unfulfilled promises that full autonomy is "at the end of next year."

Notable quotes and data:
- FSD has been priced at up to **$15,000** upfront; China still offers upfront purchase (vs. subscription-only in the US)
- New Chinese name: **特斯拉辅助驾驶** ("Tesla Assisted Driving"), replacing "Intelligent Assisted Driving"
- Tesla's system is **Level 2** ADAS under standardized classification
- Chinese media real-world ADAS test: Tesla ranked **first** on both highway and city street tests, but by a narrow margin
- Hong Kong retains separate traffic regulations (right-hand drive vs. mainland left-hand drive)

articles.title: These 6 out of 8 Tech Giants Will Die By 2030
articles.body:
This video from the farzad-fm channel presents a sweeping analysis of what the host frames as an existential AI war among eight major factions competing for dominance in the global AI economy through 2030. The core thesis is that the compounding nature of AI — where compute generates better models, which attract better users, which generate better data, which trains smarter models — means the window for new entrants has effectively closed, and by 2030 only two of the eight factions will emerge as true winners while the rest get absorbed, commoditized, or fade away. The host draws on Wright's Law, training cost trajectories, and structural analysis of each faction's data, chip, and business model advantages to make his case.

## Market & Competition

1. **The AI War's Compounding Weapon:** The host argues this conflict is structurally unlike any previous geopolitical struggle because the weapon — compute — compounds rather than depletes. Each training cycle produces a smarter model, which attracts better users, which generates better data, which trains an even smarter model. The faction already ahead widens its lead with every iteration, making it mathematically difficult for latecomers to catch up. The host argues the window for new entrants effectively closed in 2024.

2. **Training Cost Escalation:** GPT-3 training costs in 2020 were estimated between $4–12 million. GPT-4 training in 2023 cost between $40–100 million — roughly a 10x increase in three years. Historical data going back to 2016 shows training costs have grown approximately 2.4x per year, implying a single frontier model training run could exceed $1 billion by 2027. This cost trajectory is rapidly shrinking the list of organizations capable of staying in the race.

3. **High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) as the True Constraint:** The host argues that most analysts focus too narrowly on raw GPU counts. The actual binding constraint on AI model training is High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), which coordinates GPU processing. Without sufficient HBM, large GPU clusters cannot work in sync. The faction controlling the most HBM controls the actual training ceiling for frontier models.

4. **OpenAI — Massive Scale, Structural Losses:** OpenAI reached 900 million weekly active users as of February 2026, 50 million+ paying subscribers, and $2 billion in monthly revenue. ChatGPT was the most downloaded app globally in 2026 with over 770 million installs in 2025 alone, surpassing TikTok and Instagram. An ad pilot launched in January 2026 crossed $100 million in annualized revenue within six weeks. However, OpenAI posted a net loss of $13.5 billion in just the first half of 2025. Internal projections show losses tripling to $14 billion in 2026 against roughly $20 billion in expected sales. Total projected losses through 2028 are estimated at $44 billion. HSBC analysts concluded OpenAI will likely not be profitable until 2030 and faces a $207 billion funding shortfall relative to its growth plans. The company is spending $1.35 for every dollar earned.

5. **OpenAI — Inference Costs and Talent Drain:** Inference costs (running ChatGPT for users) reached $8.4 billion in 2025 and are projected to hit $14 billion in 2026 — meaning more users directly increases losses. Fortune reported OpenAI engineers are eight times more likely to leave for Anthropic than the reverse. The company spent approximately $6 billion in stock-based compensation in 2025, nearly half of projected revenue, trying to stop talent outflow. Multiple senior leaders have departed, including CTO Mira Murati and co-founder Ilya Sutskever.

6. **Microsoft — Infrastructure Lock-In Strategy:** Microsoft's strategy is not to win the AI model race outright but to own the infrastructure the race is run on. GitHub Copilot has 1.8 million paid developer subscribers and is embedded in the majority of Fortune 500 pipelines. Microsoft's AI business runs at an annualized revenue rate of $37 billion, up 123% year-over-year. Azure grew 40% in the most recent quarter, described as its fastest rate in years. The Intelligent Cloud segment brought in $26.8 billion in a single quarter in early 2025. Per April 2026 trial court documents, Microsoft holds approximately 27% equity in OpenAI from its original 2019 investment. The host notes growing tension as Microsoft's own Phi model line (released December 2024) increasingly competes with GPT for enterprise use cases.

7. **Meta — Open Source as a Strategic Weapon:** The host argues Meta's open-source Llama model releases are not ideological but strategic. Llama 4, released April 2025, has been downloaded over 1 billion times. By flooding the market with capable free models, Meta erodes the pricing power of proprietary model providers like OpenAI, preventing any single company from owning the AI interface layer above Meta's 3.56 billion daily active users across its apps as of March 2026. Meta raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $125–145 billion in late April 2026 (up from $72 billion spent in all of 2025), citing higher memory pricing as a primary driver — representing approximately 54% of revenue reinvested in infrastructure. Meta also launched its first closed-source model, Muse Spark, through a newly formed Meta Superintelligence Labs, signaling a dual-track strategy.

8. **China — Efficiency Over Chip Supremacy:** China cannot win the semiconductor race: SMIC is stuck at 7 nanometers using workarounds, while TSMC operates at 3 nanometers with EUV lithography technology China cannot access. Huawei's best chip alternative, the Ascend 910C, is built on the same constrained 7nm process. China plans to produce roughly 600,000 Ascend 910 chips in 2026, an amount Nvidia reportedly ships in a few months. China's counter-strategy is algorithmic efficiency. DeepSeek R1, released January 2025, achieved near-frontier reasoning at a confirmed training cost of $294,000, training for 80 hours on 512 Nvidia H800 chips — confirmed in a peer-reviewed paper published in Nature in September 2025. DeepSeek V4, released April 2026 and built on Huawei's Ascend chips, is priced at $3,048 per million output tokens versus OpenAI's $30 and Anthropic's comparable rate — less than 12 cents on the dollar. China's 15th Five-Year Plan released March 2026 dropped the word "chip" entirely, officially pivoting toward AI economic penetration as the primary national strategy. However, the US government's Center for AI Standards and Innovation found DeepSeek significantly underperforms American frontier models on accuracy, security, and cost efficiency.

9. **Google — Deep Substrate Advantage:** Google invented the Transformer architecture in 2017, the foundational technology every major AI model now uses. Its custom TPU chips are on their seventh generation: TPUv4 pods deliver 1.2–1.7x higher throughput than comparable Nvidia A100 setups at 53–77% of the power. The Trillium generation (TPUv6) delivers 4.7x the peak compute performance per chip versus its predecessor, with double the interconnect bandwidth and 67% greater energy efficiency. Google has 25 years of proprietary training data from Search, YouTube, Gmail, and Maps — a dataset the host says cannot be replicated or purchased at any price. Google's AlphaEvolve AI coding agent redesigned a circuit for next-generation TPUs and recovered 0.7% of Google's worldwide compute that was previously wasted. Gemini 3.1 Pro leads 13 of 16 major benchmarks as of February 2026. Google Cloud revenue surged 63% year-over-year to $20 billion in Q1 2026. Google has committed $40 billion into Anthropic, with $10 billion already deployed. The host identifies Google and the Musk integrated stack as the two likely winners by 2030.

10. **Anthropic — Enterprise Credibility vs. Government Blacklist:** Anthropic grew from $87 million in annualized revenue in January 2024 to $30 billion by April 2026 — faster than Salesforce's entire 20-year path to the same milestone. Claude Code, launched May 2025, hit $1 billion annualized revenue by November 2025 and $2.5 billion by February 2026. The company has over 300,000 business customers, with more than 1,000 spending over $1 million per year — a number that doubled in under two months between February and April 2026. Eight of the Fortune 10 are Claude customers. However, Anthropic's refusal to allow Claude for autonomous weapons systems or mass domestic surveillance led the DoD to designate it a supply chain risk — the first American AI company to receive that label. On May 1, 2026, the Pentagon signed AI deployment agreements with OpenAI, xAI, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Nvidia, AWS, Oracle, and SpaceX; Anthropic was excluded. Anthropic sued, a federal judge blocked enforcement, and reportedly the NSA is using Anthropic's Mythos model regardless due to its cybersecurity scanning capabilities. CEO Dario Amodei met with the White House Chief of Staff and Treasury Secretary in April 2026, and President Trump publicly suggested a resolution is possible.

11. **Musk Integrated Stack (XAI + SpaceX + Tesla) — Vertically Integrated AI:** XAI was acquired by SpaceX in February 2026 in an all-stock transaction valuing SpaceX at $1 trillion, XAI at $250 billion, and the combined entity at $1.25 trillion. The Colossus data center in Memphis was built in 122 days despite being told it would take four years — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang called it "superhuman." As of February 2026, the Memphis complex houses approximately 555,000 Nvidia GPUs (H100s, H200s, and GB200s) representing roughly $18 billion in silicon at a single site, approaching 2 gigawatts of total capacity — described as four times larger than the next biggest dedicated AI training site. The target is 1 million GPUs. The DoD integrated Grok into genai.mil serving 3 million active military personnel under a $200 million contract signed July 2025. Starlink crossed 10 million active customers across 160 countries. Tesla is described as the world's largest real-world AI data collection operation, with over 9 million cars delivered and over 1.2 million actively running FSD, generating labeled real-world perception data continuously. The host notes Waymo has roughly a few million miles of data accumulated over 15 years, while Tesla adds equivalent amounts in weeks. Terafab, the XAI custom chip factory, is not expected to ship until at least 2027. In May 2026, SpaceX signed a deal giving Anthropic access to Colossus 1 — the 220,000 GPU supercluster — and 300 megawatts of power.

12. **The Regulatory Faction — Simultaneous Brake on Western AI:** The EU AI Act went into full enforcement in August 2024, covering 450 million people with fines up to €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover — approximately $14 billion for Google and $8.5 billion for Meta. Full enforcement for high-risk AI systems activates August 2, 2026. Over 1,000 state AI bills were introduced in the US in 2025 alone. The host's key structural concern is asymmetry: regulatory friction operates on timelines of months to years while the compute doubling cycle operates in weeks, meaning every month of Western regulatory slowdown is a month Chinese labs — backed by explicit state capital and national AI deployment mandates — narrow the gap.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Tesla FSD as Real-World AI Data Engine:** The host describes Tesla not primarily as a car company but as the world's largest real-world AI data collection operation. With over 1.2 million cars actively running Full Self-Driving, every mile driven is labeled, analyzed, and fed back into the training pipeline daily. This data compounds with scale in a way the host argues no competitor can replicate — citing Waymo's approximately few million miles accumulated over 15 years versus Tesla's ability to add equivalent volumes in weeks from its active fleet.

## Financials

1. **OpenAI Financial Deterioration:** OpenAI's net loss was $13.5 billion in just the first half of 2025. The company projects $14 billion in losses against $20 billion in revenue for 2026, spending $1.35 for every $1 earned. Total projected losses through 2028 are estimated at $44 billion. HSBC projects a $207 billion funding shortfall relative to OpenAI's own growth plans and does not expect profitability until 2030. Stock-based compensation alone was approximately $6 billion in 2025.

2. **Meta Capex Doubling:** Meta raised 2026 capex guidance to $125–145 billion (from $72 billion spent in all of 2025), with AI infrastructure capex tracking toward 54% of revenue — more than half of every dollar of revenue reinvested into infrastructure.

Notable quotes and data:
- "900 million users who cost more to serve than they generate is a structural problem."
- OpenAI spends an estimated $8 per year on inference per user (aggregate inference costs $8.4B in 2025 for ~900M weekly active users)
- DeepSeek R1 training cost: $294,000 confirmed in a peer-reviewed Nature paper (September 2025)
- DeepSeek V4 pricing: $3,048 per million output tokens vs. OpenAI's ~$30 — "less than 12 cents on the dollar"
- Anthropic: $87M annualized revenue in January 2024 → $30 billion by April 2026; CEO said growth outstripped internal forecasts by a factor of eight
- Claude Code: $0 → $1B annualized revenue in ~6 months (May–November 2025); $2.5B by February 2026
- Memphis Colossus complex: ~555,000 Nvidia GPUs, ~$18 billion in silicon, approaching 2 gigawatts, described as 4x the next largest dedicated AI training site
- Colossus built in 122 days vs. a projected 4 years
- Google Cloud revenue: +63% YoY to $20 billion in Q1 2026
- Microsoft AI annualized revenue run rate: $37 billion, +123% YoY
- Meta daily active users across all apps: 3.56 billion as of March 2026
- Llama 4 downloads: over 1 billion since April 2025 release
- Tesla: 9 million+ cars delivered, 1.2 million+ actively running FSD
- Starlink: 10 million+ active customers across 160 countries
- EU AI Act full high-risk enforcement: August 2, 2026
- "Every month that Western frontier labs face meaningful regulatory friction is a month that Chinese labs... narrow the gap."

articles.title: How Tesla Channels Are Being Hijacked In Seconds
articles.body:
This video is a practical cybersecurity discussion hosted by Brian of FutureAzA, featuring Randy Kirk as a guest, covering how YouTube channels and social media accounts get hijacked through phishing schemes. The core thesis is that content creators — including Tesla-focused channels — are targeted by sophisticated phishing attacks disguised as sponsorship offers, and that the standard advice (stronger passwords, two-factor authentication) is insufficient against these methods. The hosts share their personal recovery experiences and offer actionable prevention and recovery tips.

## Market & Competition

1. **Phishing via fake sponsorship emails:** Both Brian and Randy Kirk describe being targeted by scammers posing as legitimate companies offering sponsorship deals. The attack vector involves an email that appears to come from a real company but is sent from a lookalike address, inviting the creator to click a link to join a Zoom meeting or review a contract. Clicking that link immediately grants the attacker access to the creator's Google/Gmail account, which in turn controls their YouTube channel. Randy notes he receives six or seven such sponsor offers per day, all of which he considers scams. Randy also mentions that Dillon Loomis had legitimate sponsors that Randy used as a reference point for what real sponsorship looks like.

2. **The attack chain and its consequences:** Once the Gmail account is compromised, attackers move quickly — changing the backup email address, backup phone numbers, and even the physical address on file with Google. In Randy's case, the hackers published a cryptocurrency scam video on his channel within a very short time. Brian described watching a real-time battle in his own account where he would change credentials and the hackers would immediately change them back, until Google locked the account entirely. Randy was locked out for approximately two days; Brian for four days; Lars from Best in Tesla for close to a week. The practical fallout includes loss of access to Gmail history, Google Photos, Google Docs, Google Slides, calendar, and contacts — described as "digital bankruptcy."

3. **Why standard security advice falls short:** Both hosts emphasize that two-factor authentication and strong passwords did not protect them, because the attack harvests active session credentials through the phishing page rather than cracking passwords directly. Brian separately described a different incident where his X (Twitter) account was posting content without locking him out — traced not to a password compromise but to a third-party app he had granted permissions to approximately ten years earlier that had since been hacked. Clearing all approved third-party apps resolved the issue.

4. **Recovery steps — reaching the community and platform support:** Randy outlines a recovery process: attempt obvious self-service steps first, then post publicly on social media to solicit community help and moral support. For Google/YouTube specifically, he found that the only viable path to human support was through X (Twitter) by contacting @YouTube and @YouTubeCreators, not through Google's own website. Brian Wong, whose account Randy also manages, went through the same process simultaneously and was resolved within a couple of days after engaging the YouTube Creators account on X. Randy also used Grok throughout the process to interpret and correctly execute each recovery step Google instructed.

5. **Using Grok as a phishing detection and research tool:** Both hosts recommend sending a screenshot of suspicious emails to Grok before clicking anything. Randy states that Grok "immediately came back and gave chapter and verse of why it was not legit" when shown an email that appeared completely legitimate to human inspection. Brian separately used Grok to identify a suspicious domain — he looked up the URL via a WHOIS lookup and found the website had been created only three days earlier. Both hosts also note they now use Grok over Google Search for general research queries, citing Google's AI overviews as frequently wrong, search results as deliberately unhelpful to maximize session time, and the overall algorithm as degraded by business interests overriding engineering quality.

Notable quotes and data:
- Randy: "They were scamming me in order to be able to scam you" — describing the two-layer fraud of using a compromised creator's channel to run crypto scams against the creator's audience.
- Brian: "You may as well have declared digital bankruptcy" — on losing access to all Google-linked services simultaneously.
- Brian: "No one's looking out for you but you" — after reaching out to an X safety contact about a phishing DM and receiving no response.
- Brian: "I can see myself doing battle in real time with the hackers where I'm trying to change things and they're quickly changing them back."
- Randy on Grok: "Completely spelled correctly, everything totally looked right — which many times they don't, and that's your clue. But this was across the board, looked great, but Grok immediately — no way, no how."
- Brian on Google: "There's a reason they took 'don't be evil' out of their motto."
- Recovery timeline: Randy — ~2 days; Brian — 4 days; Lars (Best in Tesla) — approximately a week.

articles.title: Why MicroStrategy Could OUTPERFORM Bitcoin w/ Cern Basher
articles.body:
This episode features Jo Bhakdi in conversation with Cern Basher, discussing MicroStrategy (now rebranded "Strategy") as a Bitcoin treasury company, its preferred stock instruments (particularly STRC), and the broader thesis connecting Bitcoin's proof-of-work security model to the challenge of constraining artificial intelligence agents. The core argument is that Strategy's financial engineering — raising permanent capital via perpetual preferred shares to accumulate Bitcoin — is misunderstood as a Ponzi scheme when it more closely resembles the operating model of an insurance company, and that Bitcoin's energy-grounded security may make it uniquely suited to tethering AI agents to the physical world.

## Market & Competition

1. **Strategy as a Bitcoin Treasury Company:** Cern Basher explains that Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) acquires Bitcoin by selling equity, raising convertible debt, and issuing perpetual preferred shares. The company currently holds approximately $64 billion in Bitcoin on its balance sheet and owns roughly 4% of all Bitcoin that will ever be mined. The preferred instruments — particularly STRC — are described not as debt but as permanent capital with no maturity date, meaning there is no obligation to repay principal, only to service dividends.

2. **STRC Preferred Stock Mechanics and Yield:** STRC currently pays an 11–12% dividend yield. Cern Basher argues this is sustainable because Strategy holds roughly five times as much collateral in Bitcoin as it has issued in preferred stock, meaning Bitcoin only needs to appreciate approximately 2.4% per year for the preferred dividends to be fully covered indefinitely. The company also maintains a dedicated cash reserve of $2.25 billion, sufficient to cover approximately 15–16 months of dividend payments without touching Bitcoin holdings.

3. **Capital Raising Pace and Bitcoin Per Share Growth:** Strategy completed what was described as its eighth purchase of over $2 billion in Bitcoin in a single week, the most recent being approximately $2.1 billion raised by selling STRC. Bitcoin per share grew 22.9% in 2025. As of the video's publish date, Bitcoin per share has increased 12.6% year-to-date in 2026, and if the current capital-raising pace continues through year-end, the annualized Bitcoin-per-share growth rate is projected to reach approximately 37% for 2026.

4. **NAV Premium and Leverage Profile:** Strategy's market cap currently trades at approximately a 1.23x premium to its net asset value (MNAV), compared to a historical high of approximately 4x and a low of approximately 1.02x — meaning the stock is much closer to its historical floor than its ceiling. The company carries $8.2 billion in convertible debt, but Cern Basher notes a deal was in progress to retire approximately $1.5 billion of that debt, reducing leverage. Bitcoin would need to fall to approximately $13,000 for the debt to exceed assets. The $15.5 billion in preferred stock is characterized as amplification rather than leverage because it is perpetual and never needs to be repaid.

5. **Tax Treatment of STRC Dividends:** Because Strategy pays dividends from capital raises rather than earnings, the dividends receive "return of capital" tax treatment under a U.S. tax provision described as dating to approximately 1910. This means each dividend payment reduces the holder's cost basis rather than triggering taxable income. At an 11–12% annual payout on a $100 par-value share, a holder's cost basis reaches zero after approximately 9.5 years, after which dividends are expected to be taxed as qualified dividends at long-term capital gains rates. Cern Basher and Jo Bhakdi also note that for married couples filing jointly with taxable income below $98,900, the U.S. long-term capital gains tax rate is 0%, and STRC return-of-capital payments do not count toward that income threshold.

6. **Sharpe Ratio and Investment Positioning:** Cern Basher cites STRC Sharpe ratios above 2.0, which he describes as exceeding typical hedge fund alpha generation. He positions STRC as an income alternative superior to CDs, money market funds, investment-grade bonds, junk bonds, and private credit, particularly for investors seeking yield without locking up capital for extended periods. He also suggests Tesla shareholders who sell covered calls to generate income could use STRC as an alternative that does not expose their Tesla shares to assignment risk, especially if margin rates are below 5.5%, creating a potential spread of approximately 6%.

7. **MicroStrategy's MNAV and the Digital Security Thesis:** Cern Basher argues that because Bitcoin's proof-of-work mechanism makes it a physical-energy-grounded security technology rather than merely money, Strategy's largest-corporate-holder status (4% of total Bitcoin supply) could justify a much higher MNAV than 1.23x if the market begins to price it as the world's largest digital security company rather than simply a leveraged Bitcoin vehicle. He references Jason Lowry's book *Soft War* as articulating the case that Bitcoin is fundamentally a security technology analogous to gunpowder — misunderstood as money because of its name.

## Market & Competition (AI and Bitcoin Intersection)

1. **Bitcoin as an AI Containment Mechanism:** Cern Basher argues that traditional software-based security measures (CAPTCHAs, passwords, permission codes) will become ineffective against AI agents, which can already hire humans via marketplaces to bypass CAPTCHAs. Bitcoin's proof-of-work system, which requires real-world energy expenditure that cannot be faked, may be the only scalable mechanism for constraining AI agent activity. He notes that U.S. Admiral Paparo testified before Congress approximately two weeks prior to the video's publish date that the military is actively testing Bitcoin for protecting U.S. computer systems, following a Congressional mandate from late 2025. A formal report to Congress is expected by end of 2026.

2. **Proof-of-Work vs. Proof-of-Stake for Security:** Cern Basher explains why Bitcoin's proof-of-work is preferred over Ethereum's proof-of-stake for security applications: the energy friction in proof-of-work is precisely the feature that makes it resistant to attack, whereas proof-of-stake can potentially be gamed. He acknowledges Ethereum and Solana may serve complementary roles (smart contracts, high transaction volume) but suggests Ethereum's security is materially weaker than Bitcoin's for containment purposes.

3. **AI Agent Proliferation Timeline:** Both speakers express the view that the inflection point for AI agent proliferation — where agents outnumber human internet actors and create unmanageable security problems — could arrive as soon as 2026, not 2040 as many assume. Jo Bhakdi references Nvidia's enterprise AI deployments and suggests that a company like Anthropic could become one of the largest companies on the planet within a year, citing exponential growth metrics across all AI-related benchmarks.

Notable quotes and data:
- STRC dividend yield: 11–12% (raised from initial 9% at launch)
- Bitcoin needs to appreciate only **2.4% per year** for STRC dividends to be fully sustainable at current rates
- Strategy cash reserve: **$2.25 billion**, covering approximately **15–16 months** of dividends
- Strategy Bitcoin holdings: approximately **$64 billion**
- Strategy owns approximately **4%** of all Bitcoin that will ever be mined
- Bitcoin per share growth: **22.9% in 2025**; **12.6% YTD in 2026**; projected **~37% for full year 2026** at current pace
- Current MNAV: approximately **1.23x**; historical high ~**4x**; historical low ~**1.02x**
- Convertible debt: **$8.2 billion**; deal underway to retire ~**$1.5 billion**
- Bitcoin would need to fall to approximately **$13,000** for debt to exceed assets
- Preferred stock outstanding: approximately **$15.5 billion** (perpetual, no maturity)
- STRC cost basis reaches zero after approximately **9.5 years** of dividends at current rates
- U.S. 0% long-term capital gains bracket threshold (2026): **$98,900** for married filing jointly; approximately **$49,450** for single filers
- STRC Sharpe ratio: **above 2.0**
- 57% of STRC transactions above $100 par value last week were Strategy selling new shares into the market
- Strategy made its **eighth** single-week Bitcoin purchase exceeding $2 billion; most recent purchase approximately **$2.1 billion**
- Cern Basher: *"Bitcoin in this case… only has to go up 2.4% a year for this to be sustainable forever at current dividend rates."*
- Jo Bhakdi: *"There is no such thing as safety. There's only engineering."*

articles.title: Daily X Summary (2026-05-23)
articles.body:
## Executive Summary
Today's posts surface three meaningful Tesla investor signals: Tesla's European FSD monetization strategy shifted entirely to subscription, removing one-time purchase options; Meta committed ~$200M to Tesla Megapack batteries for AI datacenter infrastructure in Wyoming; and Tesla is expanding its vehicle sales footprint into Bulgaria. The overall tone is quietly bullish, with recurring evidence of Tesla Energy becoming critical infrastructure and FSD transitioning toward a recurring revenue model in Europe.

---

## Key Posts / Themes

1. **FSD Europe Moves to Subscription-Only, Eliminating One-Time Purchases:** Tesla has ended one-time FSD purchases across Europe, making subscription the only available option. Pricing is set at £99/month in the UK and €99/month in most other European countries. This is a notable monetization shift — it converts FSD from a one-time capital purchase into a recurring revenue stream, which could improve revenue predictability and increase lifetime value per vehicle if retention is strong. It also lowers the upfront barrier to FSD adoption, potentially broadening the addressable customer base in Europe.

2. **Meta to Deploy ~$200M in Tesla Megapack at Wyoming AI Datacenters:** Meta is purchasing approximately $200 million worth of Tesla Megapack batteries to help power AI datacenters in Wyoming. Sawyer frames this as further evidence of Tesla Energy becoming critical infrastructure for the AI buildout — a theme that has been growing as hyperscalers seek large-scale grid storage solutions. This is a significant named customer win for Tesla Energy and reinforces the commercial demand signal for Megapack at scale.

3. **Tesla Expanding into Bulgaria:** Tesla filed to launch vehicle sales and service in Bulgaria for the first time last month, and has now posted multiple new job listings in the country ahead of the launch. While Bulgaria is a smaller market, it reflects continued geographic expansion of Tesla's direct-sales model in Europe.

4. **Mercedes Plans Urban Autonomous Driving Launch in Germany by End of 2026:** Mercedes announced plans to roll out an urban point-to-point automated driving system in selected German cities by end of 2026, positioning itself as one of the first carmakers to offer such technology in Germany. This is a competitive development worth monitoring, though Tesla's FSD approach and scale differ materially from Mercedes' city-limited, likely ODD-constrained system.

---

## Signal Strength: **Bullish** — The combination of Tesla Energy securing a major ~$200M AI infrastructure contract with Meta, FSD Europe transitioning to a recurring subscription model, and continued geographic expansion into new markets collectively reinforces multiple legs of the Tesla growth thesis.

articles.title: What is SpaceX Actually Worth?
articles.body:
This video from the "brighterwithherbert" channel features host Herbert and guest Larry Goldberg, a serial entrepreneur and venture capital investor, breaking down SpaceX's S1 IPO filing. The core thesis is that SpaceX is far more than a rocket or satellite company — it is rapidly becoming an AI compute-as-a-service business, with a self-described total addressable market of $28.5 trillion, the vast majority of which is in artificial intelligence enterprise applications. The discussion centers on the Anthropic compute deal, Starlink's growth trajectory, and the long-term vision for orbital data centers and beyond.

## Market & Competition

1. **SpaceX's TAM Claim — $28.5 Trillion, Mostly AI:** The SpaceX S1 filing claims what it calls "the largest actionable total addressable market in human history," estimated at $28.5 trillion. Of that, $26.5 trillion is attributed to AI, broken down as $2.5 trillion in AI infrastructure, approximately $760 billion in consumer subscriptions, $600 billion in digital advertising, and $22.7 trillion in enterprise applications. Only $370 billion is attributed to space-enabled solutions, and $1.6 trillion to connectivity (including $870 billion in Starlink broadband and $7–40 billion in Starlink mobile). China and Russia are excluded from these global estimates. Larry Goldberg notes the $22.7 trillion enterprise applications figure is consistent with figures he tracked during his own career in that industry, and argues the precise number matters less than the sheer magnitude of the opportunity.

2. **AI Compute as a Service — The "Real Business":** Both host and guest argue that the most underappreciated revelation in the SpaceX filing is that Elon Musk explicitly stated SpaceX is "offering AI compute as a service at significant scale" and is "in discussions with other companies to do the same." This positions SpaceX not merely as a launch or connectivity provider but as a hyperscaler — analogous to AWS — renting GPU compute capacity to frontier AI labs. Goldberg argues this business, enabled by SpaceX's own data center infrastructure (Colossus, Macrohard, and "Macro Harder"), is the central value driver going forward, particularly as orbital data centers come online.

3. **Anthropic Deal — $1.25 Billion Per Month:** The S1 filing discloses that Anthropic has agreed to pay SpaceX $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 for access to AI compute capacity across both Colossus and Colossus 2, with capacity ramping in May and June at a reduced fee. Either party may terminate the agreement with 90 days' notice. Anthropic publicly confirmed the deal, stating it would be scaling up on GB200 capacity through June. Goldberg claims he predicted the deal would be worth approximately $15 billion annually when analysts were citing figures of $6–8 billion, reasoning that Anthropic was losing $18–20 billion per month in potential revenue by throttling customers due to compute constraints.

4. **Competitive Landscape — AI Frontier Models:** Goldberg offers his assessment of the competitive positioning of frontier AI companies. He argues Anthropic's Claude found the right strategic path by focusing on enterprise and coding (agentic AI), while Grok focused on consumer content and OpenAI on chatbots. He contends enterprise applications represent the most important near-term battleground, and that all frontier players — Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and xAI — will find niches in what he describes as a market that has "barely scratched the surface." He warns that coding, currently the focus of competitive benchmarking, is "not even the tip of the iceberg" relative to the full AI TAM.

5. **Cursor Partnership and xAI Competitive Position:** The S1 filing includes a disclosed right for SpaceX/xAI to acquire Cursor for $60 billion. Cursor's Composer 2.5 is described as approaching the performance of Anthropic's Opus and GPT-5.5 while being significantly cheaper. The host notes Elon Musk commented that Cursor is "an important piece of the puzzle to make Grok much better" and that Anthropic "will not be destroyed" — framing Anthropic as a customer and partner, not a target for elimination. Goldberg acknowledges xAI started three to five years behind leading frontier labs and initially focused on the wrong product direction, but believes it is now "very close to the frontier."

6. **Starlink as Enabling Infrastructure:** Goldberg argues Starlink's value should not be assessed in isolation. With 9,600 satellites (75% active and maneuverable), 164 countries served, and 10.3 million subscribers, Starlink is already a substantial revenue business. More importantly, Goldberg says Starlink bandwidth is the prerequisite for orbital data centers — without a low-latency, high-bandwidth global constellation, AI inference from space-based compute is not viable. He contends that once Starship enters production, each launch could deliver roughly the equivalent bandwidth of an entire year of Falcon 9 satellite launches, causing Starlink capacity to "go vertical." He predicts competitors (citing AST SpaceMobile and Amazon) will face structurally higher launch costs, making it very difficult to compete.

7. **Terafab — The Overlooked "Other Bet":** Near the end of the conversation, Goldberg flags that Brad Gerstner's otherwise praised BG2 podcast analysis mentioned "Terafab" only as a throwaway item under "other bets." Goldberg strongly disagrees with that framing, calling Terafab "the biggest of them all" and saying he has been doing a deep dive into it with significant findings, though the discussion does not elaborate further in this episode.

8. **Predicted Next Move — Microsoft Deal:** The host predicts Microsoft will be the next company to sign an AI compute agreement with SpaceX, noting that Google is already reportedly in talks and Anthropic has already signed. No specific terms or timeline are provided for a potential Microsoft deal.

## Financials

1. **SpaceX S1 Financial Highlights:** The filing discloses the following figures: $18.7 billion in revenue, $6.8 billion in operating cash flow, and $20 billion in capex — of which $7.2 billion is attributed to Starlink and $12.7 billion to AI capex. The connectivity segment generated $3.25 billion in its first quarter with $1 billion (described also as $2 billion in one reference) in income from operations, primarily driven by Starlink, with $11.3 billion in income for operations cited at another point. Goldberg notes the company is already profitable and frames the current moment as the inflection point after 20 years of investment.

2. **Analyst Revenue Estimates and Brad Gerstner's Projection:** Brad Gerstner (BG2 podcast), quoted in the video, estimated that the Anthropic compute deal would generate an incremental $4–5 billion of revenue in the current year, on top of analyst consensus estimates in the "mid-20s" (billions). Goldberg criticizes Gerstner's estimate as too low, arguing Gerstner underestimated both the scope of the deal (not realizing Blackwell GPUs were included) and the broader opportunity by "at least an order of magnitude." Gerstner's framing — that the deal "takes pressure off xAI delivering immediate revenue" and establishes SpaceX as an immediate hyperscaler competitor — is described as directionally correct but insufficiently ambitious.

Notable quotes and data:
- **SpaceX S1 on mission:** *"We do not want humans to have the same fate as dinosaurs."*
- **Elon Musk (quoted in filing):** *"SpaceX is offering AI compute as a service at a significant scale... We're in discussions with other companies to do the same... We expect to serve AI at extremely high scale like no one else can do this."*
- **Anthropic public statement:** *"In the next few days we'll be ramping Claude inference on Colossus. Grateful to be partnering with SpaceX... We're expanding our partnership with SpaceX and will be scaling up on GB200 capacity throughout June."*
- **Brad Gerstner (BG2, quoted):** *"There's nobody better on planet Earth than Elon at converting electrons to tokens... He said he was building AWS all along or EWS all along."*
- **SpaceX TAM:** $28.5 trillion total; $26.5 trillion AI; $22.7 trillion enterprise applications alone
- **Anthropic deal:** $1.25 billion/month through May 2029, covering Colossus and Colossus 2, terminable on 90 days' notice
- **Starlink:** 9,600 satellites, 10.3 million subscribers, 164 countries
- **SpaceX revenue:** $18.7 billion; Operating cash flow: $6.8 billion; Capex: $20 billion ($12.7B AI, $7.2B Starlink)
- **Cursor acquisition option:** Right to buy Cursor for $60 billion (disclosed in S1)
- **Goldberg's Anthropic revenue estimate:** ~$15 billion annually vs. analyst consensus of $6–8 billion
- **Gerstner's incremental revenue estimate:** $4–5 billion this year from Anthropic deal, on top of mid-$20 billion analyst consensus

articles.title: Anthropic Is Paying Elon $1.25 Billion A Month
articles.body:
This video argues that the SpaceX IPO S1 filing reveals Elon Musk's overarching strategy across all his companies: build expensive physical infrastructure, then rent access to it as recurring service revenue — a playbook identical to Amazon's transformation from retailer to cloud giant via AWS. The host draws a direct line from the Anthropic compute deal to Tesla's own ambitions in robotaxi, FSD subscriptions, energy, and Optimus, framing Tesla not as a car company but as a physical AI platform in the making.

## Market & Competition

1. **The Anthropic Deal — "Elon Web Services":** In May 2026, SpaceX signed a cloud services agreement with Anthropic for $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with capacity ramping up in May and June at a reduced fee. Either side can cancel on 90 days' notice, and Anthropic retains ownership of its content, AI models, and data. Investor Brad Gerstner, appearing on the All-In podcast, dubbed this "EWS — Elon Web Services," drawing a direct analogy to AWS. Elon Musk himself called the strategy "AI compute as a service." Gerstner estimated the Anthropic deal would generate an incremental $4–5 billion in revenue for SpaceX in 2026 (not the full annualized $15 billion run rate, because capacity is still ramping through mid-2026).

2. **The Amazon Playbook Applied to SpaceX:** The S1 filing states verbatim that the structure "allows us to monetize unused compute capacity in our infrastructure while still permitting a reallocation of the capacity for our own internal initiatives if needed in the future." The host explains this mirrors Amazon's early 2000s move: Amazon built compute for its own store, found spare capacity sitting idle, and rented it to others — that became AWS, which generated most of Amazon's profit for years. SpaceX built the Colossus data center cluster (near Memphis, described as a mix of hardware including H100s, better suited for inference than top-tier model training) to train Grok, then rented the underutilized capacity to Anthropic. A rival AI company (Anthropic competes with Grok) is effectively funding the data centers that train Elon's own AI — the same dynamic as Netflix running on Amazon servers while competing with Amazon Video.

3. **SpaceX's Stated TAM and Orbital Data Centers:** The S1 filing claims SpaceX has "identified the largest actionable total addressable market in human history" at $28.5 trillion — broken down as approximately $370 billion in space, approximately $1.6–1.26 trillion in connectivity (Starlink broadband and mobile), and approximately $26.12 trillion in AI. The filing explicitly notes China and Russia were excluded from that estimate. SpaceX's longer-term vision includes orbital data centers — the company has requested permission to launch up to one million satellites for this purpose and says deployment could begin as early as 2028, leveraging unlimited solar power and the cold of space for cooling, made economically viable by reusable Starship rockets.

4. **Starlink as the Cash Engine:** According to the filing, Starlink generated approximately $11.4 billion in revenue in 2025, with operating income of $4.4 billion, growing nearly 50% in a single year. Subscribers grew from 5 million to 10.3 million across 164 countries in 12 months. The host frames Starlink as the retail business that funds the compute buildout — analogous to Amazon's retail arm funding early AWS. SpaceX as a combined entity (including the AI buildout) is still posting a net loss of a few billion dollars per quarter; the Anthropic deal is described as moving toward break-even, not immediate profitability.

5. **Competitive Risks and Honest Caveats:** The host flags three key risks: (1) The 90-day cancellation clause means the $15 billion annual run rate is not locked in — Anthropic could build its own data centers and walk away quickly. (2) The combined SpaceX/AI business is still losing billions per quarter; the Anthropic revenue offsets costs but does not yet produce profit. (3) SpaceX's valuation of approximately $1.75–2 trillion on under $20 billion in revenue implies an enormous multiple based largely on belief in Starship, orbital compute, and Grok — none of which are yet generating serious profit.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD Subscriptions as Recurring Revenue:** The host cites 1.28 million active FSD subscribers as of the time of the video, with the subscription count described as climbing. Cumulative supervised miles are stated at approximately 9–10 billion. FSD is presented as the first layer of Tesla's recurring revenue stack, analogous to Starlink subscriptions funding SpaceX's infrastructure.

## Robotaxi

1. **Austin Driverless Robotaxi — Real But Limited:** The host confirms that driverless (unsupervised) robotaxi rides with no one in the seat are running in Austin, Texas, describing it as a network that takes a cut of every ride. However, he explicitly notes Austin is the only city where this is operating and flags it as a key metric to watch — specifically whether the city list expands, with the next milestone being additional cities by 2027 as a scenario for the thesis to "half work."

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus Still in Testing Phase:** The host states that Optimus is still being tested inside Tesla's factories and is not yet working on production lines. He also notes Tesla has not given a 2026 production number for Optimus. This is offered as a candid counterpoint to the bull case — the recurring revenue story from robotics remains a thesis, not yet reflected in financial results.

## Financials

1. **Tesla's AI Capex Surge:** On Tesla's Q1 earnings call, the company disclosed it is more than doubling its AI compute in approximately 6 months. Tesla raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to over $25 billion, described as roughly three times what it spent the prior year. The host frames this as Tesla pouring money into the same category of physical AI infrastructure as SpaceX, and says the thesis is "working" only if that spending eventually converts into service revenue.

2. **The Platform Valuation Thesis:** The host argues that if even a portion of Tesla's installed base (cars already on the road), FSD subscriptions, robotaxi network, charging network, insurance, and energy business (Megapacks and Powerwalls) converts to recurring service revenue, valuing Tesla like Ford or GM "stops making any sense." The SpaceX filing is presented as the strongest real-world evidence yet that the "physical AI platform" playbook can work — but the host is careful to note the recurring revenue has not yet shown up meaningfully on Tesla's income statement.

Notable quotes and data:
- Anthropic deal: $1.25 billion/month through May 2029 → ~$15 billion annualized run rate
- Gerstner's 2026 revenue estimate from the Anthropic deal: $4–5 billion incremental
- Starlink 2025 revenue: ~$11.4 billion; operating income: ~$4.4 billion; ~50% YoY growth
- Starlink subscribers: grew from 5 million to 10.3 million in 12 months, across 164 countries
- SpaceX stated TAM: $28.5 trillion total (~$26 trillion attributed to AI), excluding China and Russia
- SpaceX requested permission to launch up to 1 million satellites for orbital data centers; potential start date as early as 2028
- Tesla FSD active subscribers: 1.28 million
- Tesla cumulative supervised FSD miles: ~9–10 billion
- Tesla 2026 capex guidance: over $25 billion (~3x prior year)
- Tesla AI compute: more than doubling in ~6 months (per Q1 call)
- Driverless robotaxi: operational in Austin only
- Optimus: still in factory testing, no 2026 production number given
- SpaceX valuation: approximately $1.75–2 trillion anticipated at IPO
- Gerstner quote: "There's nobody better on planet Earth than Elon at converting electrons to tokens."
- Elon Musk quote on EWS: "SpaceX is offering AI compute as a service at significant scale. We are in discussions with other companies to do the same."
- S1 quote on TAM: "We believe we have identified the largest actionable total addressable market in human history."
- Three SpaceX compute facilities named: Colossus, Macrohard, and Macrohard (sic — "Macro hard and Macro harder"), with 1.2 gigawatts in the latter two running Blackwell hardware

articles.title: Europe Just Triggered Tesla’s Biggest FSD Breakthrough
articles.body:
This episode of FutureAzA features host Brian and guest Herbert discussing the rapid expansion of Tesla's Full Self-Driving regulatory approvals across Europe, with multiple countries following the Netherlands' lead in quick succession. The core thesis is that European FSD approvals are snowballing — creating a "copy-paste" effect where early approvals make it easier and faster for subsequent countries to sign on. The hosts also discuss FSD's qualitative capabilities, the vision-vs-lidar debate, and broader Tesla market momentum.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Netherlands Approval Triggers European Domino Effect:** The Netherlands became the first European country to formally approve Tesla's Full Self-Driving (supervised), following approximately 150,000 kilometers of testing over roughly a year and a half. According to Case Roland, once the Netherlands approved it, other countries can effectively "copy-paste" the approval, dramatically lowering the barrier for subsequent nations. A broader EU member-state vote — involving approximately 28 countries — is expected in June or possibly September 2026.

2. **Lithuania Approves FSD; Greece, Belgium, and Ireland in Motion:** Lithuania became the second European country to approve FSD shortly after the Netherlands. Greece had been planning to be second but was narrowly beaten out and is expected to formally approve soon. Belgium's Flemish region announced plans to conduct 5,000 km of testing before approving, with the second Belgian region also signaling intent to follow. Ireland has also made noise about moving forward. Tesla is reported to be actively engaging individual country governments to facilitate approvals.

3. **FSD Now Available in Approximately 10 Regions Globally:** Herbert notes that FSD has now been approved in roughly 10 regions worldwide, though Brian clarifies this counts regions rather than strictly sovereign nations (e.g., Puerto Rico counted separately). Herbert describes extensive personal experience using FSD throughout Vancouver, Canada with no issues, and credits those demonstrations as the reason his sister decided to purchase a Model Y.

4. **Vision-Over-Lidar Argument: Intelligence vs. Sensors:** The hosts make a sustained argument that FSD's camera-based, AI-driven approach is superior to lidar-dependent systems like Waymo and Zoox. The key claim is that Tesla's system has a "smarter brain" — it can identify what objects are (a cow, a moose, a cat), understand intent (e.g., a car beginning to turn), and act preemptively, whereas lidar-based systems see objects but may not classify or respond to them as intelligently. Herbert references a Swami (likely referring to a Tesla AI executive) statement from roughly 18–24 months prior, in which he said FSD can identify fog as fog and therefore navigate through it — whereas lidar sees only an opaque wall.

5. **FSD Subscriber Growth and Paid Adoption:** Brian notes that paid FSD subscribers increased by 170,000 last quarter and expects that trend to continue as more units reach more countries.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Tesla Market Share Milestones in Emerging Markets:** Brian highlights that Tesla is the leading import in both South Korea and Japan, and — most notably — the number one car overall (not just EV) in Colombia, which he describes as a significant milestone. He expresses surprise at Tesla's dominance in these newer and emerging markets and expects 2026 to be a stronger sales year than 2025.

Notable quotes and data:
- "FSD will never be a mainstream product because it's only been approved for use in one country" — Brian citing former skeptic argument, now countered by ~10 approved regions
- FSD paid subscribers grew by **170,000** last quarter
- Netherlands conducted approximately **150,000 kilometers** of testing before approving FSD
- Belgium's Flemish region plans **5,000 km** of testing before approval
- EU member-state vote expected in **June or September 2026**, involving approximately **28 member states**
- Tesla is the **#1 car overall** (not just EV) in Colombia
- Tesla is the **leading import** in South Korea and Japan
- Herbert: "Our cars actually know what [the object] is that's running across it" — on vision vs. lidar intelligence
- Brian on lidar: "Would you want to drive a car where the driver is a committee? That's what you have when you have competing inputs."

articles.title: Will Tesla Stock Get Back To $490? Iran, SpaceX and WEEKLY OUTLOOK
articles.body:
Jo Bhakdi delivers a Sunday macro and Tesla outlook focused on whether Tesla stock can return to its prior all-time high of $490, reached on December 16th, 2025. The core thesis is that the primary variable is macroeconomic — specifically, resolution of the Strait of Hormuz situation with Iran — and that a successful outcome there, combined with strong Nvidia earnings validating the AGI investment cycle, sets up a second rally leg for Tesla and the broader market. Secondary catalysts discussed include the SpaceX Starship Flight Test 3 launch and the upcoming SpaceX IPO, as well as longer-term Tesla-specific drivers including Cybercab production scale, Optimus, and robotaxi deployment.

## Market & Competition

1. **Iran / Strait of Hormuz as the decisive macro variable:** Jo Bhakdi argues that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz was the single biggest risk factor suppressing Tesla's stock and the broader market rally. He reiterates a prediction made approximately three weeks prior that the conflict is "de facto over," citing irresistible economic pressure on both the US and Iran. Weekend news reports — including Trump's comments to CBS News and Iran's semi-official FARC news agency — indicate negotiators are finalizing an agreement that includes a process to reopen the Strait, the unfreezing of some Iranian assets, and a continuation of negotiations. Bhakdi expects Iran to retain management of the Strait and likely collect tolls, with a face-saving nuclear agreement that lacks real teeth — a pragmatic outcome driven by the impossibility of keeping global trade disrupted.

2. **Nvidia earnings as AGI validation:** Bhakdi cites recent Nvidia earnings as a "hard validation point" confirming that the AGI investment cycle is in full swing, with no signs of a bubble. He notes that across the broader market, PE ratios are actually declining even as profits explode — the opposite of bubble conditions. Combined with the Iran resolution, he views this as setting up a renewed rally in the NASDAQ and Tesla.

3. **NASDAQ trend line and Tesla stock price outlook:** Bhakdi observes that the NASDAQ has experienced a massive run-up since 2023 and is currently slightly above the long-run trend line. He considers it plausible that the trend line itself steepens given accelerating earnings growth. His base case is that Tesla makes a second attempt at $490, with the stock having previously rallied from approximately $350 to $450 before pulling back to $395 on Iran and bond yield fears. He views $490 as a reflection of Tesla's fundamental strength, independent of robotaxi scaling — it simply represents the prior all-time high that Tesla "belongs" at given the company is stronger now than in December 2025.

4. **SpaceX IPO — correlation to Tesla, not a liquidity drain:** Bhakdi dismisses fears that investors will sell Tesla shares to fund SpaceX IPO participation, citing a $75 billion IPO size with roughly 70% institutional participation — resulting in only negligible liquidity effects on Tesla. He argues the more important dynamic is that SpaceX success correlates positively with Tesla's share price due to "merger fantasies." He has reduced his probability estimate that a SpaceX-Tesla merger occurs in the current year (2026), viewing it as more likely in 2027 or later. He plans to buy approximately 10 SpaceX shares personally as a "tracker" position but does not plan significant exposure given valuation concerns and an expected post-IPO dip.

## Robotaxi

1. **Robotaxi scaling not part of the $490 thesis, but critical for upside beyond it:** Bhakdi explicitly separates his $490 price target from robotaxi scaling — he says $490 is purely based on the prior all-time high and Tesla's fundamental strength. However, he acknowledges that if robotaxi keeps failing to scale once Tesla reaches $490, the stock becomes vulnerable to another correction. Conversely, if robotaxi does scale, $490 becomes irrelevant — the stock would trade at "a completely different number." He references predictions from "Cern" and "Herbert" alongside his own of 15,000 robotaxis by end of 2026 as the bull case scenario.

2. **Cybercab production as a forcing function for robotaxi deployment:** Bhakdi responds to a commenter's suggestion that the robotaxi fleet might cap at 1,500 vehicles by year-end by pointing to Cybercab hardware production. He states that 10,000 to 15,000 Cybercabs are expected to be produced by end of 2026, noting that hardware capex creates an implicit forcing function — Tesla would not be producing that volume if they intended to leave vehicles sitting idle. He also mentions that Cybercab parking infrastructure has been spotted under construction in Dallas and other locations, signaling active operational buildout. He additionally floats a higher production scenario of 40,000–50,000 Cybercabs for the year, but uses 10,000–20,000 as his working modeling range.

3. **Austin robotaxi activity and unsupervised expansion:** A commenter raises the observation that robotaxi counts in Austin appear to be declining. Bhakdi does not dispute the observation but suggests a plausible interpretation: Tesla may be shifting toward increasing the proportion of unsupervised rides in Austin and growing from that narrower but higher-quality base, rather than maximizing total supervised trips. He does not provide specific fleet numbers from the transcript.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus reveal as a near-term catalyst:** Bhakdi mentions that an Optimus reveal is scheduled in approximately four to six weeks from the video date (implying late June to early July 2026), and describes it as potentially "very big." He classifies Optimus alongside robotaxi as a catalyst that could drive Tesla well above $490 if it materializes, but does not incorporate it into his base-case $490 prediction. He declines to share specific Optimus production number estimates, stating those will be revealed through upcoming Pioneer Lands research.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Cybertruck production comparison:** Bhakdi uses Cybertruck as a comparison point when discussing Cybercab trajectory, noting that Cybertruck production is at a level he considers the low end of what the factory can afford. He suggests a similar or greater ramp is plausible for Cybercab. He does not provide specific Cybertruck production numbers.

2. **Tesla Semi contribution to earnings:** In response to a viewer question, Bhakdi says he does not expect Tesla Semi to contribute significantly to earnings in the near term, and models meaningful Semi revenue contribution beginning in 2027, with possible Q4 2026 impact.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD personal experience, now dated:** Bhakdi mentions having personally experienced FSD approximately one year prior to the video, in Los Angeles and Texas. He notes it was a pre-current version and does not make specific claims about current FSD capability. FSD is not available to him in Germany.

## Pioneer Lands Research Platform Preview

1. **Knowledge graph and AGI cascade model:** Bhakdi previews a major research infrastructure project called the Pioneer Lands "knowledge graph" — a structured map of AGI-driven disruption themes including Space AGI, digital humans (including Optimus and Anthropic-type systems), autonomous transport (robotaxi, robo-trucking), and blue-collar robot replacement. The graph links these themes to downstream effects on stocks, sectors, personal life design, capital income, fiscal impact, and geopolitical outcomes. Quantitative models being built include robotaxi cost of goods sold per mile scenarios, robo-trucking scaling timelines for the US and Europe, Starship dollar-per-kilogram trajectory, and AI buildout elasticity. The platform will be initially available only to "Pioneer Lands Citizens."

Notable quotes and data:
- "On December 16th, we hit $490." (prior Tesla all-time high, per Bhakdi)
- "Tesla ran from $350 → $450 → pulled back to $395 on Iran and bond yield fears"
- "If we have 15,000 robotaxis end of the year, we will not be at $490. We will be at a completely different number."
- "Look at Cybercab production — we will have 15,000 or 10,000 Cybercabs produced by end of the year."
- "I think we could produce 40,000–50,000 Cybercabs this year" (higher scenario)
- "SpaceX IPO: ~$75 billion, ~70% from institutions"
- "I decrease my probability that [SpaceX-Tesla merger] happens this year — more likely next year or year after"
- Starship Flight 3: 66-minute flight, booster 19, ship 39, 33 Raptor engines, 22 Starlink simulators, launched from Orbital Launchpad 2 in Texas; booster flip maneuver failed and was destroyed; ship survived peak heating, executed controlled landing burn, splashed on target in Indian Ocean, then tipped over and exploded
- "I think Tesla Semi will become very significant in 2027. Maybe Q4 [2026]."
- "Fair value [for Tesla] is $1,000 for this year" (Bhakdi's intrinsic value estimate, distinct from stock price target)
- "If Tesla gets to $680 and robotaxi isn't scaling, I would say sell it."
- Optimus reveal approximately 4–6 weeks out from publish date (late June–early July 2026)
- Tail risk of Iran conflict escalating was assessed at approximately 5% three weeks prior

articles.title: Daily X Summary (2026-05-24)
articles.body:
## Executive Summary
Today's posts are light on high-signal Tesla investment content, with the most substantive items being two firsthand FSD V14 behavioral demonstrations and a notable FSD Europe cumulative mileage milestone. The majority of posts are low-signal (SpaceX Starship test, SpaceX shareholder meeting commentary, Tesla FIFA World Cup merchandise, and a viral photo/meme).

---

## Key Posts / Themes

1. **FSD V14 Behavioral Improvements — Real-World Demonstrations:** Two posts from Sawyer's personal driving experience highlight qualitative improvements in FSD V14's situational awareness. In one instance, FSD V14.3.3 was observed pulling well to the right to yield for an emergency vehicle. In a separate trip, FSD V14 (version unspecified beyond "V14") detected the reverse lights of a car that had overshot a stop line in an intersection and proactively backed up to make room — behavior Sawyer described as "sentience." These are anecdotal observations rather than statistically significant data, but they illustrate the system's improving real-time reactive driving logic, which is directly relevant to the safety and deployment readiness of Tesla's autonomous stack.

2. **FSD Europe Cumulative Mileage — Rapid Accumulation Rate:** Sawyer flagged an impressive mileage accumulation rate for FSD Supervised in the Netherlands and Lithuania. He notes that Tesla owners in those two countries collectively hit 15 million kilometers just two days prior, and that the subsequent 48-hour pace implies roughly 2.5 million kilometers (approximately 1.55 million miles) per day from that cohort alone. This suggests strong FSD adoption and active usage rates in early European markets, which is a positive signal for international FSD expansion momentum.

3. **SpaceX / Off-Tesla Content (Low Tesla-Relevance):** Two posts cover SpaceX's 12th Starship test flight (all 33 Raptor 3 engines ignited; one engine shut down during ascent before a successful first-stage ascent) and commentary about upcoming annual SpaceX shareholder meetings. While these are high-engagement posts, they have no direct bearing on Tesla's investment thesis. Tesla's FIFA World Cup merchandise collection (soccer ball at $55, jersey at $95, snapback at $35, socks at $30) is noted but is immaterial to the autonomous driving or robotaxi thesis.

---

## Signal Strength: **Mildly Bullish** — FSD V14's demonstrated emergency vehicle yielding and real-time reverse detection behaviors are qualitative positive indicators for autonomous capability maturation, and the rapid European FSD mileage accumulation pace supports the case for growing real-world fleet training data, though today's posts lack hard financial or deployment metrics.

articles.title: Elon, Bezos And Google Just Said The Same Thing!
articles.body:
This video from "brighterwithherbert" features host Herbert and guest Larry Goldberg, a serial entrepreneur and venture capital investor, analyzing statements made by Elon Musk, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, and Jeff Bezos about the future of AI, space, and post-scarcity abundance. The core thesis is that all three tech titans are converging on the same macro vision — a future of transformative technological growth — and that Tesla investors should understand how Elon Musk's companies (Tesla, SpaceX, Starlink) are uniquely positioned at the intersection of all three mega trends. The discussion draws parallels to historical technological revolutions like electricity, railroads, and the internal combustion engine to contextualize the scale of change ahead.

## Market & Competition

1. **Sundar Pichai on AI as the defining technology shift:** Google CEO Sundar Pichai is quoted saying AI represents the biggest technology shift since the internet, and that even a half-percentage-point boost to the US economy from AI would be a massive contribution. He acknowledges natural dampening mechanisms — including the compute buildout curve being different from the rate of model improvement — and emphasizes the need to diffuse AI into society responsibly. Herbert frames 2026 to 2030 as the window Pichai identifies where individuals can still build and invest before a handful of giants come to dominate.

2. **Larry Goldberg's more bullish counter-view:** Goldberg argues Pichai significantly underestimates AI's impact, comparing it not just to the internet but to the combined discovery of electricity, the telephone, and railroads in the 19th century. He calls it a "step change" rather than incremental growth, citing infrastructure investment numbers from his own portfolio companies as evidence of staggering momentum. He predicts growth rates at least two percentage points higher than current levels by mid-2027, which he describes as potentially the largest in recorded history.

3. **Market concentration debate — 10 titans vs. hundreds:** Herbert argues that AI will produce roughly 10 dominant titans who control industries by virtue of massive capital deployment, while Goldberg pushes back, suggesting there could be 50, 100, or even a thousand "titans" globally because the total addressable market is simply too large for a handful of firms to absorb entirely. Both agree that heavy capital spending today translates into market control tomorrow, and both cite this as a reason to want Tesla and SpaceX investing aggressively now.

4. **Jeff Bezos on AI as a productivity multiplier, not a job killer:** Bezos, interviewed on CNBC, is quoted pushing back against the view that AI will eliminate radiologists or software engineers, instead using the analogy of replacing a shovel with a bulldozer — the worker becomes dramatically more productive, not obsolete. He predicts that productivity gains will be so significant that two-income households may see one partner drop out of the workforce voluntarily, leading to a labor shortage rather than mass unemployment. He also predicts deflation in core goods like food, contingent on not over-regulating the technology too early.

5. **Bezos on for-profit value creation vs. charitable giving:** Bezos is quoted on CNBC stating that "the value to society and civilization from my for-profit companies will be much much larger than the good that I do with my charitable giving," citing Amazon's essential role during the pandemic and letters from new mothers as evidence of real-world impact. Herbert notes that Elon Musk publicly agreed with this statement. Goldberg also endorses the view, pointing to Tesla employing approximately 125,000 people and SpaceX employing somewhere between 12,000 and 16,000 people (Goldberg states he is uncertain of the exact number) as examples of for-profit societal contribution.

6. **Historical disruption cycle as a long-term check on concentration:** Goldberg argues that even if companies like Tesla or SpaceX become extraordinarily dominant, historical precedent — General Electric, Ford, the great railroads, Standard Oil — shows that all concentrated wealth eventually gets disrupted. He frames disruption as "the human condition" and sees it as a natural corrective force, expressing no concern about any single company becoming too powerful in the long run.

## Autonomous Driving / Humanoid Bots / Electric Vehicles (Tesla Positioning)

1. **Elon's vision of "amazing abundance for all":** A video clip of Elon Musk is played in which he describes his ideal future as one where "there's amazing abundance for all," where everyone has incredible medical care, nothing is incurable, no one is hungry, and people are free. He adds nuance around the concept of peace, noting that total peace might require suppression of people and may not be desirable in absolute terms, distinguishing between the absence of large-scale war and total conflict-free existence. Herbert and Goldberg present this vision as the philosophical underpinning of Tesla's mission in autonomous driving, robotics, and energy.

2. **Tesla, SpaceX, and Starlink as convergence plays on all three mega trends:** The hosts explicitly connect the three macro themes — AI, space, and post-scarcity abundance — to Elon's companies, arguing that every major bet these tech titans are making "runs straight through Elon's companies." Starlink is cited as democratizing global internet access, Tesla's workforce and products are framed as direct contributors to societal value, and SpaceX's reusable rocket program is defended against critics who calculate cost-per-ton-to-orbit as a misleading metric for long-term value creation.

3. **Post-scarcity abundance as gradual, not binary:** Goldberg cautions against expecting a sudden abundance switch in 2028, 2035, or 2050, drawing on historical precedent from the printing press and the internet to argue that even transformative technologies improve conditions broadly but don't eliminate relative poverty. He believes a high level of abundance for a large number of people is achievable, but relative poverty will persist. Herbert and Goldberg agree this is a decades-long transition, not a five-year flip.

Notable quotes and data:
- Sundar Pichai (paraphrased): "Even at a half a percentage point higher [GDP growth from AI], that's a massive contribution."
- Jeff Bezos (direct quote): "The value to society and civilization from my for-profit companies will be much much larger than the good that I do with my charitable giving."
- Jeff Bezos (direct quote on AI): "You've been digging out a basement for your house with a shovel and somebody's about to hand you a bulldozer — you should be so happy."
- Elon Musk (direct quote): "Probably a future where there's amazing abundance for all, where everybody has incredible medical care... where anything can be cured, where no one is hungry and people are free to do what they would like."
- Larry Goldberg: "I think it's greater than the discovery of electricity, telephone, and the railroads combined in the 19th century."
- Larry Goldberg: "By the middle of next year [mid-2027], we're going to be seeing growth at least two points higher than it is now — it's going to be historically the largest growth we've ever seen."
- Larry Goldberg: "It is the most exciting time since 1890 to be alive."
- Tesla employment cited: approximately 125,000 people
- SpaceX employment cited: approximately 12,000–16,000 people (Goldberg uncertain of exact figure)
- Bezos on taxation (paraphrased, no clip): bottom 50% of income earners contribute only ~3% of tax revenue and should pay zero taxes; top 1% already pays 40% of all taxes but should pay more

articles.title: Tesla Executives Drop New Announcements
articles.body:
This episode of "brighterwithherbert" covers a wide range of Tesla and SpaceX developments from Memorial Day weekend 2026, featuring commentary from supply chain and manufacturing expert Jeff Lutz.
