There is no payout cap, no requirement to purchase separate intelligent driving insurance, and claims will not raise commercial insurance premiums. Coverage applies to God's Eye A and B systems for one year from delivery; existing owners receive it upon updating to God's Eye 5.0 OTA and it is not restricted to the first or registered owner.

2. **Precedent from parking feature:** BYD applied a similar liability guarantee to L4 smart parking in July 2025, which it says drove feature usage from 21% to 93%. The new policy extends that model to city driving, which BYD calls a "double guarantee."

3. **Tesla's contrasting position:** Tesla's FSD (Supervised) is a Level 2 system and its owner's manual explicitly states drivers bear full responsibility at all times. A Miami federal jury awarded a $243 million judgment against Tesla over a fatal Autopilot crash, assigning Tesla one-third of the blame — a liability Tesla contested rather than absorbed voluntarily.

## Market & Competition

1. **Price gap underscores the contrast:** BYD's LiDAR-equipped God's Eye B system is a one-time 12,000-yuan (~$1,770) option available across BYD's full lineup. Tesla's equivalent in China ("Tesla Assisted Driving") costs 64,000 yuan (~$9,400) as a one-off purchase with no subscription option — roughly five times more expensive, while placing all crash liability on the driver.

2. **BYD's fleet scale:** BYD states it now has 3.15 million vehicles on the road with assisted driving, generating up to 200 million kilometers of driving data per day.

## Editorial Stance
Lambert argues BYD has answered the liability question the industry has spent a decade avoiding, framing the guarantee as both a credible safety statement and a data-harvesting strategy. He contends Tesla, despite 10 billion FSD miles logged, hides behind Level 2 disclaimers and arbitration clauses, and challenges why Tesla won't make a similar commitment. He also cautions readers that God's Eye, like Tesla FSD, remains a Level 2 system requiring driver attention.

Notable quotes and data:
- BYD chairman Wang Chuanfu: "Taking on Level 3 and Level 4 liability early during the Level 2 stage demonstrates the company's absolute confidence in its own technology."
- God's Eye B one-time cost: 12,000 yuan (~$1,770) vs. Tesla Assisted Driving in China: 64,000 yuan (~$9,400)
- BYD fleet: 3.15 million assisted-driving vehicles; up to 200 million km of driving data per day
- Smart parking liability guarantee (July 2025) lifted usage from 21% to 93%
- Tesla Autopilot Miami jury verdict: $243 million, with Tesla assigned one-third of fault

articles.title: Tesla FSD v14 is so good it’s making me dangerously complacent
articles.body:
Electrek editor Fred Lambert — who has tested every version of Tesla Autopilot and FSD since before the original launch — argues that FSD v14 is the most capable version yet, and that its near-perfect performance is creating a dangerous complacency problem that Tesla's marketing is actively worsening.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD v14 performance and the complacency trap:** Lambert reports that after daily driving FSD v14 for several weeks, he now routinely travels hundreds of miles without needing to intervene. Emerging data suggests FSD v14 can travel roughly 2,000 miles between critical interventions — equating to approximately 30–40 hours of driving. He invokes the "ironies of automation" concept (documented since the 1980s) and the "vigilance decrement" effect, noting research shows drivers need 5–8 seconds to mentally reengage after an automated system requests a takeover. Lambert warns that even a 3x safety improvement over prior versions doesn't eliminate the risk of a single moment of inattention.

2. **Real-world incident and third-party warnings:** Lambert cites the crash of Raffi Krikorian — former head of Uber's self-driving division — who totaled his Tesla Model X after FSD's near-perfect performance lulled him into a false sense of security before the system failed in a turn. He also references IIHS warnings about Level 2 system design, NHTSA's expanded crash reporting requirements for Level 2 ADAS, and a Reuters report in which seven of nine former Tesla AI data labelers said they would not trust FSD to drive them.

3. **Tesla's marketing amplifying the risk:** Lambert details a pattern of Tesla's official X account and Elon Musk framing FSD as a substitute for an attentive driver. Specific examples cited: Tesla called FSD "your personal chauffeur" and said it "gives back your freedom" and "takes the stress out of driving." Tesla amplified testimonials from a 71-year-old with failing eyesight, a 93-year-old driving to church, and a man born without arms — all framing FSD as providing independent mobility for people who cannot otherwise drive. Musk replied "yes" when asked if FSD allows texting depending on traffic context, despite texting while driving being illegal in nearly all 50 states and Tesla's own terms requiring full driver supervision. Musk also posted that "by V14.3, your car will feel like it is sentient" — which Lambert characterizes as a psychological prompt to over-trust the system, not a technical claim.

## Editorial Stance
Lambert argues Tesla is actively choosing to worsen the complacency problem through its marketing rather than address it, and calls on the company to strengthen driver monitoring, stop promoting FSD as a driver substitute, and be honest about the system's real limitations. He warns that when a complacent FSD driver misses a critical intervention, third parties on public roads bear the consequences without having consented to Tesla's beta test.

Notable quotes and data:
- "FSD v14 can travel a couple thousand miles between critical interventions" — ~30–40 hours of driving without needed input
- Drivers need "5 to 8 seconds to mentally reengage after an automated system hands control back" (cited psychological research)
- Tesla's official account: "FSD Supervised can give you back your freedom" and "takes the stress out of driving so you can enjoy going places"
- Musk on texting while using FSD: "Depending on context of surrounding traffic, yes"
- Musk: "by V14.3, your car will feel like it is sentient"
- Seven of nine former Tesla AI data labelers (per Reuters) said they would not trust FSD to drive them
- Lambert: "I wrote back in October 2024 that FSD was getting more dangerous as it got better. Now, a year and a half later, the system is dramatically more capable — and the complacency problem is dramatically worse."

articles.title: Why Elon Just Bought A LOT of Land & Robotaxi Fleet Developments ⚡️
articles.body:
This episode of Electrified, hosted by Dillon Loomis, covers a wide range of Tesla and broader tech developments including the stalled robotaxi expansion in Houston and Dallas, FSD 14.3 performance impressions, Tesla's European sales surge, the Terafab land acquisition in Texas, and competitive moves from BYD and OpenAI in autonomy and robotics. The core thesis is that while Tesla's supervised FSD is showing strong real-world performance globally, the unsupervised robotaxi rollout appears to be lagging expectations, creating a confounding near-term picture for the autonomy thesis.

## Robotaxi

1. **Texas Self-Certification and Official Registry:** Tesla officially self-certified its robotaxis as Level 4 under a new Texas law that went into effect last week, allowing continued robotaxi operations in the state. This is described as largely a formality and procedural change — no new capability was added. The Texas Motor Carrier website now lists Tesla's robotaxi service with 42 VINs registered across 42 rows. For comparison, Waymo has 619 VINs listed in Texas, and AVID has 317 VINs registered.

2. **Houston and Dallas Fleet Contraction:** On-the-ground reporters indicate the Houston robotaxi fleet has dropped from six operational vehicles down to two, a situation that has persisted for several weeks. In Dallas, Spencer reported being unable to get a robotaxi two days in a row, with the app showing "no rides available nearby" — indicating no vehicles operating in the fleet rather than high demand. Dillon Loomis noted he warned on April 18th (four days before the earnings call) that if the Houston and Dallas launches didn't scale beyond a few vehicles within weeks, they may have been timed for positive earnings momentum rather than genuine readiness.

3. **Cybercab World Cup Speculation and Caution:** Many are speculating Tesla will debut the Cybercab on the robotaxi network in Houston and/or Dallas around June 14th when World Cup games begin. However, Dillon Loomis cautions that Tesla has been historically cautious and is unlikely to rush a Cybercab debut for marketing exposure. Ashoke stated that "soon the Cybercab will be driving itself into Austin City reporting for duty," though Dillon notes "soon at Tesla has many different interpretations."

4. **Supervisor Hiring for New Robotaxi Cities:** Tesla currently has six job listings for a robotaxi fleet support supervisor in Palo Alto, Tampa, San Antonio, Orlando, San Francisco, and Miami. Three of those cities — Miami, Orlando, and Tampa — match three of the five cities Tesla is reportedly targeting for robotaxi service launch by the end of June 2026. The role involves ensuring vehicles are in excellent condition for 24/7 operations, including vehicle prep, inspections, and lot management.

5. **Dallas Facility Repurposed for Autonomous Vehicles:** A court document reveals Tesla is building a 51,000 sq ft EV sales, service, and delivery center in Grand Prairie, Texas (between Dallas and Fort Worth, near Interstate 20). A revised operational plan in the document states the facility will be used for charging, cleaning, repair, and general maintenance of Tesla-owned autonomous vehicles. This signals that Tesla's existing service center and gallery infrastructure is insufficient for planned robotaxi scale. The facility is currently under construction and will not be open in time for the World Cup.

6. **RobotaxiTracker Hiring Watch List Update:** The RobotaxiTracker.com hiring watch list now shows 41 entries, including 33 active listings of cities where Tesla is currently hiring for an AI safety operator role. Historical cities where Tesla previously hired for this role are still visible, suggesting those positions have been filled.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD 14.3 Real-World Performance — Positive Signals:** Multiple noteworthy FSD demonstrations have surfaced. Joe Anderson drove through all 48 contiguous US states plus DC on FSD version 14.3.2 — over 7,200 miles across 9 days — with FSD driving every mile. Tesla's official account congratulated him. Separately, a team drove coast-to-coast across Canada — over 3,700 miles on version 14.3 — with zero disengagements of any kind. The head of research at Silicon Data was quoted saying "self-driving has been quietly completely solved with steady daily improvements." A tester in Germany drove for almost an hour through villages, country roads, and highways with no issues. FSD has also gone viral in China with testers pushing extreme scenarios. Tesla's FSD is now approved in the Netherlands, Lithuania, and Estonia across the EU.

2. **FSD 14.3 Personal Experience — Mixed:** Dillon Loomis shares his own experience with 14.3, describing it as "very far from a banger" despite Elon's public praise. He reports persistent jittery behavior, micro-braking events that would make passengers uncomfortable, poor navigation in his area, and notably poor parking behavior — the car has parked in entirely different parking lots from the intended destination on multiple occasions. He attributes some of this to Tesla rewriting the compiler and runtime from the ground up, acknowledging a few steps back may be expected. He also notes that Elon's credibility for touting upcoming FSD improvements is "as low as it's ever been" in his view.

3. **Hardware 3 Version 14 Light Expected in June:** Dillon notes that hardware 3 owners should be expecting a "version 14 light" sometime in June 2026 if Tesla delivers on its timeline.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **European Sales Surge:** Tesla sales in Europe have surged significantly in May 2026, partly reflecting low year-ago comparables from the Model Y and Model 3 changeovers. Country-level data for May: Portugal up ~350% year-over-year (January–May up 58%, outpacing a 33% rise in all EV sales); Sweden up 71%; Denmark up 136% (Model Y was Denmark's best-selling vehicle in May); Spain up 113%; Norway up 29%; France up 655%. Giga Berlin is expanding output capacity, and a broader supervised FSD rollout across the EU later in 2026 is expected to further accelerate sales.

2. **Canada Chinese-Built EV Quota:** Tesla has already used approximately 12% of Canada's available quota for Chinese-built EVs in the first allocation window. Nearly all of the roughly 2,900 Chinese-built EVs imported so far are Model 3s from Giga Shanghai. The current quota window allows up to 24,500 Chinese-built EVs to be imported between program launch and August 31st, 2026.

3. **Tesla Semi Grapevine Test:** Covenant conducted a two-week real-world test of the Tesla Semi with a major California customer on the Grapevine route — described as one of the most demanding real-world routes for any truck due to steep grades, heavy load management, and heat. The driver reported being "amazed" at the Tesla Semi's performance and felt a level of confidence hard to match in a diesel truck. A summary from Covenant is described as coming soon.

4. **Graphite Supply Chain Update:** Australia's Syrah Resources announced Tesla has withdrawn a notice of intent to end their graphite supply deal, accepting that Syrah is now producing conforming samples. Tesla had originally issued a default notice in July 2025 citing conformity issues with active anode material samples from the Vidalia facility. Dillon flags the importance of securing anode material suppliers outside of China.

## Market & Competition

1. **BYD Autonomous Driving Liability Policy:** BYD announced a new policy offering comprehensive coverage for damages incurred while its "God's Eye" autonomous driving system is engaged. BYD will cover all losses with no cap for vehicle repairs, third-party property damage, and personal injury liabilities, and the policy will not raise the owner's regular commercial insurance for the following year. The policy is valid for one year. God's Eye is technically a Level 2 system. Dillon notes a precedent: when BYD introduced a similar guarantee for automatic parking in July 2025, usage jumped from ~21% to over 90%. He flags this as a signal that automakers will increasingly need to take liability for their autonomous systems.

2. **OpenAI Robotics Entering Humanoid Space:** Sam Altman announced OpenAI Robotics is now hiring to program and manufacture robots. OpenAI's stated near-term focus is on robots to support skilled workers building infrastructure; long-term vision is a personal robot for everyone. Dillon recaps the history: OpenAI invested in Figure in 2024 and partnered to develop AI models for Figure robots, but Figure ended that partnership roughly a year later after claiming a major in-house AI breakthrough. OpenAI has since been doing data collection and teleoperation work with hands but has not yet revealed a full humanoid prototype. In January 2026, OpenAI issued an RFP seeking humanoid manufacturing partners in the US for components like gearboxes, actuators, and motors. Dillon expects partnerships given OpenAI's lack of manufacturing experience and views this as a very long game over decades.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Terafab Land Acquisition Near Austin:** SE Robinson reported that Witt LLC — a purchasing entity sharing the physical address of XAI in Palo Alto — is buying over 3,100 acres in Grimes County, Texas (at the Gibbons Creek Reservoir), just over a two-hour drive from Giga Texas. A public hearing is scheduled for June 3rd, 2026, with SpaceX listed as the property owner for the tax abatement session. The project is described as a "multi-phase next-gen vertically integrated semiconductor manufacturing and advanced computing fab facility." Estimated capital investment for initial phases is $55 billion, with a total potential investment of $119 billion if additional phases are built. XAI's general counsel James Burnham has signed on behalf of Witt LLC. Dillon identifies this as the land for the Terafab, noting Elon uses tech entities tied to his companies to acquire land ahead of formal approvals, which are still pending.

2. **Macrohard and Digital Optimus Context:** Dillon briefly references Macrohard and "something like a digital Optimus" as potential internal uses for SpaceX's compute capacity (Colossus), noting that SpaceX retaining optionality to reallocate GPUs for internal Optimus-related projects represents asymmetric long-term upside.

Notable quotes and data:
- Tesla: 42 VINs registered for robotaxi service in Texas; Waymo: 619 VINs; AVID: 317 VINs
- Houston robotaxi fleet: down from 6 vehicles to 2, has been that way for "a few weeks"
- Dallas: "no rides available nearby" — two consecutive days with no operational vehicles
- FSD 14.3.2: 7,200+ miles across all 48 contiguous US states + DC, zero driver interventions
- FSD 14.3 Canada coast-to-coast: 3,700+ miles, zero disengagements
- Tesla sales May 2026: Portugal +350% YoY; France +655%; Denmark +136%; Spain +113%; Sweden +71%; Norway +29%
- Model Y: Denmark's best-selling vehicle in May 2026
- Canada Chinese EV quota: Tesla used ~12% (~2,900 vehicles, nearly all Model 3 from Giga Shanghai) of 24,500-vehicle allocation window ending August 31, 2026
- BYD God's Eye: automatic parking guarantee in July 2025 drove usage from ~21% to over 90%
- Terafab: 3,100+ acres in Grimes County, TX; $55B initial phase capex, up to $119B total
- SpaceX IPO context: only Facebook and Alibaba have been valued at $100B+ after their first day on US exchanges
- SpaceX direct share program: up to 5% of stock reserved for employees and select persons; not subject to lock-up restrictions
- Tesla stock closed at $415.88, down 4.57%; NDX up 0.6%; volume 19% below average
- RobotaxiTracker hiring watch list: 41 entries, 33 active AI safety operator listings
- Elon Musk on Anthropic/SpaceX Colossus deal: "Let's not get carried away. This is a short-term deal." — 180-day lease with 90-day mutual cancellation notice

articles.title: The iPhone Moment for Robots Just Happened
articles.body:
This video argues that humanoid robotics has reached its "iPhone moment" — a genuine technological inflection point where three converging S-curves (AI brain/VLA models, data flywheels, and rapidly cheapening actuator hardware) have finally made deployable, economically viable humanoid robots a reality. The host uses Figure AI's live-streamed warehouse robots (Bob, Frank, and Gary) as the defining demonstration of this shift, comparing it to the launch of the original iPhone on June 29th, 2007. The core thesis is that the $40 trillion annual global physical labor market is about to be disrupted, with near-term deployment filling genuine demographic labor vacancies, but a more disruptive and politically volatile middle wave arriving around 2030.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Figure AI's live warehouse demo as the inflection point:** Figure AI's three humanoid robots — Bob, Frank, and Gary (Figure 3 units) — have been running a publicly live-streamed, continuous warehouse mission at a facility in California since May 14th, sorting packages at human-parity speed, autonomously swapping out for battery charges, and operating end-to-end from camera pixels via neural network without teleoperation (except when errors occurred). The runtime counter had surpassed 60 hours at the time of recording. The host characterizes this as the most significant demo in technology history, comparable in significance to the original iPhone launch.

2. **Three converging S-curves making humanoids viable:** The host identifies three simultaneous technological breakthroughs. First, the "brain": Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models — a single neural network taking raw camera pixels plus natural language instructions plus body state and outputting continuous motor commands hundreds of times per second, with no hand-coded scripts. Jim Fan at NVIDIA leads a related project called Groot. Second, the "data flywheel": Tesla has been collecting real-world manipulation data inside factories with Optimus for 2 years and with its 9 million FSD vehicle fleet for longer; NVIDIA released a synthetic data generator called Cosmos running world simulations on gaming GPUs to produce robot training trajectories. Third, the "body": actuator costs have collapsed dramatically (detailed below).

3. **Actuator cost collapse enabling economics:** In 2020, a high-torque actuator (hip or knee joint) cost $2,000–$5,000 each at low volume, making the full actuator subsystem on a single robot $50,000–$100,000. By 2026, the same actuator runs $500–$2,000 at low volume. Morgan Stanley projects that at Tesla's target scale of 1 million units per year, actuator costs could fall to $100–$300 each — an order of magnitude reduction in 6 years. The Chinese EV supply chain (precision motor and gear manufacturers supplying BYD and others) is the key enabler of this commoditization.

4. **Humanoid pricing trajectory and competitive landscape:** Unitree (Chinese company) is currently selling a full humanoid for $13,500 — roughly the price of a used Honda Civic. Bank of America projects average humanoid material cost drops from approximately $35,000 today to $13,000–$17,000 by 2035. IDTechEx projects average selling price falls from $115,000 to $37,000 over the next four years. Tesla is targeting a $20,000 price point for Optimus at 1 million units, which it hopes to reach by around 2030.

5. **Current real-world humanoid deployments:** Multiple humanoid robots are already deployed in commercial settings. Figure 3 robots are working BMW's Spartanburg, South Carolina factory in the body shop, sheet metal placement, and weld inspection areas. Apollo robots (by a company called Electronics Robot/Apptronik per context) are deployed at Mercedes plants, Jabil electronics factories, and GXO logistics warehouses. Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid has crossed 100,000 totes moved at a GXO facility in Flowery Branch, Georgia. Tesla Optimus is in internal pilots at Fremont and Giga Texas, with mass production starting in summer 2026.

6. **Figure AI's production scaling and TAM:** Figure AI CEO Brett Adcock stated on X on April 23rd and in a Forbes interview that Figure's Bot Q manufacturing plant went from producing one robot per day to one robot per hour in approximately 4 months — a 24x scaling in 120 days. The plan for calendar year 2026 is north of 12,000 robots, with a long-term goal of 1 million robots per year. Adcock's total addressable market estimate is roughly half of global GDP, approximately $50 trillion per year.

7. **Tesla Optimus production targets:** Tesla has stated a goal of reaching 1 million Optimus units per year (timeframe approximately 2030). The host notes Tesla recorded production in March 2026 and aimed to 3x that by May 2026.

8. **The demographic vacancy argument (Wave 1):** The host argues the initial wave of humanoid deployment is not displacing workers who want jobs — it is filling vacancies that already exist due to demographic collapse. Amazon warehouse turnover runs 100–150% per year; one in three new fulfillment hires quits within 90 days; a New Jersey study clocked Amazon warehouse turnover at 124% vs. 72% for comparable non-Amazon warehouses. The U.S. trucking industry is short 60,000–82,000 drivers, projected to reach 160,000 by 2028, with annual driver turnover at large carriers of 90–95%. Manpower Group's 2026 survey shows 84% of Japanese employers and 83% of German employers cannot find workers to hire. Japan's elder care sector has a job-to-applicant ratio of 3.9:1 and is projected to be short 570,000 care workers by 2040.

9. **The disruptive middle wave (Wave 2, ~2030):** Around 2030, the host warns humanoids will begin displacing jobs humans actually want: fast food prep, non-high-turnover warehouse roles, light manufacturing, hotel housekeeping, big box retail stocking, construction framing, and agricultural harvesting. In the U.S. alone, he estimates roughly 10 million workers in directly automatable physical labor categories (approximately 7 million material movers at $30,000 median wage, 2 million assemblers at $44,000, 2 million in related roles at $37,000). He explicitly worries about a scenario where cost curves run faster than government response, potentially producing 20 million laid-off material handlers within 3 years and violent political backlash.

10. **The systemic flywheel thesis:** The host argues humanoid robots are not a standalone industry but the physical manufacturing endpoint of a single integrated flywheel encompassing AI, batteries, EVs, data centers, and manufacturing AI itself. Tesla builds Optimus in a factory already producing 2 million cars per year using the same AI infrastructure as FSD and feeding into Grok. Figure uses actuators from the same Chinese supply chain as EVs and residential batteries. NVIDIA's Cosmos generates humanoid training data on the same GPUs training LLMs. The flywheel cannot be stopped without abandoning AI, batteries, EVs, or domestic manufacturing competitiveness — all politically untouchable.

11. **Political and regulatory disruption as the real near-term battleground:** Unlike the iPhone's indirect, invisible labor displacement over a decade, humanoid displacement is visible — robots have name tags and are on live streams. The host predicts the political response will be driven by optics before economics, resulting in deployment bans, component tariffs, union carveouts, and city/state/country-level regulatory fragmentation. He frames the countries that get the regulatory balance right as capturing a structural multi-trillion dollar productivity advantage that others cannot recover from within the century.

## Market & Competition

1. **$40 trillion physical labor market as the disruption target:** The host estimates the total annual value of global human physical labor at approximately $40 trillion — roughly one-third of the entire global economy and ten times the size of the market created by the iPhone ($4 trillion per year). This is the market humanoid robots are positioned to disrupt.

2. **China's supply chain advantage:** The Chinese EV supply chain — precision motor and gear manufacturers serving BYD and thousands of other Chinese EV makers — is directly enabling humanoid actuator commoditization. Unitree's $13,500 full humanoid is cited as a product of this supply chain maturity. The host identifies this as a geopolitical and industrial competition dimension, noting that restricting humanoid deployment means ceding ground to China across EVs, batteries, and manufacturing simultaneously.

Notable quotes and data:
- "We had record production in March and we're going to try to 3x that by May. We want to be able to get to a million units a year." — Tesla on Optimus production
- Figure AI production: 1 robot/day → 1 robot/hour in ~4 months (24x scaling in 120 days), per Brett Adcock
- Figure AI 2026 target: north of 12,000 robots
- Actuator cost: $2,000–$5,000 (2020) → $500–$2,000 (2026 low volume) → $100–$300 (Morgan Stanley estimate at Tesla's 1M unit/year scale)
- Unitree full humanoid: $13,500 currently available
- Bank of America: average humanoid material cost from ~$35,000 today → $13,000–$17,000 by 2035
- IDTechEx: average selling price from $115,000 → $37,000 over next four years
- Tesla Optimus price target: $20,000 at 1 million units (~2030)
- U.S. trucking driver shortage: 60,000–82,000 now, projected 160,000 by 2028; 90–95% annual turnover at large carriers
- Amazon warehouse turnover: 100–150% per year; 124% per New Jersey study vs. 72% for comparable non-Amazon warehouses
- Japan: 84% of employers can't find workers (Manpower Group 2026); elder care job-to-applicant ratio 3.9:1; projected 570,000 care worker shortage by 2040; 29% of population over 65, 1 in 5 over 75
- Germany: 83% of employers can't find workers; crossed demographic threshold in 2026 where retirees outnumber new labor force entrants
- Agility Robotics' Digit: 100,000+ totes moved at GXO Flowery Branch, Georgia
- Effective robot operating cost estimate: ~$2/hour
- Brett Adcock TAM estimate: ~$50 trillion/year (half of global GDP)
- Figure AI live stream launched: May 14th (2026)
- "The market it disrupts is not 4 trillion a year. It is 40 trillion a year."
- "The political response to the optics will arrive before the political response to the economics."

articles.title: CLIFF DIVING AGAIN?!? GPS madness masked as AP/FSD Failures. 16 Hot News Items to start your week
articles.body:
This June 1st livestream from FutureAzA covers approximately 20 news items spanning Tesla safety incidents, FSD/Autopilot misreporting, regulatory developments, EV adoption trends, battery durability, and competitor news. The host's core argument is that mainstream media systematically misrepresents Tesla's driver-assistance systems — conflating Autopilot with FSD, amplifying cherry-picked negative data from label workers, and ignoring the broader safety record — while Tesla vehicles continue to demonstrate exceptional structural safety and long-term reliability. The session concludes with an extended Q&A covering Model Y purchasing advice, battery health data, and general EV ownership topics.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Tesla Model 3 survives 300-ft cliff plunge in Malibu:** A Model 3 plunged roughly 300 feet off a cliff on Mulholland Highway in Malibu on a Friday morning, with occupants surviving. The host attributes this to the Model 3's NHTSA five-star overall rating in every category and subcategory, and its record as having the lowest probability of injury of any car ever evaluated by the US New Car Assessment Program. The absence of a traditional engine provides additional crumple zone, and the rigid occupant cell structure is credited for the outcome.

2. **87-year-old driver dies after Tesla enters pond — Autopilot misreported as FSD:** In Tampa, an 87-year-old man driving a Model Y veered off the road, struck an electrical box, and drove into a pond while Autopilot was engaged. The host emphasizes that Autopilot (lane-keep assistance) is categorically different from Full Self-Driving, and that the vehicle's speed — sufficient to break through an electrical pole and still reach the pond in what he describes as a 30–35 mph zone — points strongly to human error rather than a system failure. The host criticizes media coverage that uses incidents like this to discourage adoption of what he calls demonstrably the safest driving system in the world.

3. **Reuters "fake FSD" story dismissed as misinformation:** A Reuters report claimed Tesla staff admitted to selling fake self-driving with fake numbers, citing workers at a Utah office who label video footage of crashes, near-misses with children, and animal strikes. The host argues these data labelers are deliberately shown only the most traumatic edge-case footage — perhaps 10 miles of bad driving per day — while Tesla's fleet is accumulating roughly 30 million miles of good driving daily. He notes that at 10 billion supervised FSD miles driven, the catastrophic death toll that critics imply would exist has simply not materialized, and he calls the Reuters framing deliberately misleading.

4. **Tesla owner repeatedly uses Autopilot from back seat:** A news story profiled a man who has been arrested multiple times for riding in the back seat while Autopilot is engaged. The host strongly discourages this behavior. He also notes the article falsely cited two men killed in Texas while sitting in back and passenger seats of an Autopilot-engaged Tesla — which he identifies as being the unrelated story of intoxicated occupants who crashed into a tree, calling the article "pure slop."

5. **Estonia becomes third European country to clear self-driving on public roads:** Estonia has approved self-driving vehicle operation on its roads, joining the Netherlands and Lithuania. The host notes that while this is technically classified as Level 2 driver assistance under SAE levels, he argues the SAE framework is essentially meaningless — designed before the systems existed, it lumps mild lane-keep through Full Self-Driving into the same band. Drivers remain legally responsible. Other European countries are expected to follow.

6. **Supervised FSD surpasses 10 billion miles:** The host references that Tesla's supervised Full Self-Driving has surpassed the 10 billion mile mark, and that the fleet is now accumulating approximately 30 million miles per day.

## Robotaxi

1. **Waymo's new robotaxi uses Chinese-built Zeekr vehicle, now accepting riders:** Waymo's newest robotaxi — described as the Zeekr (referred to in the transcript as the "Zeer" / "Ohigh") — is Chinese-manufactured and is now operating in California and expanding to more riders and cities. The host notes the interior is intentionally sparse and easy to clean, which he considers appropriate. However, he argues the economics are unfavorable: if the base vehicle costs $35,000, the 100% import tariff effectively doubles it to $70,000. He contends that for Waymo's robotaxi to compete economically with a Tesla Cybercab — which he says requires less cleaning, less energy, and less maintenance — the Chinese van would need to cost around $12,000 after tariffs, a price he says it will never reach even before sensor integration costs.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **72% of new EV buyers traded in a gas car despite losing the $7,500 tax credit:** EV trade-ins as a share of new EV purchases rose from 67% in January 2026 to 72% by April 2026. The host interprets this as evidence that EV adoption is expanding beyond early adopters into the broader market. Analysts cited high interest rates and more expensive gasoline as contextual factors.

2. **Model 3 reaches 360,000 miles — battery replaced at 321,000 miles for $5,000:** A Model 3 owner hit 360,000 miles, replacing the battery at 321,000 miles. A reconditioned pack cost approximately $5,000, well below the $15,000–$22,000 range for a new battery replacement. The host notes this is exceptional longevity compared to traditional vehicles, and that the original motors remain functional.

3. **Model Y with 111,000 miles retains 90–92% battery capacity despite near-total DC fast charging:** A pre-refresh Model Y at 111,000 miles had received only 36 kWh of charging from AC sources — virtually all charging was DC fast charging — yet retains 90–92% of original range capacity. The host calls the persistent narrative about fast charging destroying EV batteries "ludicrous."

4. **FSD praised by mainstream automotive press:** The host cites a piece describing Tesla's supervised Full Self-Driving as technology that "felt like sci-fi 10 years ago," with a new owner who bought a Model Y after his son recommended it, calling it "the most impressively engineered consumer product since forever." Features highlighted include voice control, Grok integration (available with the spring update), self-parking, summon, collision avoidance, and home charging convenience.

5. **Ford Escape to return as all-electric vehicle in 2029:** Ford is reportedly planning to revive the Escape nameplate as a fully electric vehicle after ending production following the 2026 model year. The host notes a parallel with the Mustang Mach-E strategy of using established nameplates to introduce new technology, though he expresses skepticism about Ford's EV execution. He also notes a Ford Explorer electric exists in Europe but is built by Volkswagen.

6. **AC Cobra electric supercar — host correction:** The host initially reported on an electric AC Cobra supercar before discovering mid-segment that the vehicle may not actually have an electric version, acknowledging the error on air.

## Market & Competition

1. **BYD charges to 97% in 12 minutes even in freezing cold:** BYD's Denza Z9 GT, powered by the second-generation Blade battery, can charge from 10% to 70% in 5 minutes and 10% to 97% in under 10 minutes in ideal conditions — now demonstrated at 12 minutes in freezing temperatures. The host notes these batteries are not available in the US due to import tariffs (cited at approximately 30% for batteries) and export restrictions on equipment to manufacture cutting-edge LFP cells, meaning US LFP factories are using older designs.

2. **Toyota cancels next-generation EV development:** Toyota announced it will cancel development of the LFZ electric sedan under the Lexus brand, reallocating management resources to SUVs. The host frames this as consistent with Toyota's stated "multi-pathway" strategy — gas, hybrid, EV, and hydrogen — which he argues amounts to committing fully to nothing.

3. **Ferrari's new Purosangue-successor criticized by chairman and Italy's deputy PM:** Ferrari's new electric vehicle (referred to as the "luche") drew criticism from Ferrari's former chairman and Italy's deputy prime minister, sending the stock down 8%. The host notes it has a larger battery than a Cybertruck but shorter range than a Cybertruck, and appears designed to compete with Chinese EVs rather than as a traditional Ferrari performance product.

4. **Xiaomi losing $5,600 per car sold; Chinese EV gross margins declining:** Xiaomi (called "Shia" in the transcript), the phone-maker-turned-EV-manufacturer praised by Ford CEO Jim Farley, is losing $5,600 per vehicle. Gross margins for EVs in the broader Chinese market fell from 23.2% to 20.1%. The host pushes back on the narrative that China is simply dumping subsidized cars, noting that a subsidy of $10,000 per car across ~33 million annual sales would amount to over three years of a trillion dollars — a figure he calls implausible.

5. **Vinfast's US factory promise collapses:** Vinfast made promises about building a US factory, went through embassy vetting, but never completed the facility, instead building plants in Indonesia and India. The host expects efforts to claw back committed funds will fail.

6. **GM wins NASA contract to build battery for Moon-bound vehicle:** GM has been awarded a NASA contract to build a battery for a lunar vehicle. The host notes GM is not building the lunar buggy itself — that contract went to Astrolab and Lunar Outpost at $220 million each — and jokes about GM's track record with battery fires.

7. **DC converting streetlights into EV chargers using Dieselgate settlement funds:** Washington DC is using existing light poles — which have surplus electrical capacity after switching from high-wattage sodium lamps to low-wattage LEDs — to install EV charging equipment funded by Dieselgate penalty money. Companies like Shell Recharge and BP have equipment that fits inside or onto the poles. The host estimates these would deliver charging speeds roughly between Level 1 and Level 2, suitable for street parking in dense urban areas.

8. **Tesla stock snapshot (as of June 1, 2026):** Down approximately 3% on the day, down approximately 2.5% over five days, up approximately 7% for the month, down slightly over six months, down slightly year-to-date, significantly up on one-year and five-year timeframes.

## Energy

1. **Tesla patents self-cleaning camera lens with built-in eyelid wiper:** Tesla filed a patent for a self-cleaning camera lens featuring a built-in wiper mechanism described as functioning like an eyelid. The host notes most patents never reach production but calls it a more elegant solution than fluid-spray approaches used by others, or the high-speed spinning lens approach used by some competitors.

Notable quotes and data:
- "10 billion miles" — supervised Full Self-Driving cumulative miles surpassed
- "~30 million miles per day" — current Tesla FSD fleet daily mileage accumulation
- 300 ft — cliff drop survived by Model 3 in Malibu
- Model 3: lowest probability of injury of any car ever evaluated by NHTSA's New Car Assessment Program, five-star rating in every category and subcategory
- 67% → 72% — share of new EV buyers trading in a gas car, January to April 2026
- 360,000 miles on one Model 3; battery replaced at 321,000 miles for ~$5,000 (reconditioned pack); full replacement would cost $15,000–$22,000
- Model Y at 111,000 miles: only 36 kWh from AC charging, rest DC fast charging; retains 90–92% range capacity
- Waymo Zeekr robotaxi: ~$35,000 base vehicle cost → ~$70,000 after 100% import tariff; Cybercab would need to cost ~$12,000 to match
- BYD Denza Z9 GT: 10–97% charge in 12 minutes in freezing conditions; 10–70% in 5 minutes in ideal conditions
- Xiaomi losing $5,600 per EV sold; Chinese EV gross margins fell from 23.2% to 20.1%
- Astrolab and Lunar Outpost each received $220 million NASA contracts for lunar buggy
- Estonia is the third European country (after Netherlands and Lithuania) to clear self-driving for public road use
- Ford Escape expected to return as all-electric in 2029, following end of current production after model year 2026
- Toyota canceling LFZ Lexus electric sedan development
- Ferrari new EV: battery larger than Cybertruck, range shorter than Cybertruck, stock down 8%
- "It will be quite a niche thing in 10 years to actually be driving your own car" — attributed to Elon Musk
- Model Y battery health from viewer: 81% at 123,000 miles (host notes progression: 83% at 90k, 86% at 60k — implying decline with age as expected)

articles.title: Bears And Bulls Are Now Calling For a Stock Market Sell OFF And Tesla Is Ready To Run.
articles.body:
This video from "investingagainstthegrain" covers three main topics: a macro market analysis arguing against imminent crash predictions, a commentary on AI job displacement narratives from OpenAI and Anthropic CEOs, and a bullish Tesla thesis centered on Cybercab production ramp and Texas Level 4 authorization. The host's core argument is that popular bearish indicators are largely noise, momentum signals remain constructive, and Tesla is uniquely positioned to hit all-time highs driven by its robotaxi buildout.

## Market & Competition

1. **Dismissing Common Bear Indicators as Noise:** The host systematically argues that the Buffett Indicator (currently at 237%), the CAPE/Shiller ratio (currently at 42.7, second only to the dot-com bubble), and record margin debt ($1.3 trillion) are unreliable signals because they fail to account for globalized corporate profits (~40% from overseas), productivity and technology advances, and the natural scaling of nominal figures over time. He characterizes these as click-bait headlines rather than actionable indicators.

2. **The Inverted Yield Curve as the One Legitimate Signal:** The host identifies the 10-year/2-year Treasury yield inversion as the only macro indicator he takes seriously, noting it has predicted every recession since the 1950s. He cautions it is imperfect — during the Great Recession, the curve inverted at end-2006 but the market didn't peak until approximately 18 months later in late 2007. Currently, the 2-year yield sits at approximately 4% and the 10-year at approximately 4.45%, which he describes as healthy and non-inverted.

3. **BX Trender Monthly Momentum as Primary Decision Tool:** The host relies heavily on a proprietary momentum indicator called the "BX Trender" on monthly timeframes to guide his portfolio decisions. He walks through historical examples: it correctly signaled exits at S&P 4,778 in January 2022 (avoiding a drop to ~3,200–3,300), during COVID (from ~3,382), and in October 2007 (~1,600, avoiding a 60%+ drop during the Great Recession). As of the end of May 2026, the monthly BX Trender has closed green, following a light-red April (higher low vs. dark-red March), which he reads as a bullish continuation signal.

4. **S&P 500 Forward P/E and Contrarian Consumer Sentiment:** The host notes the S&P 500 forward P/E peaked around 23x in 2025 but has since compressed to approximately 20–21x due to strong earnings from companies like Micron, Nvidia, and others — suggesting the market is actually less overvalued now than a year ago. He also cites consumer sentiment at all-time lows as a contrarian bullish signal: historically, when sentiment is in the bottom 3%, the S&P has returned nearly 20%, versus only ~2.2% when sentiment is in the top 3%. The Fear & Greed Index is currently at 60 (greed), which he characterizes as normal rather than euphoric.

5. **Tom Lee's 20% Selloff Warning and the Host's Rebuttal:** The host references bull analyst Tom Lee as now calling for a 20% market selloff, and uses this as a framing device to explore whether current signals justify concern. His conclusion is that with no yield curve inversion, a green monthly BX Trender, a compressed S&P forward P/E, and low consumer sentiment (a contrarian positive), the market is in good shape heading into the second half of 2026.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Texas Level 4 Self-Certification — A Pivotal Regulatory Milestone:** The host highlights a development reported by James Stephenson on May 29, 2026 (Thursday relative to the recording date of May 31, 2026): Tesla has been authorized by the state of Texas to operate driverless vehicles commercially under a new law that took effect May 28, 2026. Tesla self-certified the software running on its robotaxi as Level 4. The host characterizes this as potentially the key regulatory hurdle Tesla had been waiting for before deploying Cybercabs commercially.

2. **Cybercabs Driving Themselves Off the Production Line:** The host references Elon Musk reposting a video of Cybercabs driving themselves off the production line to parking lots — a signal he interprets as the Cybercab being close to feature-complete and ready for operational deployment. He notes this is distinct from similar demonstrations previously done with Model Y vehicles. He also references a statement from Tesla's head of AI ("Shockwami" — likely a transcription of a name) saying Cybercabs will soon be rolling off the line and heading to work in Austin.

## Robotaxi

1. **Cybercab Physical Deployment Signals Across Multiple Cities:** The host references Joe Tegtmeyer's videos documenting Cybercab production volume and deployment spread. He notes Cybercabs are appearing in Dallas, Houston, Pennsylvania, and that dealership lots in some cities are clearing space and positioning black-and-red Model Y vehicles labeled as "Cybercab Plus" or "Robotaxi Plus." He interprets this geographic spread and physical presence as Tesla preparing for an imminent large-scale rollout.

2. **Robotaxi Tracker Crowd-Sourced Data Cautioned Against Over-Indexing:** The host acknowledges that some observers are pointing to the robotaxi tracker showing declining numbers and using that as a bearish signal. He dismisses this, arguing that crowd-sourced data is inherently incomplete and that the physical production and deployment evidence is more telling than tracker counts.

3. **FSD Version Referenced as Impressive:** The host briefly mentions using "14.3" (a version of FSD), calling it "amazing," as additional evidence that the software side is progressing in parallel with the hardware rollout.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Tesla Stock at Its Highest-Ever Level for This Time of Year:** With Tesla trading at approximately $437, the host points out this is the highest Tesla has ever been at this point in the calendar year — noting that in the same period last year the stock was around $200–$300, and the year before that, around $100. He frames this as historically unprecedented seasonal strength, supporting his thesis that all-time highs are imminent.

## Market & Competition (AI/Jobs Narrative)

1. **Sam Altman and Dario Amodei Walking Back AI Job Apocalypse Claims:** The host highlights a Fortune article reporting that both Sam Altman (OpenAI) and Dario Amodei (Anthropic) are walking back their earlier AI jobs apocalypse predictions ahead of anticipated blockbuster IPOs. The host claims he has been saying since 2024 that the doomsday AI job displacement narrative was primarily a capital-raising marketing strategy — designed to generate hype and attract venture capital in private markets rather than reflect ground-level reality.

2. **AI Increases Productivity But Is Not Replacing Jobs — Autonomy Will:** The host draws a distinction between AI improving worker efficiency (one person doing more) versus actually replacing jobs. He argues the true job displacement vector will be autonomous vehicles and robotaxis — not generative or agentic AI. He cites the continued aggressive hiring of software engineers at Nvidia, Anthropic, and OpenAI as evidence that AI is not displacing the very jobs its proponents claim it will eliminate within 12 months.

Notable quotes and data:

articles.body:
In this June 1, 2026 livestream, Jo Bhakdi covers three rapid headlines: Tesla's stock sliding on the day, a sharp deterioration in Anthropic's Claude AI model (specifically Claude 4.8/Opus 4.8), and Nvidia's strong performance following its Computex laptop announcement. The video's core thesis is that Tesla's slide is a normal technical pullback within an ongoing uptrend, and that June 2026 is a potentially transformative month due to imminent Cybercab deployment catalysts, the FIFA World Cup, and Tesla's self-imposed deadline to unlock multiple cities before H2 2026.

## Robotaxi

1. **Cybercab deployment prediction for June 2026:** Bhakdi predicts that June will see "multiple dozens" of unsupervised Cybercabs deployed across multiple cities — what he describes as a "first mini scale" launch. He cites widespread sightings of Cybercabs in Dallas, ongoing Tesla hiring for robotaxi operators, remote operators, and operational maintenance roles across multiple cities, and the near-attainment of what he calls a "critical mass" of approximately 1,000 Cybercabs produced and deployed.

2. **Tesla's Q4 earnings commitment as a hard deadline:** Bhakdi references Tesla's Q4 2025 earnings deck, in which the company — including the CFO — stated that multiple cities would be unlocked before the second half of 2026. With roughly 30 days remaining before that deadline as of June 1, 2026, Bhakdi argues Tesla is unlikely to embarrass itself by missing a commitment made at the corporate level, not just by Elon Musk personally.

3. **World Cup timing as a launch opportunity:** The FIFA World Cup kicks off in Dallas, Texas on June 14, 2026. Bhakdi views this as a prime marketing and deployment opportunity for Tesla's Cybercab, noting that dozens of Cybercabs have already been spotted in Dallas and that the event brings enormous global attention to the Dallas–Texas market.

4. **Unsupervised fleet stagnation noted:** A commenter in the live chat notes that there has not been a single new unsupervised Cybercab addition since May 9, 2026 — a point Bhakdi acknowledges as a reason for the current stock slide, while arguing that a surprise expansion is imminent based on circumstantial signals.

5. **Rough concurrent fleet figures cited in chat:** A chat commenter ("Miss Mark") mentions that Tesla launched with approximately 8 concurrent 24/7 Cybercabs and is now closer to 13–15 running around the clock. Bhakdi does not dispute this but notes he initially misread the comment as referring to a June 2, 2026 launch.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus progress over announcements:** In response to a chat comment suggesting Tesla needs to stop hiding Optimus progress in the face of OpenAI's humanoid robot announcements, Bhakdi disagrees, arguing it is more important that Tesla actually complete Optimus development than talk about it publicly. He views the silence as discipline rather than weakness.

## Market & Competition

1. **Nvidia's Blackwell laptop announcement as a TAM-doubling event:** Bhakdi views Nvidia's Computex announcement — launching RTX Spark Blackwell GPUs (with 6,144 CUDA cores) with NVLink into laptops and desktops in partnership with Microsoft — as a strategic expansion beyond AI data centers into edge computing for consumers. He argues this effectively doubles the total addressable market for personal computing, as average laptop prices could rise from roughly $900 to $2,000–$2,500, with approximately 50–90% of that price differential accruing to Nvidia due to chip costs.

2. **Claude 4.8 (Opus 4.8) described as a catastrophic regression:** Bhakdi, a self-described longtime Claude advocate, says the model has undergone a complete collapse in English writing quality, logical reasoning, and design capabilities over the prior two days. He quotes multiple X users including himself echoing the same experience, comparing it to "ChatGPT 3-level" output. He highlights that enterprises reportedly spend up to $500 million per month on Anthropic tokens, making a capability regression of this scale potentially very costly for large customers. He announces he is switching to ChatGPT in the interim.

3. **Apple faces existential pressure from Nvidia–Microsoft PC push:** Bhakdi argues Apple has no viable custom silicon response to the Nvidia Blackwell laptop platform and must partner with Nvidia or risk rapid irrelevance in the AI PC era. He believes Apple will ultimately announce something with Nvidia but needs to move quickly.

4. **Tesla stock technical analysis:** Bhakdi identifies a rising support trendline connecting lows at $343 (April 8, 2026), $372, and $404, projecting the next bounce level at approximately $420. On the day of recording, Tesla is down approximately 3.9%, and Bhakdi's leveraged portfolio is down roughly 5–6%, partially offset by his 4x-over-core Nvidia position. He states he is break-even on short puts down to the $415 level.

Notable quotes and data:

## Executive Summary
Today's posts center on Tesla's expanding Cybercab testing footprint (now reaching Pennsylvania), a strong FSD endorsement from a credentialed engineering professor, and a Tesla vehicle safety highlight. This carries above-average credibility given Marks' stated technical background, and serves as a qualitative signal of FSD's continued improvement in real-world perception among technically sophisticated users.

Sawyer Merritt used this incident to reinforce Tesla's safety narrative. This is a SpaceX/Starlink update with limited direct Tesla investment relevance, though Starlink's scale and cadence is occasionally cited as context for Elon Musk's operational bandwidth and resource allocation.

articles.body:

## Brief

- Texas Level 4 self-certification live; Ashok signals Cybercab "reporting for duty" in Austin imminently.
- FSD daily miles hit 26.7M/day — up 44% in one month per Morgan Stanley.
- Reuters: Tesla's "10x safer" FSD claim inflates true ratio ~3x; NHTSA has 4 open investigations.

- Optimus factory steel erection begun at Giga Texas; Fremont pilot line visible.
- China FSD fraud trial opens; 1M+ HW3 vehicles face triple-damage exposure.
- Musk pay "change in control" clause waives all operational milestones upon a merger.

---

## Robotaxi

- **Texas Level 4 authorization is the week's structural unlock.** New Texas law took effect May 28–30, allowing manufacturer self-certification for driverless commercial operation. Tesla certified Cybercab as Level 4 on day one — the regulatory gate bears had called years away is now cleared. Tesla simultaneously pre-staged Cybercabs at hubs in all three Texas cities the same week.

- **Ashok Elluswamy's "reporting for duty" post is the clearest internal signal yet.** Tesla's head of AI quote-tweeted Musk's factory self-drive video (15M views) and stated Cybercab would soon "drive itself into Austin city, reporting for duty." The brighterwithherbert analysis: because Ashok controls FSD version, safety data, and route validation, "soon" implies real-world weeks, not months. The ~20-mile public-road drive from Giga Texas to Austin would let the fleet grow itself without human transport drivers.

- **June 30 city-launch deadline is a hard IR commitment, not a Musk tweet.** Tesla's Q4 2024 investor relations document committed to robotaxi coverage in Las Vegas, Tampa, Orlando, Miami, and Phoenix by June 30, 2026. Nationwide AI safety operator hiring across 15+ states simultaneously (per Tesla Yoda, May 27) reads as an operational pre-launch signal with roughly 30 days left on the clock.

- **Cybercab production running ~30–36 units/day per Bhakdi**, citing Tegtmeyer drone footage — implying roughly 1,000 units/month. Starlink Mini units confirmed on Cybercabs in Austin and Houston, providing redundant connectivity for dead zones and fleet-scale OTA updates. All three Giga Texas production lines (Model Y, Cybertruck, Cybercab) confirmed running simultaneously for the first time in six to eight months.

- **Staged ≠ deployed; real gaps remain.** Staged Cybercabs still have steering wheels attached. RobotaxiTracker.com shows no growth in the unsupervised count for the full week. Bhakdi estimates ~1,000 Cybercabs produced to date but acknowledges his prior April–May target of 1,800 unsupervised units was missed by roughly a year. The repricing threshold he cites begins above 1,000 deployed unsupervised units — not staged.

---

## Autonomous Driving

- **FSD daily miles hit 26.7M/day, up 44% month-over-month**, per Morgan Stanley's May note — from 18.5M/day in April. The metric is Morgan Stanley's explicit proxy for subscriber growth and engagement, and drew the highest investor engagement of the week.

- **European mutual recognition is now a copy-paste process.** Lithuania approved supervised FSD in under 40 days by leveraging the Netherlands' 18-month, 1.12M-mile evaluation; Greece is next via the same mechanism. FSD Supervised is now confirmed in three European countries, with Czech Republic, Slovenia, and Austria preparing for unsupervised approval. Combined Netherlands + Lithuania FSD mileage hit 12.5M miles, with ~3M added in under 72 hours.

- **FSD 14.5 and 14.6 confirmed in internal testing.** FSD V14 Light — delivering all V14 features to HW3 vehicles — is targeted for late June 2026 per Ashok's Q1 earnings commentary. A reasoning model is already running in FSD V14.x on production vehicles, per Ashok's October 2025 ICCV paper. A transcontinental zero-intervention Canada drive completed at 3,760 miles — the first on record.

- **Grok Build actively accelerating FSD and Cybercab development.** Tesla AI VP Yantasai confirmed Grok Build is in active use for both programs; Tesla AI engineers have effectively unlimited token access within the Musk ecosystem's compute stack. Separately, thin-barrier detection (tape or chains across a parking lot entrance) remains an open edge case, flagged via repeated employee testing in Austin.

---

## Optimus

- **Giga Texas Optimus factory has entered steel erection phase.** Beams and columns are being staged at the North Campus site, which targets at least 10M units/year across two phases — Phase 2 reclaiming an adjacent mining site to nearly double the footprint. A realistic production-ready estimate from on-site observers is end of 2027 or 2028, not 2026.

- **Fremont pilot production line is further along than public disclosures suggested.** Footage from the Model S/X Signature Edition event showed manufacturing cells, some enclosed in glass (indicating automated steps), with workers present. Lars Moravy confirmed the Model S/X discontinuation and Optimus line conversion were explicitly linked decisions. Bhakdi expects a V3 reveal in approximately 4–6 weeks (late June–early August); Elon's April 22 earnings call placed it ~90 days out.

- **Macrohard (Digital Optimus) disclosed in the SpaceX S-1**, described as a joint Tesla-SpaceX agentic AI replicating computer-based human work via vision rather than APIs. Elon targets a product launch by end of 2026. Ashok is confirmed lead engineer; his ICCV paper states the same video generation models powering FSD "also work for Optimus robots navigating the Tesla Gigafactory" — shared AI stack confirmed in writing.

- **Cortex 2 partially operational since April; full capacity targeted end of summer/fall 2026.** Roughly half capacity is live, training both FSD and Optimus. Approximately 130 Megapacks installed at Cortex 2 today; ~400 planned across all Giga Texas sites.

---

## Energy

- **SpaceX purchased ~$500M in Megapacks from Tesla in 2025**, up from ~$200M in 2024 — driven by AI data center power stabilization. Meta is confirmed as an additional Megapack customer for Wyoming AI data centers ($200M order). Tesla's Megapack is cementing a position as critical AI infrastructure.

- **Megapack 3 Belgium deployment: 180 units, 700 MWh, >$116M**, on the site of a former power plant; grid connection scheduled November 2026, commissioning by end of 2027 — one of the first large-scale Megapack 3 deployments in Europe.

- **Limondale BESS in Australia coming online: 144 Megapacks, $145M**, configured for 100 MW charge / 50 MW discharge. Tesla Energy vertical integration expanding simultaneously: Corpus Christi lithium refinery Line 1 running 24/7, Line 2 equipment arriving; cathode plant at Giga Texas receiving new equipment; 4680 area has active permit filings and new equipment installation underway.

---

## Electric Vehicles

- **Lower-cost Cybertruck ($59,990 Dual-Motor AWD) VINs assigned; deliveries mid-to-late June 2026.** Joe Tegtmeyer describes demand as "pretty big." Q1 2026 Cybertruck sales were 4,186 units, down from ~7,000 in Q1 2025 — the original $39K price promise vs. ~$95K launch price cited as the primary demand suppressor.

- **Tesla Europe April 2026: +46.5% YoY, 10,654 units** (EU-only growth exceeded 67%) — third consecutive month of YoY growth following +84% in March. YTD EU/EFTA/UK: 89,429 units, +45.8%. France and Spain reportedly at record highs.

- **Tesla Roadster confirmed for Giga Texas production** per Lars Moravy on the Ride the Lightning podcast; alpha prototypes in testing. Elon's framing from Q1 earnings: "Long-term, the only manually driven car will be the new Tesla Roadster" — positioning it as the last great driver's car, not a performance halo.

- **Model S/X final production completed** with a Giga Texas sendoff event. Lifetime sales: 755,000 units (400K Model S, 355K Model X).

---

## Financials

- **Piper Sandler 17-business DCF yields ~$400/share, excluding Optimus and distributed inference.** At ~$450s, the market is effectively pricing Optimus at zero. Robotaxi becomes ~45% of Tesla revenue and roughly half of gross profit by 2045 in the model; FSD licensing modeled at ~$400B revenue by 2045. Potter's conservatism is explicitly regulatory, not technical: "You can't see second place with a telescope."

- **Musk pay "change in control" clause waives all operational milestones upon merger.** Electrek analysis flags that the 2025 performance stock agreement language states "the Operational Milestones shall be disregarded" upon a buyout — meaning targets including 1 million commercial robotaxis and 1 million Optimus bots could be bypassed for some or all of 12 tranches of stock. The article is opinion-editorial, but the clause language is sourced from the agreement.

- **Tesla capex-to-revenue ratio cited at ~9–10x** vs. 3–5x for Microsoft, Google, and Amazon, per Cern Basher's analysis using Q1 2016-onward data. The robotaxi and Optimus periods ahead are framed as the direct test of whether that ratio holds under a >$25B annual capex regime.

---

## Market & Competition

- **SpaceX IPO targeting ~$1.75–$2T valuation, expected June 12 (ticker: SPCX).** Merger odds: Wedbush's Ives at "80–90%" by early 2027; Kalshi at 33% before May 2027. NASDAQ rule change reportedly compresses index inclusion to 10 days post-IPO, forcing passive funds to buy at peak — with dilution risk for Tesla shareholders if an all-stock merger follows.

- **BYD EU/EFTA/UK YTD: 101,000+ units, +144% YoY.** Chery Auto grew 338% YoY in the same markets. EU full BEV share reached 19.7% YTD vs. 15.3% a year ago. GM/Samsung fully paused their $3.5B Synergy Cells battery plant; GM simultaneously directed $6B+ toward ICE investments including sixth-generation V8 engines.

- **Grok fell from second to fifth most-popular AI chatbot globally** by April 2026, per Electrek; monthly active users dropped 12.5% to 12.2M versus Claude's 23M (+44%). In enterprise, only 7% of companies reported using Grok vs. 48% for Claude. xAI's 62 unpermitted gas turbines in Memphis and Southaven face NAACP/Earthjustice emergency court action.

---

## Bear Case of the Week

- **Reuters investigation: Tesla's "10x safer" FSD claim overstates the true ratio by ~3x.** University of Michigan researcher Marco Benedetti corrected Tesla's methodology — which compared airbag-deployment crashes in Tesla's newer-than-average fleet against federal data including all tow-truck crashes — and found the corrected ratio is ~3x farther between crashes, not 10x. Ten of 11 traffic-safety researchers who reviewed the methodology told Reuters it amounted to misleading marketing. NHTSA has 4 active FSD/Autopilot investigations open, including a probe into dozens of cases where FSD ran red lights or turned into oncoming traffic. Tesla was also hit with a $243M verdict after an Autopilot crash in Florida killed a 22-year-old woman.

- **Reuters documented weeks of intensive pre-launch mapping in Austin**, directly contradicting Musk's repeated claim that Tesla's approach requires no "laborious local mapping." Utah labeling staff doubled to ~300 in the six months before the Austin launch. One former employee: "You can't get creative outside of that." The operational reality — a carefully mapped geofence — is structurally different from the vision-only generalization narrative used with investors.

- **Seven of nine former Tesla data labelers told Reuters they wouldn't trust FSD to drive them.** Labelers described FSD routinely failing to yield to emergency vehicles, give motorcyclists adequate space, brake on freeway off-ramps, and avoid construction zones. FSD was also reported regularly exceeding speed limits by 20–30 mph in "Mad Max" mode, with one instance of 60 mph in a 25-mph zone. One labeler: he wouldn't ride in a Tesla robotaxi "if you fucking paid me."

- **China FSD fraud trial opened May 30; triple-damage exposure on 1M+ HW3 vehicles.** Ten owners seeking $583K allege they paid ~$7,800 each for FSD between 2019 and 2021 and were excluded when Tesla's Chinese rollout supported only HW4. Under China's Consumer Rights Protection Law, triple damages are available. Tesla renamed the system "Tesla Assisted Driving" nine days before the hearing — a move Electrek characterizes as a tacit admission the original "Full Self-Driving" branding was misleading. Total global FSD/Autopilot-related litigation: $14.5B.

- **Unsupervised fleet count has not grown in over three weeks.** RobotaxiTracker.com shows no change from the May 9 snapshot across all three Texas cities. Cybercab production is running at ~30–36 units/day, vehicles are staged, Texas Level 4 authorization is live — yet the count of vehicles operating commercially without a human remains static. Bhakdi's own prior target of 1,800 unsupervised units by April–May 2026 missed by approximately a year, and his current projection of 1,000+ by end of June faces the same structural tension between production cadence and actual deployment pace.

- **Musk pay package "change in control" clause waives all operational milestones upon a Tesla–SpaceX merger.** If a merger occurs, Tesla need not deliver 1 million commercial robotaxis, 1 million Optimus bots, 20 million vehicle deliveries, or 10 million FSD subscriptions for Musk to collect some or all of 12 compensation tranches. Merger probability is actively debated at 33–90% depending on the source; the clause creates a direct structural conflict between Musk's financial incentive and Tesla shareholder interest in hitting the milestones that justify the current valuation.

articles.title: Three Robotaxi Leaders Just Changed The Game
articles.body:
This video covers three major developments in the robotaxi race: Tesla's continued infrastructure buildout in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, Waymo's launch of its new Zeekr-based "Oho" van with sixth-generation sensor hardware, and BYD's unprecedented move to offer full damage coverage for users of its "God's Eye" Level 2 autonomous driving system in China. Host Bert is joined by Jeff Lus, a former C-suite supply chain executive from Motorola, Google, and Lenovo, who provides commentary on unit economics, manufacturing strategy, and competitive dynamics. The central thesis is that all three companies are making significant strategic moves that signal the robotaxi industry is accelerating, but with very different approaches to scale, cost structure, and liability.

## Robotaxi

1. **Tesla's Fourth Known Fleet Support Facility Discovered:** A 51,000-square-foot service and delivery center is under construction in Grand Prairie, Texas — located between Dallas and Fort Worth, near Interstate 20. City documents confirm the facility's approved use includes charging, cleaning, repair, and maintenance of Tesla-owned autonomous vehicles, making it a potential robotaxi fleet support hub. This is now the fourth such facility discovered across the country: three in Texas (including a previously found 36,000-square-foot facility also in the Dallas area and one in Austin) and one in Las Vegas. Jeff Lus notes the "combo" design of combining service/delivery with fleet support maximizes both asset and labor utilization, and he interprets the infrastructure buildout as Tesla telegraphing a major, high-scale Cybercab rollout rather than a modest ride-share operation.

2. **World Cup Cybercab Launch Theory:** The video discusses a theory attributed to Jo Bhakdi that Tesla will time a Cybercab rollout in Dallas to coincide with the FIFA World Cup, which is expected to have games at Cowboys Stadium in Arlington, Texas. Bert expresses skepticism, noting the facility will not be complete in time and that FSD still requires more months of real-world data before a full unsupervised commercial deployment. Jeff Lus suggests that Cybercab hardware is likely ready given that Tesla has already committed to start of production, but the key remaining question is a software release that resolves edge cases sufficient for a large-scale public launch.

3. **Waymo Launches "Oho" Van for Public Rides:** Waymo has begun offering public rides in its new vehicle called the "Oho," a van built by Chinese automaker Zeekr that is imported to the US and retrofitted with Waymo's sixth-generation hardware at its Arizona facility. The sixth-gen hardware includes 13 cameras, four lidars, and six radars — representing 42% fewer sensors than the previous generation — but with upgraded 17-megapixel cameras that Waymo says improve performance despite the reduced sensor count. The hardware also integrates heaters, wipers, and sprayers directly into sensor pods for all-weather operation. Selected riders in San Francisco, Phoenix, and Los Angeles currently have access, with planned expansion to Denver, Las Vegas, and San Diego. Waymo also plans to add Hyundai Ioniq 5 robotaxis to its fleet soon.

4. **Waymo Oho Vehicle Cost and Unit Economics Questions:** Industry analyst "Barely AI" projects the Oho van costs $75,000–$100,000 per vehicle even after tariffs, compared to approximately $200,000 per vehicle for the current Jaguar I-Pace fleet. Jeff Lus cautions that this quoted price likely reflects a best-case scenario dependent on Zeekr achieving sufficient production volumes — if minimum volume commitments are not met, the actual all-in landed cost (including import, tariffs, and retrofitting in Arizona) could be materially higher. He notes that purpose-built low-volume platforms carry significant fixed cost risk because tooling and capex must be divided across a small unit base, unlike Tesla's Cybercab which is being planned for hundreds of thousands or potentially millions of units per year.

5. **Waymo's Ongoing Operational and Financial Challenges:** Waymo recently issued a voluntary software recall covering nearly 3,800 fifth- and sixth-generation robotaxis after some vehicles drove into standing water or flooded roads — the fix was a software update. Waymo also temporarily paused freeway rides after identifying issues around construction zones; the company says it encounters approximately 10,000 construction zones daily. On the financial side, the video references recent data showing Waymo is losing $5–6 billion and estimated to be losing approximately $100 per ride. Jeff Lus expresses frustration that financial media has not more aggressively scrutinized the cost-per-mile economics of robotaxi operators after six years of service.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD Progress and Path to Unsupervised Deployment:** Bert describes personal testing of what he refers to as a newer FSD version, noting that the system has removed the driver monitoring "nag" and allows increasingly long periods without driver intervention — though it is still officially labeled supervised FSD. The discussion frames Tesla's path to unsupervised FSD as closely tied to the geofenced areas already used for robotaxi operations: if Tesla is already comfortable running driverless robotaxis in Austin, Dallas, and Houston within specific geofences, extending unsupervised personal FSD to those same areas is a logical next step.

2. **Tesla Insurance as an "Infinite Money Glitch":** Jeff Lus argues that when Tesla eventually offers insurance coverage for unsupervised FSD, it will function as an "infinite money glitch" — because Tesla's data already demonstrates the system is not at fault in accidents, the insurance product will rarely if ever need to pay out. He draws an analogy to fully waterproofed smartphones where manufacturers sell water damage plans despite knowing the product won't fail. Lus notes Tesla already sells an insurance product in multiple regions and has reportedly taken out a license or entity in China to offer insurance there, giving it the actuarial data foundation to underwrite such a product confidently.

## Market & Competition

1. **BYD Offers Industry-First Full Damage Coverage for L2 System:** BYD announced it will provide one free full year of 100% damage coverage — including vehicle repairs, third-party property damage, and personal injury liabilities with no payout cap — for owners using its "God's Eye" Level 2 urban navigation system in China, as long as the system is used properly and in compliance with traffic regulations. This is described as the first time any automaker has ever provided damage reimbursement for an advanced driving system. BYD had previously offered coverage for its intelligent parking system, and is now extending it to full driving assistance.

2. **BYD's God's Eye Problems and Regulatory Crackdown in China:** The move comes amid serious user complaints about BYD's God's Eye system, including reports of unintended acceleration, erratic steering, and navigation failures, with BYD sales reportedly dropping 36%. More broadly, China has seen a wave of AV-related incidents: hundreds of BYD vehicles automatically stopped in a manner compared to Waymo's San Francisco power outage incidents; a fatal crash involving a Xiaomi SU7 using assisted driving killed three people after striking a highway structure and catching fire. Chinese regulators responded by restricting marketing terms like "autonomous driving" and "smart driving," drafting stricter Level 2 safety rules, and scrutinizing exaggerated claims across BYD, Tesla, Xiaomi, Xpeng, NIO, and others. Tesla can no longer use the "Full Self-Driving" label in China as a result.

3. **China's AV Competitive Landscape:** The video asserts that Tesla is the leader in China for autonomous driving capability, with Xpeng believed to be second. Huawei is also noted as a significant player — many robotaxis in China use Huawei technology — but Huawei itself has faced major incidents. BYD's scale (millions of vehicles sold) gives it a potential data advantage, but the video argues BYD currently lacks neural net and vision-only capability, still relying heavily on LiDAR, and is therefore behind Tesla by roughly one to two years. Xpeng is noted as having recently shifted to vision-only and eliminating LiDAR, offering its system for free to build the data volume needed to catch edge cases — described as a move that directly follows Tesla's approach.

4. **Competitive Pressure on Tesla's FSD Pricing and Insurance:** The discussion raises whether Tesla may face competitive pressure to reduce FSD subscription pricing if Xpeng is offering its system for free, and whether Tesla will need to introduce insurance coverage if BYD is offering it at no cost. Jeff Lus suggests Tesla will monitor the competitive dynamics and may need to respond, but notes that Tesla's brand strength and customer loyalty at its price tier provide a buffer against being forced into immediate price matching.

Notable quotes and data:
- Tesla's Grand Prairie, Texas facility: 51,000 sq ft, approved for charging, cleaning, repair, and maintenance of Tesla-owned autonomous vehicles
- Previously discovered Tesla fleet facilities: 36,000 sq ft in Dallas area, one in Austin, one in Las Vegas — now four total known
- Waymo's current fleet: approximately 3,700 vehicles (per recent filing cited in video)
- Waymo Oho projected vehicle cost: $75,000–$100,000 per vehicle after tariffs (per Barely AI estimate cited)
- Waymo Jaguar I-Pace fleet cost: approximately $200,000 per vehicle
- Waymo sixth-gen hardware: 13 cameras, 4 lidars, 6 radars — 42% fewer sensors than prior generation; upgraded to 17-megapixel cameras
- Waymo Oho van target: 100 vehicles currently operating, 1,000 on the road by end of 2025 (resolved: year-end 2026 per publish date context — though the transcript says "year end" without specifying)
- Waymo voluntary software recall: ~3,800 fifth- and sixth-gen robotaxis for flood/standing water navigation issue
- Waymo estimated losses: $5–6 billion total; approximately $100 loss per ride
- Waymo encounters ~10,000 construction zones daily
- BYD God's Eye insurance: 1 free year, 100% damage coverage, no payout cap, covers vehicle repairs, third-party property damage, and personal injury
- BYD sales reportedly dropped 36% amid God's Eye complaints
- Global annual traffic fatalities: approximately 1.19 million per year (cited in video from BYD God's Eye 5.0 presentation)
- BYD launched God's Eye 5.0 with a self-developed "Zhuanji A3" chip
- Jeff Lus: "Tesla's telegraphing. This stuff is just all out there in the public domain. You just have to be able to put two and two together."
- Jeff Lus on Cybercab hardware: "Tesla would not have gone to start of production unless reliability and convenience hardware issues have been worked out."
- Jeff Lus on Tesla insurance: "When you've engineered and solved that problem, you've created the infinite money glitch where people still will need to carry some policy... but the policy will never have to yield."

articles.title: Every AI Giant Just Moved, Tesla's in All Four
articles.body:
This video from "brighterwithherbert" features host Herbert and guest Jo Bhakdi — an economist, investor, and tech entrepreneur with a presence at pionerlands.org — reviewing a wave of major AI industry announcements that all broke within a single 24-hour period.
