2026-05-05.title: Daily X Summary (2026-05-05)
2026-05-05.body:
## Executive Summary
Today's posts are headlined by a meaningful Robotaxi operational milestone — Tesla's Unsupervised Model Y Robotaxis are now running at night in Austin, extending service hours, and a single day set a new record for unsupervised vehicle sightings across multiple cities. On the FSD adoption front, the Netherlands rollout is generating strong early data (6.2M miles in just 23 days), and FSD now accounts for ~0.25% of all miles driven in North America annually. European EV sales showed sharp recovery in April 2026 for most markets, while a 40-unit Tesla Semi order from Big F Transport signals continued commercial fleet interest. Overall signal is bullish, driven by expanding robotaxi operations and accelerating FSD adoption.

---

## Key Posts / Themes

1. **Unsupervised Robotaxi Expands: Night Operations Begin in Austin, Record Daily Sightings:** The most significant post of the day confirms that Tesla's Unsupervised Model Y Robotaxis have begun operating at night in Austin — a meaningful operational expansion beyond daytime-only service. Separately, the same day set a new record for new Unsupervised vehicle sightings, with 7 new Unsupervised Model Ys spotted across Dallas, Houston, and Austin combined. The post notes Tesla continues to operate Unsupervised vehicles only within its defined geofenced zones. This suggests Tesla is systematically expanding both operating hours and fleet presence across its initial launch cities, incrementally de-risking the path to broader commercial deployment.

2. **FSD International Rollout Gaining Traction: Netherlands Milestone:** Tesla FSD (Supervised) launched in the Netherlands on April 11, 2026, and has already accumulated 6.2 million miles in just 23 days — an average of over 270,000 miles per day. This rate of adoption is notable as an early indicator of pent-up demand for FSD in European markets. Combined with the separate data point that FSD now accounts for approximately 0.25% of all miles driven by humans in North America annually (~0.05% globally and rising), these figures illustrate the compounding scale of Tesla's real-world FSD data collection and the growing footprint of its autonomous driving system across geographies.

3. **Tesla Europe EV Sales Surge in April 2026:** Tesla's April 2026 European sales data showed strong year-over-year gains in most tracked markets: France (+112%), Sweden (+111%), Denmark (+102%), Ireland (+100%), Romania (+53%), Belgium (+47%), Netherlands (+23%), and Switzerland (+15%). Notable laggards were Portugal (-43%) and Norway (-71%). Europe's broader BEV share of new car registrations rose to 20.5% in the first four months of 2026, providing a favorable macro tailwind. The sharp recovery in most markets likely reflects the refreshed Model Y and improving consumer sentiment following prior quarters of weakness.

4. **Tesla Semi Commercial Momentum: 40-Unit Order from Big F Transport:** Big F Transport has ordered 40 Tesla Semi trucks following a recent demo unit trial. Driver feedback cited smoother and quieter operation, while fleet operators highlighted emissions reduction benefits tied to Scope 3 targets and California's WAIRE point regulatory incentives. This order is a concrete data point in Tesla Semi's commercial adoption story and signals that operational demos are converting to fleet commitments, particularly where regulatory incentives align.

5. **SEC Settles with Elon Musk for $1.5M Over Twitter Disclosure:** The SEC has settled its long-running lawsuit against Elon Musk regarding the delayed disclosure of his 2022 Twitter stake acquisition. Musk will pay $1.5 million without admitting wrongdoing. His attorney Alex Spiro stated Musk has been "cleared of all issues related to the late filing." While the dollar amount is immaterial to Tesla's financials, the resolution removes a lingering regulatory overhang and eliminates distraction risk for Musk — a modest positive for Tesla investor sentiment.

---

## Signal Strength: **Bullish** — Robotaxi night operations launching in Austin and record unsupervised vehicle sightings represent concrete operational progress, while FSD international adoption data and a rebound in European EV sales reinforce multiple legs of the Tesla growth thesis simultaneously.

2026-05-06.title: Tesla’s Biggest Mystery Is The Stock! Here's Why
2026-05-06.body:
The video features host Herbert and guest Jo Bhakdi — an economist, investor, and tech entrepreneur with a YouTube channel covering Tesla and AGI — discussing why Tesla's stock has remained flat around $400 for roughly four to five years despite enormous technological progress. The core thesis is that the stock market's tendency to price in entire futures instantaneously causes long plateaus followed by explosive re-ratings, and that Tesla is on the cusp of such a re-rating driven by robotaxi, Optimus, and broader AI/physical automation dominance. The conversation also zooms out to a macro view of AGI-era investing, competitive dynamics, and the argument that traditional value investing frameworks are insufficient for this technological moment.

## Market & Competition

1. **Tesla's stock plateau explained via market psychology:** Jo Bhakdi argues that Tesla's stock has been essentially flat since 2021 — hovering around $400, the same level it was at roughly four or more years ago — not because Tesla has failed to execute, but because the stock market front-loads all future value at once. He draws a parallel to the 2014–2019 period, when Tesla stock went from approximately $18.49 to $17 over five years — essentially flat — before exploding roughly 700% in the following year once Model Y's scalability became undeniable. He argues the same dynamic is playing out now, with the market skeptical about robotaxi and Optimus, but a similar explosive re-rating is coming once those prove out.

2. **Auto business vs. story premium in the $400 price:** Bhakdi estimates that Tesla's core auto business, valued with a generous growth multiple, is worth approximately $90 per share. That implies roughly two-thirds of the current $400 stock price represents some form of optionality or future revenue streams — robotaxi, Optimus, and other emerging businesses. He notes this breakdown is based on assuming the auto business continues to perform reasonably well going forward.

3. **The "10 Titans" competitive framework:** The discussion references analyst Cern Basher's thesis that the current Magnificent 7 will evolve into roughly 10 mega-titans that collectively come to own or displace most of the Fortune 500 through AI dominance. Bhakdi broadly agrees with this framing and argues Tesla/Elon's ecosystem is positioned to be among those titans, but warns the competition is formidable — particularly the Anthropic/Amazon axis, which he calls "dangerously strong." He ranks the competitive landscape as: Tesla/SpaceX first, Anthropic/Amazon second, with Meta (Zuckerberg) and OpenAI as important outliers to watch. He dismisses Google and Microsoft as cash-generative but not truly disruptive.

4. **Value investing is obsolete for AGI-era companies:** Bhakdi argues that Graham-style value investing — reading balance sheets, rear-mirror fundamentals — is no longer sufficient or even relevant for companies like Tesla in the age of AGI. He contends the only viable approach is predicting the future over 5–10 year horizons, identifying inflection points and forcing functions, and spotting mispricings between current price and reasonable future projections. He cites Cern Basher and ARK Invest as examples of analysts attempting this correctly.

5. **Cash flow robustness as the "indestructibility" criterion:** While dismissing traditional value investing, Bhakdi does emphasize one financial metric as critical: companies must consistently generate more cash than they spend. He argues this "indestructibility" — exemplified by SpaceX's Starlink free cash flow exceeding xAI spending — is what separates durable winners from those that flame out. He applies this to the Magnificent 7 broadly and to Tesla/SpaceX specifically.

## Robotaxi

1. **Robotaxi as the near-term inflection and forcing function:** Bhakdi identifies robotaxi as "imminent" and the key near-term catalyst that will trigger the next major stock re-rating. He argues that once the market sees robotaxi scaling — not at 1,000 or 2,000 units but on a trajectory toward tens of millions — it will not incrementally reprice Tesla but will instantly reprice the entire future fleet, similar to the 700% move seen when Model Y scalability was confirmed. He expects robotaxi to begin scaling at "super scale" by 2027 at the latest.

2. **2026–2027 as the revenue inflection window:** Bhakdi frames 2026 as "the year of robotaxi" and 2027 as when both robotaxi and Starlink will be generating meaningful cash flows. He suggests that by 2028, Tesla and SpaceX combined could be generating hundreds of billions in capex capacity from these new revenue streams, putting them on equal financial footing with the largest tech companies.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus as a longer-term but larger opportunity than robotaxi:** Bhakdi views Optimus as ultimately larger than robotaxi in terms of economic scale, though with a longer timeline to cash flow. He frames it as part of Elon's plan to become the "physical AI king" — the ability to instantaneously displace entire physical manufacturing industries, analogous to what Anthropic is doing to software industries. He gives a hypothetical example of being able to take over global shipping or increase US manufacturing output dramatically within a very short time once the physical AI + robotics stack is mature.

## Financials

1. **Tesla auto segment valued at approximately $90/share:** In Bhakdi's model, the auto business alone — valued with a growth multiple larger than comparable car companies — is worth roughly $90 per share. The remaining approximately $310 of the current ~$400 stock price is attributed to future optionality across robotaxi, Optimus, energy, and other emerging businesses.

2. **Path to cash flow parity with Mag 7 by 2027–2028:** Bhakdi argues Tesla does not currently have a cash flow problem — it is cash flow positive — but that robotaxi and Starlink revenues arriving at scale in 2027 will give Tesla the capacity to fund hundreds of billions in capex by approximately 2028, resolving any concern about being outspent by the Magnificent 7.

Notable quotes and data:
- "In 2014 September 18 bucks 49. When you move forward... basically exactly five years into 2019, 17 bucks. So for exactly five years that thing went from 18 bucks to 17 bucks over five years... one year later this thing is up 700%." — Jo Bhakdi
- "If you put a much bigger multiple on it than on the other car companies... it's probably 90 bucks. So, a huge chunk, two-thirds of the company is some kind of fantasy or future revenue streams." — Jo Bhakdi on the $400 stock price breakdown
- "At the moment where it becomes clear that this actually works, that you can actually scale robo taxi, they're not going to say, 'Oh, it's 1,000 robo taxis, let's see.' No, they're going to say, 'Well, if it's 2,000 now and grew like this, then it's going to be 20 million soon. Discount it back. Boom.'" — Jo Bhakdi
- "I think robo taxi is imminent and once robo taxi is imminent Tesla can move like eye to eye with Google." — Jo Bhakdi
- "They will start scaling at the very latest at super scale in 2027, both of them [robotaxi and Starlink]." — Jo Bhakdi
- "If you can't predict the future, you can't invest in these stocks." — Jo Bhakdi
- Tesla stock approximately $400 at time of recording; flat versus approximately 4–5 years prior (late 2021 highs)
- Tobias Lütke (CEO of Shopify) cited as a Tesla Model Y owner who praised FSD, Starlink, and X's auto-translation on the 20VC podcast

2026-05-06.title: Tesla's $14 Billion Truck Business Nobody Talks About
2026-05-06.body:
This video from "brighterwithherbert" argues that Tesla's Semi truck business is a massively underappreciated opportunity that most investors and analysts are overlooking. The host walks through a wave of recent fleet orders, Washington State's new $175,000 rebate program, the launch of Tesla's high-volume production line, and a new charging product suite — then pivots to the thesis that autonomous freight (robo trucking) could ultimately be a larger market than robotaxi, potentially arriving at commercial scale sooner than most expect.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Wave of major fleet orders in a single week:** In the span of roughly seven days, three significant Tesla Semi orders were publicly announced. Watt EV — a freight and charging operator based in Long Beach that runs its own depot network and software platform — placed a single order for 370 Tesla Semis, described as approximately $100 million and one of the largest electric Class 8 deployments in California history. The first 50 trucks are set to deliver in 2026, with the full 370-truck fleet operational by end of 2027; over 300 of those vehicles will support a joint program with the Port of Oakland for drayage and regional freight. Big F Transport, which already operated nine Freightliner eCascadia trucks out of the Port of Long Beach, brought in one Tesla Semi for a demo and immediately ordered 40 more, citing driver comfort, scope 3 emission targets, and favorable total cost of ownership versus diesel. Nika Container Freight Line, based in Los Angeles and servicing the ports of Long Beach, LA, and Houston, ordered 20 Semis, with those trucks slated to be operating by early 2027. Both the Big F and Nika fleets will charge at Form Mobility's new charging depot under development in Rancho Dominguez, California. The host notes DHL also has orders beyond a handful, putting the total of publicly announced recent orders at well over 430 trucks.

2. **Washington State's WAZIP program slashes upfront cost below diesel:** Washington State launched the Zero Emission Incentive Program (WAZIP), which knocks up to $175,000 off the price of a qualifying heavy-duty electric truck. The long-range Tesla Semi — originally priced at approximately $290,000 — drops to roughly $115,000 after the rebate, making it approximately $60,000 cheaper upfront than a new diesel Class 8 truck (priced at roughly $175,000 on average), before accounting for fuel and maintenance savings. The standard-range Semi at $260,000 is not yet on the approved list. The program is funded through Washington's Climate Commitment Act with a $120 million pool and the discount applies at point of sale. California already offers a comparable $200,000 voucher for clean trucks, and 900 of those vouchers have already gone to the Tesla Semi.

3. **High-volume production line goes live in Nevada:** On April 29, 2026, Tesla Semi's official account posted a video captioned "First Semi off high volume line," which accumulated 2.1 million views. The dedicated factory in Sparks, Nevada — 1.7 million square feet, located adjacent to Gigafactory Nevada — is designed to eventually produce 50,000 trucks per year. At Tesla's pricing of roughly $260,000 (standard range) and $290,000 (long range), 50,000 trucks per year works out to approximately $14 billion in annual revenue at full ramp. The host estimates 2026 production will be somewhere between 5,000 and 15,000 units based on analyst projections. The host's view is that the historic bottleneck — battery cell supply — has likely been resolved now that the 4680 cell factory is in the same complex.

4. **Tesla Semi specs and competitive positioning:** The long-range Semi delivers 500 miles of range with a full payload and consumes 1.7 kWh per mile, compared to the diesel equivalent of 5–7 kWh per mile — making it roughly 3 to 4 times more efficient than diesel. The truck features a tri-motor powertrain with 800 kW (approximately 1,073 horsepower), three times the power of an average diesel semi. The battery is designed to last 1 million miles. The standard-range version has a turning radius comparable to a Tesla Model 3 or Model Y, and a drag coefficient of 0.04 (described as better than most pickup trucks). Fleet uptime is reportedly 95%. The truck uses the same 4680 cells as the Cybertruck, has wireless charging on the roadmap, and can power refrigeration trailers via the same power-share technology as Cybertruck. Individual owner-operators, not just fleets, can purchase the Semi. A Fox News segment cited in the video noted that a 500-mile California trip costs approximately $520 in diesel at $7.66/gallon versus approximately $275 for a single Semi charge — roughly half the cost per trip.

5. **New charging product suite removes depot infrastructure barrier:** On May 1, 2026, Tesla launched "Semi Charging for Business," comprising two products. The Mega Charger delivers 1.2 MW of power, achieving 60% range in 30 minutes, and is built for freight corridors; a basic two-post setup starts at approximately $188,000. The Base Charger is a 125 kW unit designed for overnight depot charging, adding 60% range in approximately four hours; it is a fully integrated unit requiring no separate AC-to-DC cabinet, priced at $40,000 for two units installed. Up to three Base Chargers can be daisy-chained on a single breaker without a major utility upgrade. Bulk pricing scales to $9.4 million for 100 Mega Charger posts or $2 million for 100 Base Chargers. Deliveries of the Base Charger begin in early 2027, aligning with the high-volume Semi ramp. The host quotes Jordan from The Limiting Factor: "This is massive. With a base charger as an option, I'm no longer concerned that the charging network will be the rate limiting factor for semi production." Tesla has also mapped 66 planned Mega Charger locations across 15 states at 1.2 MW each; Texas leads with 19 sites and California has 17, covering I-10 and I-5. A deal with Pilot Flying J targets 46 Mega Charger stations operational by early 2027.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Highway driving is structurally easier for AI than urban robotaxi environments:** The host argues that the conventional assumption — that robotaxi arrives before autonomous trucking — may be backwards. Urban robotaxi operation requires handling pedestrians, cyclists, construction zones, complex intersections, and school zones. Long-haul highway driving features consistent speeds, clear lane markings, predictable driver behavior, and very few intersections. Tesla's own FSD data is cited as support: Tesla recently crossed 10 billion FSD miles, and over 62% of those miles are highway miles, meaning the AI system is more extensively trained on the environment where trucks spend most of their time.

2. **Tesla Semi is "autonomy ready" per spec sheet:** A walkaround posted by Sora Merritt ahead of ACT Expo (May 4–7, 2026, the largest clean transportation trade show in North America) showed two new Tesla Semis in Las Vegas and noted Tesla describing the trucks as "autonomy ready," with cameras called out explicitly. The host frames this as a small phrase with large implications for the robo trucking thesis.

3. **Staged autonomous trucking timeline:** The host outlines a three-stage framework. Stage 1 — supervised highway autonomy with a monitoring driver — is estimated at roughly two years from now (approximately 2028), with pilot-form activity already underway. Stage 2 — hub-to-hub autonomous freight where a truck drives 400 highway miles driverless between terminals while humans handle yard operations — is estimated at roughly three years away for Tesla (approximately 2029). Stage 3 — fully door-to-door autonomy including yard navigation, loading, and docking — is estimated at roughly six years away. The host emphasizes that Stage 3 is not required to capture massive value; eliminating the highway driver alone eliminates a cost of $70,000–$90,000 per year in salary plus benefits.

4. **Competitive landscape in autonomous trucking:** Aurora Innovation launched commercial driverless freight runs in Texas in late 2024, and Plus.ai is running autonomous miles for paying customers. The host acknowledges Tesla is not currently the leader in autonomous trucks. However, Tesla's differentiators are cited as: the largest real-world FSD dataset on the planet; vertical integration across vehicle, battery, and software; and its own dedicated truck factory. Aurora, by contrast, is software-only and runs on Kenworth trucks.

## Market & Competition

1. **Goldman Sachs projects autonomous trucking is a larger market than robotaxi by 2035:** Goldman Sachs recently published a deep analysis projecting that the global robotaxi market reaches $415 billion by 2035, while the global autonomous trucking market reaches $560 billion by 2035 — making autonomous freight the larger opportunity by Goldman's own numbers. The host ties this to the underlying market: US freight trucking revenue exceeds $830 billion annually, and global freight trucking is approximately $2.6 trillion. Freight demand is described as massive, predictable, and growing due to e-commerce.

2. **Driver shortage creates structural tailwind for autonomous trucking:** There are approximately 60,000 unfilled truck driving positions in the US currently, with industry groups projecting that number could nearly triple. Annual driver turnover at major carriers runs approximately 90% per year. The host frames autonomous trucking as the most obvious structural fix to what he calls a "broken labor model."

3. **Cost-per-mile crossover projected around 2028:** Goldman Sachs projects the cost per mile for autonomous trucks drops from $8.56 today to approximately $2.30 by 2035. The crossover point at which autonomous trucks become cheaper per mile than human-driven trucks is projected for around 2028.

## Financials

1. **Semi revenue potential at full ramp:** At 50,000 trucks per year at an average price of approximately $275,000, the Semi business represents approximately $13–14 billion in annual revenue — a standalone business separate from cars and energy. The host notes this is not being priced in by the market, let alone the additional upside from autonomous freight-as-a-service. Capturing even a single-digit percentage of the $830 billion US trucking market would materially change the valuation multiple, per the host.

Notable quotes and data:
- Watt EV CEO: "The Semi was the easiest choice, based on cost, performance, and availability."
- Nika Container Freight CEO Jackie Lopez: "We want to invest in advanced technology. We're excited to grow our business with these awesome new zero emission trucks."
- Jordan (The Limiting Factor): "This is massive. With a base charger as an option, I'm no longer concerned that the charging network will be the rate limiting factor for semi production."
- Elon Musk tweet, April 15: "Tesla semi" (40 million views)
- Fox News segment: 500-mile California trip costs ~$520 in diesel vs. ~$275 on a single Tesla Semi charge
- Tesla crossed 10 billion FSD miles; over 62% are highway miles

2026-05-06.title: Why on Earth Is No One Talking About This ⚡️
2026-05-06.body:
This video from the "electrified" channel covers a wide range of Tesla news, with particular focus on the Tesla Semi's growing order book and the Watt EV "truck-as-a-service" business model, updates on FSD regulatory progress in the EU and China, competition in autonomous driving, and a grab-bag of smaller Tesla news items including brand loyalty data, new product updates, and the Boring Company's Nashville residential loop announcement.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Tesla Semi Orders and Watt EV Deployment:** Watt EV announced an order for 370 Tesla Semis to be deployed across California. Deliveries are expected to begin with 50 trucks in 2026, with the full fleet operational by the end of 2027. More than 300 of those trucks will be deployed under a joint program with the Port of Oakland. The deployment will be supported by megawatt charging depots at the Port of Oakland and Fresno, with additional planned sites in Stockton and Sacramento. Watt EV also has 15 additional charging sites under development as part of a broader statewide and eventual nationwide network.

2. **Watt EV's "Truck-as-a-Service" Model:** The host argues that a widely overlooked aspect of the Tesla Semi story is Watt EV's business model. Rather than simply operating its own freight fleet, Watt EV offers a turnkey electrification solution — bundling the truck, access to charging depots, maintenance, telematics, and operational support into a single monthly subscription. This eliminates the major upfront capital cost for smaller fleet operators looking to electrify. Fleets that already own electric trucks can also subscribe separately to Watt EV's charging depot network. The host contends this model — mirrored by companies like Alio and Volvo on Demand — will be a critical accelerant for electric semi adoption, particularly for smaller operators, while large players like Amazon, Walmart, and FedEx are expected to continue buying direct.

3. **Tesla Semi Dashboard Tracker:** The host announced they are building a crowdsourced dashboard (vibe-coded with Perplexity Computer) to track Tesla Semi orders and the status of megawatt charging depots nationwide. The tracker will be made publicly available within the next week or two, and currently shows confirmed orders from Watt EV, NICA, and Big F Transport, along with depot locations filterable by operational, under construction, and planned status.

4. **Cybertruck Lease Price Increase:** Tesla raised the price of the Cybertruck Premium all-wheel drive lease in the US by 10%. The host declined to read deeply into this but expressed eagerness to see Cybertruck sales for Q2 and Q3 2026, hoping for a directional improvement rather than a dramatic jump. Anecdotal evidence and lower-priced trim deliveries are cited as reasons for cautious optimism.

5. **Model Y L Five-Star Safety Rating and Imminent US Launch:** Tesla's Model Y L received a five-star safety rating from ANCAP. A mystery car spotted under a cover at Giga Texas is speculated by the host to be the Model Y L, with the release described as feeling "imminent" for the US market.

6. **Tesla Semi ACT Expo UI and Mega Charger Showcase:** David Moss captured footage of the Tesla Semi at the ACT Expo in Las Vegas, showing the truck's UI — including deck lights, side storage, hood vitals, charge port controls, and per-tire PSI and temperature readouts. The Tesla Semi's Mega Charger handle and stall scale were also showcased, described as significantly larger than standard charging hardware.

7. **Next-Generation Roadster Trademark:** Sawyer found a new trademark application for what appears to be the next-generation Tesla Roadster logo or badge. The filing describes lines depicting speed, propulsion, heat, or wind. One observer noted the shape closely resembles SpaceX's Starship V3 quick-disconnect receptacle panel, reinforcing speculation about a SpaceX technology collaboration for the vehicle.

8. **Battery Health Certificate in Tesla App:** A Tesla app decompile revealed Tesla is adding an official, exportable digital certificate confirming high-voltage battery repairs or replacements directly in the app. The host highlights this as a meaningful improvement for the used EV market, where verifying battery health has historically been a limiting factor for buyers.

9. **Giga Texas Test Track Under Construction:** Joe Tegtmeyer shared footage of asphalt being laid at Giga Texas for a new on-site test track, which will allow Tesla to conduct proving ground-type testing — including high-speed handling, braking, acceleration, and durability testing — without shipping vehicles to a remote location.

10. **Tesla Brand Loyalty Leads All US Brands:** S&P Global Mobility data for February 2026 shows Tesla at 61.1% brand loyalty, ranking number one in the US ahead of Subaru, Toyota, and Ferrari. The host notes this sharply contrasts with headlines from August 2025 claiming Tesla's brand loyalty had collapsed following Elon Musk's political activities.

11. **FSD One-Time Purchase Ending in Europe:** Tesla is ending one-time FSD purchases across Europe on May 21st, 2026, affecting the UK, Germany, France, Italy, Belgium, Switzerland, Denmark, and others — consistent with Tesla's strategy in North America to shift customers toward subscriptions.

12. **Tesla Supercharger Lounge in France:** Tesla is opening a Supercharger lounge in partnership with BK World in Lyon, France, featuring 28 Superchargers. This is the fifth joint location in France.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **EU FSD Regulatory Update — No Vote at May 5th Meeting:** The May 5th TCMV meeting passed without a vote on supervised FSD approval across the EU. Regulators sat through approximately one hour of FSD demonstrations covering European traffic and mixed weather conditions, but raised concerns about the system occasionally exceeding speed limits, wildlife hazards (specifically moose in Nordic countries), icy roads, and the name "Full Self-Driving" itself. There was also reported pushback related to political pressure from Tesla supporters contacting officials.

2. **Next EU Vote Window and Individual Country Paths:** The next opportunity for an EU-wide vote is June 30th, 2026. If no vote occurs then, the next gathering is in October. Roughly 15 of 27 member countries would need to vote in favor for the measure to pass. The host describes a broad EU FSD rollout this summer as "pretty optimistic" and suggests Q4 2026 may be a more realistic timeline. In the interim, individual countries can choose to recognize the Netherlands' existing approval independently.

3. **Belgium, Denmark, Sweden, and Switzerland Express Interest:** Belgium's Minister of Mobility asked Tesla to transfer supervised FSD files to his administration, instructing it to provide clarity on a possible "rapid homologation" by end of week. A regulator from Denmark stated Tesla's vehicles "performed very well in the complex traffic of rush hour in Copenhagen." Sweden's transport agency said the country is "generally positive on automated driving tech as long as it follows regulations." Switzerland's regulator (Astra) said it has no problem with level two plus systems as long as Tesla clearly communicates that the driver remains fully responsible.

4. **FSD in China — Internal Employee Trial and Q3 Approval Target:** An unverified account reported that Tesla made a version of FSD (cited as version 14.3.2) with full functionality available to employees in China. Separately, analyst Ming noted Tesla recently added a confidentiality clause to its employee FSD trial policy in China, with violations carrying a penalty of approximately $732,000 — suggesting Tesla employees are unlikely to be leaking information. On Tesla's Q1 earnings call, the company stated it expects broader FSD approval in China in Q3 2026. The host characterizes FSD's status in China as "a black box" and describes the current approval as limited, with Tesla working to gather data and accelerate the process given strong local competition.

5. **Momenta — Key Chinese Autonomous Driving Competitor to Watch:** The host introduces Momenta, a Chinese autonomous driving software company that has been operating for roughly a decade. Momenta supplies its AI software to OEMs rather than building vehicles itself, and uses an end-to-end neural network approach handling perception, planning, and control — similar to Tesla's FSD architecture. The company uses lidar but claims its software is system- and chip-agnostic. Investors include GM, Mercedes, and Tencent. More than 50 production vehicle models have been delivered with Momenta's software, representing hundreds of thousands of vehicles. Momenta has two products: M Pilot (level two plus, driver-assisted) and MSD (targeting full autonomy at levels three and four). It also has a strategic partnership with Uber to launch in Europe. The host frames Momenta as a significant competitive threat to Tesla FSD in China and a name to watch in Europe.

6. **Huawei NCA Incident in China:** The host briefly noted a reported incident in which Huawei's NCA level two autonomous driving technology struck a child. The individual who shared video of the incident on social media was reportedly reported to police and forced to sign a pledge not to spread negative news about Huawei. Chinese authorities are alleged to be suppressing further discussion.

## Market & Competition

1. **Nuro Receives California DMV Permit for Driverless Lucid Gravity Testing:** The California DMV modified Nuro's existing driverless AV permit to include the Lucid Gravity SUV, allowing Nuro to test its autonomous system without a safety driver on public roads. Nuro has held a driverless permit in California for six years, previously covering only low-speed autonomous delivery vehicles. However, Nuro still requires two additional approvals — a driverless ride-hailing permit from the CPUC and a separate commercial deployment permit from the DMV — before it can offer paid rides. The host notes that, like Tesla, Nuro has not yet applied for the CPUC permit needed for a true AV passenger service, putting both companies at a similar stage for commercialization despite Nuro being slightly ahead on the DMV testing permit.

2. **Tesla Regulatory Credits in Australia:** Tesla earned $3 million in regulatory credits sold to legacy automakers in Australia under the country's new vehicle emission standards, which came into force in 2025 — the first year such income was generated. The host notes that emission targets tighten annually, meaning demand for Tesla's credits is likely to grow. Also highlighted: battery storage has grown from 15% of Tesla's Australian revenue in 2023 to 55% in 2025, surpassing EVs as the primary revenue driver in that market.

## Energy

1. **Tesla Battery Storage Dominates Australia Revenue:** In Australia, battery storage now accounts for 55% of Tesla's revenue, up from 15% in 2023, despite a substantial fall in battery prices over that period. The host frames this as evidence of the surging success of Tesla's storage business internationally and notes that regulatory vehicle credits do not cover the storage segment.

## Financials

1. **Tesla Stock and Volume:** Tesla stock closed at $398.73, up 2.4% on the day, while the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) was up 2.08%. Trading volume was 17% below the daily average.

2. **Terafab Chip Fabrication Facility — $119 Billion Total Investment:** Elon Musk commented on a post identifying Grimes County, Texas as a location under consideration for what is described as "the largest and most advanced chip fabrication facility in the world." The estimated capital for the initial phase is $55 billion, with an estimated total investment of $119 billion. The host notes that SpaceX is expected to cover the majority of the cost for the Terafab facility itself, while Tesla would cover R&D chip fabrication at Giga Texas. The host characterizes Elon's public comment as a likely negotiating tactic to encourage competing location offers.

---

Notable quotes and data:
- Watt EV order: 370 Tesla Semis, 50 deliveries in 2026, full fleet by end of 2027, 300+ under Port of Oakland joint program
- EU FSD: Next vote opportunity June 30, 2026; then October if no June vote; ~15 of 27 countries must vote in favor
- Belgium Minister of Mobility: "You should not slow down innovation, but make it possible in a thoughtful and safe way."
- Switzerland Astra director: "The only thing that we are demanding is that these systems are to be denominated as such. They aren't level three, they are level two plus."
- Denmark regulator: "The vehicles did perform very well in the complex traffic of rush hour in Copenhagen."
- FSD China employee trial penalty clause: ~$732,000 for violating confidentiality policy
- Tesla Q1 call guidance: Broader FSD approval in China expected Q3 2026
- Momenta: 50+ production vehicle models delivered with their software, hundreds of thousands of vehicles; investors include GM, Mercedes, Tencent; Uber partnership for European launch
- Tesla brand loyalty: 61.1% as of February 2026 (S&P Global Mobility), #1 in the US
- Tesla Australia: $3M in regulatory credits, battery storage = 55% of revenue (up from 15% in 2023)
- Tesla FSD one-time purchases ending in Europe: May 21, 2026
- Nuro: Holds driverless CA DMV permit for 6 years; now modified to include Lucid Gravity; still needs CPUC + commercial DMV permits for paid rides
- Terafab: $55B initial phase, $119B total estimated investment; Grimes County, Texas under consideration
- Tesla stock close: $398.73, +2.4%; volume 17% below average
- Cybertruck Premium AWD lease price raised 10%
- Boring Company Nashville residential loop: airport in ~9 minutes, lower Broadway in ~2 minutes
- Tesla lounge with BK World in Lyon, France: 28 Superchargers, fifth joint France location

2026-05-06.title: Tesla’s $29K Model 3 Strategy Breakdown
2026-05-06.body:
This video from FutureAzA covers Tesla's surprise launch of the rear-wheel drive Model 3 Premium in Canada at approximately $29,000 USD — the cheapest new Tesla available in North America. Host Brian is joined by Canadian guest Mark to break down the pricing strategy, the Canadian government's Chinese import quota allowance, and what this means for Tesla's sales momentum heading into Q2 and Q3 2026.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Canada's $29K Model 3 Premium Launch:** Tesla quietly listed a rear-wheel drive Model 3 Premium on its Canadian website overnight, priced at approximately $29,000 USD (roughly $39,990 CAD). This is a significant reduction from the previous starting price of approximately $79,990 CAD, which had been elevated due to cross-border tariff complications stemming from the suspension of USMCA. The vehicle is built in China and uses an LFP battery, which Mark and Brian note carries the advantage of being safely chargeable to 100% without the degradation risk associated with high-nickel NMC or NCA batteries. For comparison, the same Model 3 rear-wheel drive Premium on the US website is listed at $42,490 USD — over $13,000 more than the Canadian price.

2. **Chinese Import Quota as the Pricing Mechanism:** The dramatically lower price is made possible by Canada's policy allowing 49,000 Chinese-built vehicles to be imported at reduced tariff rates in the current year, with the quota growing to close to 70,000 per year over the 5-year term of the deal. Critically, only 50% of the quota must consist of vehicles with an import price below $35,000 CAD — the retail price can be higher. Tesla's Shanghai-built Model 3 apparently qualifies with an import cost under the $35,000 CAD threshold, enabling the aggressive retail pricing. Mark and Brian speculate that Tesla has likely claimed a significant portion of this quota and that ships from Giga Shanghai are reportedly already en route to Canada's west coast, while Giga Berlin-sourced Model Y units are being delivered to the east coast via Halifax, Nova Scotia.

3. **Tesla's Competitive Advantage in Capturing the Quota:** Mark emphasizes that Chinese EV brands like BYD and Geely, while rumored to be scouting dealership locations in Canada (BYD reportedly looking countrywide, Geely looking regionally in Ontario), have not yet established the sales networks, parts distribution, or warranty infrastructure needed to capitalize on the quota. Polestar, while having a Canadian presence through Volvo, does not have qualifying vehicles in the right price range. This leaves Tesla positioned to capture not just the majority but potentially nearly all of the 49,000 quota in the first year — split roughly between the lower-priced standard models and the premium/long-range/performance variants.

4. **Strong Demand Signals and Delivery Timelines:** Mark visited a Tesla dealership in Brampton, Ontario and observed a steady stream of customers inquiring about the new Model 3 offer since the announcement. Delivery estimates have already slipped from June to October 2026, indicating strong order intake. Mark advises Canadian buyers on the fence to act quickly, warning the allocation may run out. Brian contextualizes this within broader Tesla sales momentum: the Model Y ranked #1 among all cars (not just EVs) in Colombia for two consecutive months, and globally for March 2026, the Model Y and Model 3 ranked #1 and #2 respectively among EVs.

5. **Model Y Long Range (Model Y L) in Canada:** Discussion briefly touched on the possibility of Tesla eventually importing the Model Y L (long range variant) from Shanghai to Canada. Mark believes it is possible but expects a delay, as Tesla is focused on the current Model 3 launch first, and any additional Chinese-built imports would draw from the same 49,000-vehicle quota. Brian suggests Tesla may time the Model Y L Canada launch to coincide with a US release.

## Market & Competition

1. **Chinese Brands Not Yet a Threat in Canada:** Despite geopolitical narratives around Chinese EV dominance, Mark confirms that BYD, Geely, and Xiaomi currently have no sales or distribution presence in Canada. They are in early scouting phases for dealership locations but have not signed leases or opened any sites. The practical requirements of warranty coverage, parts distribution, and service networks mean these brands cannot realistically compete for the 2026 import quota allocation.

2. **Tesla's Margin and Competitive Position:** Brian notes that contrary to narratives about Tesla losing customers, sales numbers are coming in stronger than expected in most markets, and Tesla continues to lead on margin compared to competitors. The Canadian pricing strategy is cited as a further demonstration of Tesla's ability to leverage its global manufacturing and supply chain flexibility in ways that rivals currently cannot replicate.

Notable quotes and data:
- Model 3 rear-wheel drive Premium Canada price: ~$29,000 USD / ~$39,990 CAD
- Previous Canada Model 3 starting price: ~$79,990 CAD (pre-quota, post-tariff suspension)
- Same Model 3 Premium on US website: $42,490 USD
- Canadian Chinese-vehicle import quota: 49,000 vehicles in 2026, growing to ~70,000/year over a 5-year deal
- 50% of quota reserved for vehicles with an import cost below $35,000 CAD; retail price can be higher
- Delivery wait times for new Canadian Model 3 orders: pushed from June to October 2026
- Model Y units shipping from Giga Berlin to Halifax, Nova Scotia (east coast); Model 3 units shipping from Giga Shanghai to Canada's west coast
- Model Y ranked #1 among all cars (not just EVs) in Colombia for the past two months
- Model Y #1 and Model 3 #2 globally among EVs in March 2026
- Model 3 LFP 0–100 km/h time reportedly listed with a 1-second typo on Tesla's Canadian website; confirmed to be the same vehicle as previously sold
- Brian: "Making me jealous is what it's doing" — on the $13K+ price gap between Canadian and US Model 3 pricing

2026-05-06.title: Terafab Location, Boring Station Named, Robotaxi on Android, & more... Live at 8am Pacific
2026-05-06.body:
This FutureAzA live stream from May 6, 2026 covers a broad range of Tesla and EV-adjacent news, including the robotaxi app launching on Android, FSD being fast-tracked in Belgium, a massive Tesla Semi order, and a first Model Y Long sighting in North America. The host also touches on SpaceX's proposed chip fab in Texas, the Boring Company's Nashville loop station, China's pause on new robotaxi licenses, and the Nuro/Lucid/Uber autonomous vehicle partnership. The tone is optimistic on Tesla's trajectory while skeptical of competitor announcements.

## Autonomous Driving
1. **FSD Fast-Tracked in Belgium:** FSD has been fast-tracked for regulatory approval in Belgium through a process described as "rapid homologation." The host notes this may not cover all of Belgium — potentially only portions — but welcomes any expansion of FSD's geographic reach as an opportunity to demonstrate the technology to more people.

2. **FSD Quality Perception at a Plateau:** The host notes anecdotal feedback from the community that FSD has become so capable that users can no longer easily identify what has improved between versions. The host personally recounts a round-trip drive to Costco where nothing notable happened — no edge cases, no interventions — describing this as a positive sign, not a negative one.

3. **China Pauses New Robotaxi License Issuance:** On March 31st, over 100 of BYD's Apollo Go robotaxis froze simultaneously due to a server connectivity failure. In response, Chinese regulators paused the issuance of new robotaxi expansion licenses and new applications, though operators already approved are allowed to continue. The host views this as a measured regulatory response.

## Robotaxi
1. **Tesla Robotaxi App Launches on Android:** Tesla's robotaxi app has officially launched on Android, bringing feature parity with the existing iOS version. The host notes Android users missed the introductory pricing window (humorously referenced as $4.20) that was available at the iOS launch.

2. **Nuro/Lucid/Uber Partnership — Skepticism Warranted:** Nuro has received a modified DMV driverless testing permit in California to test Lucid Gravity SUVs as part of a three-way partnership with Lucid and Uber. Lucid has delivered 75 engineering vehicles to Nuro for testing. The vehicles use Nvidia's Drive AGX Thor compute platform. However, the host is sharply skeptical: Nuro has held a driverless permit for 6 years but only ever operated low-speed vehicles, scrapped that program, pivoted to licensing technology, and is not yet ready to launch a real service. The host questions what proprietary technology Nuro actually brings to the table. In California, the host notes there are four distinct permitting steps required to operate a real commercial service, and Nuro is far from that.

## Electric Vehicles
1. **Tesla Semi Receives 370-Unit, $100 Million Order:** At the ACT Expo, Tesla Semi received an order for 370 units totaling approximately $100 million from three separate buyers. Updated pricing was confirmed: $260,000 for the short-range variant and $290,000 for the long-range variant. The host, citing industry analysts and professionals in electric trucking, says $300,000 is the price threshold below which electric trucking makes economic sense — putting both Semi variants in favorable territory.

2. **First Model Y Long (Model Y L) Mule Spotted in North America:** A camouflaged Model Y Long mule was photographed on I-280 northbound in what the host describes as expected timing for Q2 2026. The host had been hoping for a formal announcement by this point but acknowledges Tesla is likely holding back to avoid an "Osborne effect" on current Model Y sales. The host notes the vehicle is visually similar to a standard Model Y and the camouflage actually draws more attention than the car would otherwise.

3. **Tesla Battery Certification Feature Rolled Out:** Tesla has quietly added an official battery repair certification feature in its app. When Tesla performs a major high voltage battery repair or full replacement, a permanent, verifiable digital certificate now appears in the vehicle's service history tab, downloadable as a PDF. The host frames this as solving a major used EV market pain point — service records often disappear when vehicles change hands, making battery health a negotiation liability for sellers.

## Energy
1. **$225 Million Megapack BESS Project in South Australia:** A new $225 million Megapack battery energy storage system is under construction in South Australia, with the Kulonga battery project scheduled for completion by September 27th. Uno Ekis is the developer, owner, and operator. The host clarifies this is a deployment project, not a new Megapack factory.

2. **Solar and Wind Reach Price Parity:** Solar and wind energy now costs $54–$82 per megawatt hour, down from approximately $100 just a few years ago. New coal capacity in China costs $70–$85 per megawatt hour, and new gas capacity globally exceeds $100 per megawatt hour — putting renewables at or below parity with fossil fuel alternatives. The host uses this to rebut common arguments that renewables are too expensive or require subsidies, noting fossil fuels also receive substantial subsidies.

## Market & Competition
1. **SpaceX Proposes $55–$119 Billion Chip Fab in Grimes, Texas:** SpaceX has filed to build a next-generation, vertically integrated semiconductor manufacturing and advanced computing fabrication facility in Grimes County, Texas, approximately 2 hours from Austin. The proposed investment is listed at $55 billion with a possible ceiling of $119 billion. A public hearing is scheduled for June 3rd. Elon Musk noted this is one of several locations under consideration for what he described as the largest and most advanced chip fab in the world. The host cheekily insists the chip fab already planned near Giga Texas will be more advanced.

2. **Boring Company Announces Nashville Residential Loop Station:** The Boring Company announced its first residential loop station agreement in Nashville, serving residents of the Prime, Al Cove, and Paramount Towers. Residents will take an elevator from their building directly to a loop station, with travel times of 9 minutes to the airport and 2 minutes to lower Broadway. The host is enthusiastic about the time savings and dismisses aesthetic objections to underground infrastructure.

Notable quotes and data:
- Tesla Semi pricing: $260,000 (short range), $290,000 (long range); 370-unit, ~$100 million order from three buyers at ACT Expo
- Solar/wind cost: $54–$82/MWh, down from ~$100; new gas globally: >$100/MWh; new coal in China: $70–$85/MWh
- South Australia Megapack BESS: $225 million, scheduled completion September 27th
- SpaceX chip fab proposed investment: $55 billion listed, up to $119 billion; location: Grimes County, Texas; public hearing June 3rd
- Boring Company Nashville loop: 9 minutes to airport, 2 minutes to lower Broadway
- Lucid delivered 75 engineering vehicles to Nuro/Uber for robotaxi testing
- China: 100+ Apollo Go robotaxis froze on March 31st due to server failure; new license issuance paused
- Tesla Megapack gross margin referenced as approximately 30%; Tesla vehicle gross margin approximately 20%
- Host on FSD usability: "It is really hard to tell if anything has improved. I no longer record my average FSD drives unless I've got something very specific."
- On Tesla Semi economics: "$300,000 is the sweet spot. If you're under that, it makes sense."

2026-05-06.title: LIVE: SpaceX And Claude STRATEGIC ALLIANCE - What it Means
2026-05-06.body:
This live stream from Jo Bhakdi covers the breaking news of a strategic compute partnership between Anthropic (makers of Claude) and SpaceX, specifically granting Anthropic access to the Colossus One data center's 220,000+ Nvidia GPUs and 300 megawatts of capacity. Bhakdi's core thesis is that this deal represents the early formation of a "magic trinity" — Nvidia, SpaceX, and Anthropic — that he believes will define the trajectory of AGI and ASI development, with orbital AI compute being the ultimate long-term business model for SpaceX. He also briefly touches on Tesla's robotaxi progress and his personal portfolio performance.

## Market & Competition

1. **Anthropic-SpaceX Colossus One Deal:** Anthropic has signed an agreement with SpaceX to use compute capacity at the Colossus One data center, gaining access to over 220,000 Nvidia GPUs (described as mostly Blackwell B200s) and 300 megawatts of power capacity. Bhakdi emphasizes this is happening "within the month" (May 2026) and considers it far more significant than Anthropic's other compute deals, including a 5-gigawatt agreement with Amazon and a separate 5-gigawatt agreement with Google and Broadcom (slated to come online in 2027), and a $30 billion partnership with Microsoft and Nvidia. He argues 300 megawatts of Blackwell-class GPUs is likely at least three times more effective than equivalent wattage in Amazon Tranium or Google TPU chips.

2. **XAI Merged Into SpaceX; Colossus 2 Frees Up Colossus 1:** Elon Musk announced that XAI has been fully integrated into SpaceX. Musk noted that SpaceX AI had already moved its training workloads to Colossus 2, which freed up Colossus One to be leased to Anthropic. Bhakdi notes this was never the original design intent for Colossus One and represents a significant strategic shift — SpaceX is now openly positioning itself as a compute provider to third parties, including those who could be considered competitors to Grok.

3. **Elon's "Evil Detector" and Strategic Rationale:** Musk publicly stated he spent significant time with senior Anthropic leadership to evaluate whether Claude poses risks to humanity, and that "no one set off my evil detector." Bhakdi interprets this as genuine — not merely commercial — motivation, arguing Elon understands ASI is close and wants to ensure leading AI labs are not dangerous. Bhakdi frames the partnership as 10% business and 90% strategic/safety-motivated on Elon's part.

4. **The "Magic Trinity" Thesis — Nvidia, SpaceX, Anthropic:** Bhakdi's central analytical argument is that three entities are converging into a de facto strategic alliance: Nvidia (unbeatable on AI chips), SpaceX (uniquely positioned for unlimited orbital energy and compute), and Anthropic (which Bhakdi considers the clear leader in frontier AI, ahead of OpenAI and Google). He argues Anthropic has partially developed AGI/ASI — particularly in coding and design — and is accelerating AI development at a pace no competitor can match. Each party needs the others: Anthropic needs compute and energy, Nvidia needs somewhere to deploy chips at scale with sufficient energy, and SpaceX needs a killer application to monetize orbital energy.

5. **Orbital AI Compute as SpaceX's Core Business Model:** Bhakdi argues the ultimate business opportunity is orbital AI compute — harvesting effectively unlimited solar energy in space and converting it into compute capacity. He predicts orbital compute will begin in earnest within the next 12 months, reach significant scale by 2028, and enter hyperscale before 2030. He frames the Anthropic deal as the first real-world commercial step toward this vision, noting SpaceX is now building a terrestrial-to-orbital compute continuum. Bhakdi states he is updating his internal SpaceX financial model to merge the terrestrial Colossus compute business with the future orbital compute business into a single vertical.

6. **Anthropic's Compute Constraints and Competitive Position:** Bhakdi references rumors that Anthropic withheld a major model release not for safety reasons but because of compute constraints. The Colossus One deal, alongside other partnerships, is Anthropic's solution. He also notes Anthropic is expanding compute internationally to meet data residency requirements in regulated industries (finance, healthcare, government), and has committed to covering consumer electricity price increases caused by its data centers in the US, with plans to extend that commitment internationally.

7. **SpaceX IPO and Tesla Merger Speculation:** Bhakdi briefly discusses the SpaceX IPO, which he believes will be highly hyped and potentially overvalued at launch, and states he is unlikely to buy SpaceX at IPO. He expects the Tesla-SpaceX merger, if it happens, is more likely in 2027 though possibly as early as November 2026. He notes that a higher Tesla stock price (e.g., $500) could complicate the merger economics since a premium would need to be paid on top.

8. **Terafab Capex Update:** Bhakdi briefly mentions that Tesla's Terafab has a newly announced capex plan of $55 billion, which he describes as realistic.

## Robotaxi

1. **Unsupervised Robotaxi Fleet at 36:** During the live Q&A, Bhakdi mentions in passing that the robotaxi counter is "up to 36 unsupervised today," with another two added, calling it "hot stuff." He does not elaborate further in this video.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus and FSD Training Capacity:** In response to a viewer question about whether the SpaceX-Anthropic deal affects FSD and Optimus training capacity, Bhakdi states he does not think there are any problems — Tesla has "enormous capacity now." He also notes that Tesla can build custom chips (via Terafab) for Optimus and robotaxi applications and be very successful at it, even if it cannot displace Nvidia in core training and inference at scale.

## Financials

1. **Pioneer Alpha Portfolio Performance:** Bhakdi shares that the day of the broadcast was the best single day for his Pioneer Alpha portfolio since its inception on January 1, 2024. He attributes approximately 80% of the day's gains to Tesla options/derivatives (short puts), with roughly 10% each from Nvidia and Tesla stock directly, resulting in approximately a 9% portfolio gain on the day. He credits his high-conviction call that Tesla would reach $400 that week as the basis for the leveraged position.

Notable quotes and data:
- Colossus One: 220,000+ Nvidia GPUs, 300 megawatts of capacity, coming online for Anthropic within May 2026
- Anthropic's other compute deals: up to 5-gigawatt agreement with Amazon; 5-gigawatt agreement with Google and Broadcom (online 2027); $30 billion partnership with Microsoft and Nvidia; $50 billion investment with Fluid Stack
- Bhakdi's estimate: "300 megawatts of Colossus are probably at least three times the amount of energy you would need at Tranium chips or even the Google chips to get to the same compute"
- Elon Musk: "I spent a lot of time last week with senior members of the Anthropic team to understand what they do to ensure Claude is good for humanity and was impressed... No one set off my evil detector."
- Elon Musk: "Space X AI had already moved training to Colossus 2" — freeing Colossus One for Anthropic
- Bhakdi's orbital compute timeline: begins in earnest within 12 months, significant scale by 2028, hyperscale before 2030
- Terafab capex plan: $55 billion (newly announced, per Bhakdi)
- Unsupervised robotaxi fleet: 36 as of broadcast date (per RobotaxiTracker.com; Bhakdi cites "up to 36")
- Bhakdi on singularity: "I said early 2025 that we have reached the singularity... I predicted it will be 90% concluded in 2027"
- Pioneer Alpha best day: ~9% gain, ~80% from Tesla derivatives

2026-05-06.title: Daily X Summary (2026-05-06)
2026-05-06.body:
## Executive Summary
Today's posts are dominated by Tesla Semi momentum (two separate fleet orders totaling 390 trucks), strong EV market share data from Norway, and a meaningful FSD regulatory development in Belgium. Secondary themes include a large Megapack deployment in South Australia and Lucid's catastrophic Q1 miss, which underscores Tesla's competitive moat in the EV space. Overall signal is moderately bullish across the EV and energy segments.

---

## Key Posts / Themes

1. **Tesla Semi gains significant commercial traction with two major fleet orders:** Two separate commercial fleet announcements landed on the same day. WattEV announced the deployment of 370 Tesla Semi trucks — described as the largest single electric truck deployment in California — valued at approximately $100 million. The first 50 units are slated for delivery in 2026, with the full fleet completed by end of 2027; over 300 of those trucks will be deployed in California. Separately, Nica Container Freight Line Inc ordered 20 Tesla Semis, with operations expected to begin next year. Combined, these announcements represent 390 trucks in new committed orders in a single day. Sawyer also posted a walk-around video of two redesigned Tesla Semis at the ACT Expo in Las Vegas, noting that Tesla describes the vehicles as "autonomy ready" and that volume production of the redesigned Semi began recently. A software update — the 2026 Spring Update — also enabled European-style semi-truck visualizations in the vehicle's FSD display, suggesting active software development for the platform.

2. **FSD regulatory progress in Belgium:** The Flemish Minister of Mobility, Annick De Ridder, has officially requested that Tesla submit its FSD dossier to the Flemish administration, with explicit instructions to explore a possible fast-track homologation process. This is a notable step toward FSD approval in parts of Belgium and represents one of the more concrete regulatory signals from Europe to date. No approval timeline was specified, but the fast-track language is meaningful.

3. **Tesla dominates Norway Q1 2026 sales; BEV market share hits 97.9%:** The Tesla Model Y was the #1 best-selling vehicle overall in Norway in Q1 2026 with 5,406 units — outselling the next five non-Tesla vehicles combined. The Model 3 ranked #2. BEVs overall captured a 97.9% market share in Norway during the quarter, reinforcing Tesla's positioning in the most EV-saturated major market globally.

4. **$225M Megapack project announced in South Australia:** Construction is set to begin soon on a 200MW / 800MWh Tesla Megapack battery energy storage system in Koolunga, South Australia, valued at $225 million. The project is being developed and operated by Equis Development, with commissioning scheduled for September 2027. This is a large-scale deployment that adds to Tesla's Energy segment pipeline.

5. **Tesla Australia: battery storage dominates revenue mix:** Tesla Australia reported its first revenues ($3M) from Australia's new vehicle emissions standards. More notably, battery storage accounted for 55% of Tesla's Australian-sourced revenue in 2025, highlighting how dominant the Energy segment has become in that market relative to vehicle sales.

6. **Lucid Q1 2026 earnings signal continued EV competitive weakness:** Lucid reported a severe Q1 2026 earnings miss — revenue of $282M vs. $440M expected, a net loss of -$1 billion, and a loss per share of -$3.46 vs. -$2.64 expected. Lucid said it plans to reduce production due to elevated vehicle inventories. While not directly a Tesla data point, this reinforces Tesla's dominant position and the difficulty competitors face in scaling profitably.

7. **Cybertruck lease price increase:** Tesla raised Cybertruck Premium AWD lease prices in the U.S. by approximately 10–12%. The new monthly rates are $1,100/month with $0 down (up ~10%) and $949/month with $5,000 down (up ~12%). Cyberbeast pricing remained unchanged. The direction of the change (upward) may suggest improved demand or margin management on the Cybertruck line.

8. **Tesla battery certificate feature and Model S/X Signature Edition:** Tesla is developing an in-app certificate feature for high-voltage battery repairs or replacements, intended to improve resale value and buyer confidence in the used market. Separately, official Model S/X Signature Edition badge and animation assets were revealed, suggesting a limited edition variant is in preparation — though no pricing or availability details were disclosed.

---

## Signal Strength: **Bullish** — Tesla Semi is gaining real commercial momentum with nearly 400 trucks committed in a single day, FSD is making tangible regulatory progress in Europe, and Tesla's energy and EV dominance in key markets remains intact while competitors struggle.

2026-05-06.title: Tesla's 'Battery Shortage' Mystery Solved (It wasn't the 4680)
2026-05-06.body:
This video by Jordan Giesige of The Limiting Factor investigates the "battery shortage" Tesla has intermittently referenced over the past year, revealing that the constraint is not a cell supply problem but rather battery *pack* assembly capacity. The core thesis is that Tesla is deliberately creating a temporary, self-imposed bottleneck by upgrading and insourcing battery pack production across multiple factories — a strategic move to reduce costs and improve margins in an increasingly competitive EV market.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Battery Pack Assembly — Not Cells — Is the Bottleneck:** In Q1's earnings call, Tesla CFO Vaibhav clarified that the limiting factor is battery pack capacity, not the cells themselves (i.e., not the 4680 or LFP cell production lines). This resolved widespread speculation that the 4680 ramp was causing the constraint. Lars reinforced this, noting that new capacity is actively being added across multiple facilities and that the situation is expected to improve over the coming months.

2. **Giga Berlin Shifting to In-House 4680 Cells:** At Giga Berlin, Tesla has launched a Model Y battery pack using in-house 4680 cells produced in the United States. This is described as ramping up and contributing to Berlin's output, helping meet the demand surge seen in Europe. These cells are cheaper than third-party alternatives both because they eliminate supplier margins and because Tesla receives a $35 per kilowatt-hour production tax credit on them.

3. **Giga Nevada Production Line Upgrades:** At Giga Nevada, Tesla is retooling battery pack production lines that were originally stood up in 2017–2018 — nearly a decade old. The upgrades are expected to yield higher production rates and lower production costs, and may also include improvements to the battery pack design itself.

4. **Giga Shanghai Insourcing LFP Modules from Sunwoda Cells:** At Giga Shanghai, Tesla has begun purchasing battery cells from Sunwoda (rather than CATL) and assembling the modules in-house. Previously, CATL supplied both cells and modules. The Sunwoda cells are expected to be cheaper than CATL's, and in-house module assembly should provide additional cost savings.

5. **Vehicle Backlog and Future Sales Upside:** Tesla exited Q1 with its highest vehicle backlog in over two years. Once the battery pack bottleneck is resolved, Jordan argues this should translate into higher vehicle sales in upcoming quarters and potentially new highs for total vehicle deliveries.

6. **Strategic Cost Reduction Thesis:** Jordan frames all three factory initiatives as part of a unified strategy: by reducing costs on the battery pack — the most expensive assembly in the vehicle — Tesla can either lower vehicle prices to compete more aggressively or capture the savings as higher margin.

## Energy

1. **Megapack Q1 Deployments Down Sharply:** Tesla's energy storage deployments in Q1 came in at 8.8 GWh, a 38% reduction from 14.2 GWh in Q4 2025. Tesla attributed the decline to the lumpy nature of the energy storage business, which is subject to customer project timelines and construction schedules.

2. **Megapack Gross Margins Hit All-Time High — But for the Wrong Reason:** Megapack gross margins reached an all-time high in Q1, but Jordan notes this was driven by adjustments related to tariffs paid in prior quarters rather than organic operational improvement. Tesla is guiding that Megapack gross margins should be expected to decline in future quarters due to increased competition and tariff impacts.

3. **Megapack U.S. Domestic Cell Supply and Future Cost Trajectory:** For U.S.-bound Megapacks, Tesla plans to increasingly use domestic LFP battery cells to avoid tariffs, though production costs will initially be higher domestically. Jordan notes that this cost dynamic could change in the future if Tesla brings prismatic LFP cell production in-house using lithium from its Corpus Christi refinery, LFP cathode material from Austin, and its dry electrode coating process.

4. **Megapack 3 Coming to Houston Later in 2026:** Tesla reaffirmed that Megapack 3 production will begin later this year in Houston, Texas. Jordan characterizes Megapack 3 as a more competitive product than Megapack 2.

5. **Giga Shanghai Megapack Capacity Listing Anomaly:** In Tesla's Q1 quarterly report, Giga Shanghai's Megapack production capacity was listed as 20 GWh, down from the usual 40 GWh figure. Tesla made no comment on this change during the earnings call. Jordan flags it as potentially worth raising at the next earnings call, but notes it doesn't appear significant given Tesla's reaffirmed strong demand and production outlook.

Notable quotes and data:
- **Vaibhav (Tesla CFO):** *"At the moment, I think the limiter is not the cells itself, it's the battery pack capacity. Like I said in my opening remarks, we're actively working on resolving this. There's more capacity being added as we speak."*
- **Lars (Tesla):** *"We started launching a Model Y battery pack with our in-house 4680 cells a few months ago, and that is ramping up nicely, adding to Berlin's output and helping with the demand surge that we've seen in Europe."*
- **Lars (Tesla):** *"We're adding additional capacity in our Reno facility, sort of retooling it as it's been building packs now for almost 10 years."*
- Q1 energy storage deployments: **8.8 GWh** (vs. 14.2 GWh in Q4 2025 — a **38% decline**)
- Megapack gross margins: **All-time high in Q1**, but driven by prior-quarter tariff adjustments
- 4680 in-house cell production tax credit: **$35 per kilowatt-hour**
- Tesla exited Q1 with its **highest vehicle backlog in over 2 years**
- Giga Nevada pack lines originally stood up in **2017–2018**
- Megapack 3 production to begin **later in 2026** in **Houston, Texas**
- Giga Shanghai Megapack capacity listed as **20 GWh** in Q1 report vs. the usual **40 GWh**

2026-05-06.title: Tesla's Robotaxi Just Did Something Insane!
2026-05-06.body:
This week's episode from The Tesla Space covers a range of technology and space news, with the central Tesla-related focus on the rapid expansion of Tesla's unsupervised robotaxi fleet in Texas and the milestone of FSD surpassing 10 billion supervised miles. The video also covers the Tesla Semi's new charging infrastructure program, Neuralink's automated surgical robot, and SpaceX's Mars colony compensation plan for Elon Musk. The core thesis is that Tesla's data-driven FSD strategy is now bearing fruit in real-world autonomous deployments, with exponential fleet growth beginning to materialize.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD Hits 10 Billion Supervised Miles:** Tesla's supervised Full Self-Driving has now accumulated over 10 billion real-world miles. The video frames this as a critical threshold — Elon Musk's 2016 Master Plan Part Two originally estimated that approximately 6 billion miles of data would be needed to demonstrate that FSD is safer than the average human driver and unlock broader regulatory approval globally. With 10 billion miles now logged, Tesla has substantially exceeded that original benchmark.

2. **Regulatory Progress in Europe and China:** In the Netherlands, the RDW (the country's official vehicle regulator) has formally approved Full Self-Driving supervised, stating that when used properly with driver monitoring in place, the system is safer than other driver assistance systems and makes a positive contribution to road safety. In China, Tesla has secured partial approval for a supervised FSD release, with early owner feedback described as very positive and broader rollout still in progress.

3. **California Robotaxi Accountability Rules:** California has clarified how autonomous vehicles will be handled when they violate traffic laws. Starting July 1, 2026, robotaxis in California will be ticketed like any other vehicle — if they run a red light or fail to stop for pedestrians, the company managing the vehicle will be liable for the fine. California DMV Director Steve Gordon framed the new rule as enhancing public safety, transparency, and accountability for AV manufacturers.

## Robotaxi

1. **Rapid Unsupervised Fleet Expansion in Texas:** Tesla has expanded its robotaxi operations beyond Austin to include Houston and Dallas, Texas. According to community tracking data from RobotaxiTracker.com, approximately 36 fully unsupervised Model Y vehicles are now operating across these Texas cities. The video highlights a fleet growth chart showing an initial rollout in early 2026, followed by a period of stagnation, then a resumption of growth in early April 2026, culminating in a near-vertical acceleration in fleet size in the weeks prior to the video — described as "what the beginning of exponential growth looks like."

2. **Night Operations Now Active:** The unsupervised Tesla robotaxi fleet in Texas has extended its operating hours into nighttime driving. The video notes that night driving presents distinct challenges for a vision-only system — reduced visibility, headlight glare, and harder-to-detect objects — making the extension of night operations a meaningful signal of Tesla's confidence in FSD's around-the-clock performance.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Tesla Semi Efficiency and Cost Advantage:** The Tesla Semi is rated at under 1.7 kWh per mile. Real-world tests from companies including DHL and PepsiCo indicate it is approximately three times more efficient than a diesel truck. This translates to an operating cost of roughly 23 cents per mile for the Semi, compared to over 80 cents per mile for a traditional diesel rig — a major cost advantage for high-mileage commercial fleets.

2. **New Semi Charging for Business Program:** Tesla is launching a structured charging infrastructure program for Semi fleet operators. The Megacharger delivers 1.2 megawatts of power, enabling the Semi to recover approximately 60% of its range in 30 minutes — aligning with mandatory rest break requirements for truck drivers. A lower-cost base charger is arriving in early 2027, delivering 125 kilowatts of power and priced at around $40,000 for two units. The base charger is designed for overnight depot charging, and Tesla will handle maintenance, network operations, and driver support for both charger types under the program.

Notable quotes and data:
- FSD supervised: **10 billion miles** accumulated
- Elon Musk's original data threshold estimate (2016 Master Plan Part Two): **~6 billion miles**
- Unsupervised robotaxi fleet (Texas cities): **~36 Model Y vehicles** per RobotaxiTracker.com
- Tesla Semi energy consumption: **under 1.7 kWh per mile**
- Tesla Semi operating cost: **~23 cents per mile** vs. **over 80 cents per mile** for diesel
- Semi efficiency vs. diesel (real-world DHL/PepsiCo tests): **~3x more efficient**
- Megacharger output: **1.2 megawatts**, recovers ~60% range in **30 minutes**
- Base charger output: **125 kW**, cost: **~$40,000 for two units**, arriving **early 2027**
- California robotaxi ticketing rule effective: **July 1, 2026**
- SpaceX compensation targets: **$7.5 trillion valuation** and **1 million-person Mars colony**; award includes **200 million super voting restricted shares**

2026-05-07.title: Tesla Just Dropped Multiple Big Signals
2026-05-07.body:
This video from "brighterwithherbert" features host Herbert and guest Brian White (of the FutureAzA YouTube channel) breaking down five major Tesla-related developments from the week: the SpaceX Terafab chip fabrication filing, the Boring Company's Nashville residential loop agreement, a rumored FSD version rollout in China, new Roadster trademark filings, and a new tiered Model Y lease structure. The core thesis is that Tesla and its ecosystem companies are accelerating on multiple fronts simultaneously, reinforcing a long-term bull case centered on autonomous driving, infrastructure, and vehicle affordability.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Rumored FSD Version 14.3.2 Push to Employees in China:** According to a rumor circulating online, Tesla may have pushed FSD version 14.3.2 — described as "full functionality" — to its employees in China. Brian White notes that FSD rollout in China has been delayed from an expected March launch due to unresolved government regulatory hurdles. He explains that China must train on locally sourced and processed data, and that the driving style there differs significantly from the US. White recounts that Xiaomi engineers who conducted head-to-head comparisons told him that Chinese FSD (running version 13) is not on par with US FSD, which they described as "just about flawless." He suggests that if the rumor is true and employees are receiving the latest version, it signals the Chinese government may be preparing to approve a wider rollout — which would unlock a significant new recurring revenue stream for Tesla.

2. **Boring Company Nashville Loop to Use FSD:** The Boring Company has signed its first residential loop station agreement in Nashville, covering luxury towers at Prime Al Cove and Paramount Towers in downtown Nashville. Residents will take an elevator directly to an underground loop station, board a Tesla, and reach the airport in 9 minutes or Lower Broadway in 2 minutes. Herbert notes that the Boring Company has already begun testing Tesla Full Self-Driving inside its Las Vegas loop (as of October), with the car running robotaxi software on version 14. The Nashville project is described as privately funded, with first segments targeted for late 2026. Brian White emphasizes the economic model: the Boring Company asks only for permits and land at terminal endpoints, then recoups its investment through fares — a model made viable because its tunneling costs (targeting ~$50 million per mile) are a fraction of traditional subway construction ($500 million to $2 billion per mile).

3. **FSD Subscriber Growth and Version 14 Momentum:** Herbert mentions that Tesla gained another 170,000 FSD subscribers, describing this as a small but persistent and growing revenue stream. He and Brian White both express enthusiasm for FSD version 14, with White suggesting it may be time for Tesla to offer another free one-month trial given how good the software has become.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **New Five-Tier Model Y Lease Structure:** Tesla has rolled out a new flexible five-tier Model Y lease. The entry-level standard rear-wheel drive starts at $459/month, the dual motor all-wheel drive at $499/month, a premium tier at $569/month, premium all-wheel drive at $669/month, and the performance variant at $799/month — all requiring just over $4,000 at signing. Brian White highlights the competitiveness of these numbers by citing a comparison in which a Model 3 standard lease on a 48-month, 10,000-mile-per-year, zero-down basis came in at $299/month — cheaper than a comparable Toyota Camry or Honda Civic lease — while also saving nearly as much in fuel costs as the monthly payment itself.

2. **Leasing as a Robotaxi Pipeline Strategy:** Both hosts discuss the strategic logic of Tesla's lease pricing: by offering attractive terms, Tesla gets cars into consumers' hands with low upfront commitments, then reclaims those vehicles at lease-end (typically 3–4 years, ~30,000–40,000 miles on the odometer) and redeploys them into the robotaxi fleet. White notes this strategy dates to 2018 Model 3 leases, which contractually prevented buyers from keeping the cars. At that time, the robotaxi fleet wasn't ready, so Tesla sold the returned cars as near-new, effectively collecting margin twice. White frames this as a plan that works whether or not the robotaxi deployment is ready at lease-end.

3. **Canada's Affordable Model 3 and Model Y L Spotted in the US:** Brian White highlights a newly introduced Canadian-market rear-wheel drive Model 3 Premium priced at CAD $39,000 (approximately USD $29,000), calling it cheaper than anything "remotely comparable" even before factoring in fuel savings. Separately, White mentions that a camouflaged Model Y L (long version) was spotted in the United States, which he views as a positive signal that the vehicle may arrive sooner than Elon Musk's stated "end of year" timeline — White had publicly predicted a first-half 2026 arrival.

4. **Model Y Five-Star ANCAP Safety Rating:** The refreshed Model Y received a five-star safety rating from ANCAP (the Australian equivalent of Euro NCAP).
