2026-05-10.title: Daily X Summary (2026-05-10)
2026-05-10.body:
## Executive Summary
Today's posts from @SawyerMerritt were relatively light on high-conviction Tesla investment signals, with the most notable items being a new FSD V14.3 safety behavior (slippery weather detection), an impressive FSD V14 demonstration in Europe, and a new UK Renewable Energy Bundle from Tesla. The Model S/X Signature Edition delivery event postponement and the Frost Blue Model 3 Performance rollout were notable EV updates. Overall, the day's content skews mildly bullish on FSD progress and Tesla's energy bundling strategy, with no major robotaxi or Optimus data points.

---

## Key Posts / Themes

1. **FSD V14.3 Adds Slippery Weather Detection:** Sawyer reported his first personal experience with a new safety behavior in FSD V14.3, where the system detects potential hydroplaning surfaces and automatically limits the vehicle to Standard mode (or below) and caps the maximum speed at 70 mph. This is a meaningful incremental safety feature that addresses real-world adverse weather conditions — a gap critics have historically flagged in FSD. Separately, a viral FSD V14 clip showed the system correctly stopping for a hand signal, and another post highlighted what Sawyer described as one of the more impressive FSD videos from Europe, suggesting the European rollout is generating strong user content. Together, these posts reinforce a narrative of continued FSD capability maturation across safety-critical edge cases and new geographies.

2. **Tesla Launches UK Renewable Energy Bundle:** Tesla introduced a "Renewable Energy Bundle" in the UK combining Tesla Solar and Powerwall 3 for £199/month (including installation, 0% interest). Tesla is also offering a combined package with a Model 3 for £494/month. The offer appears targeted at existing Tesla owners. This is a notable bundling strategy that could drive cross-product attach rates in a key European market, tying together Tesla's energy and automotive businesses in a subscription-like structure.

3. **Model S/X Signature Edition Delivery Event Postponed:** Tesla has postponed the previously scheduled May 12th delivery event for the Model S/X Signature Edition. No new date has been announced. While not elaborated on by Sawyer, the postponement may signal logistics, production, or product readiness issues, and is worth monitoring for rescheduling updates.

4. **Frost Blue Model 3 Performance Rolling Out:** Sawyer shared up-close images of the new Frost Blue color on the Model 3 Performance, noting that car haulers have already been spotted transporting large numbers of them, suggesting showroom deliveries are imminent. This is a positive demand-side signal for Model 3 refresh momentum.

5. **"Getting Closer to the First V3 Launch":** Sawyer posted a brief, vague teaser — "Getting closer to the first V3 launch!" — without specifying what product or version "V3" refers to. Given the context of adjacent posts (FSD versioning, Model 3, energy), this could relate to a hardware or software version, but no further detail was provided. This is low-signal until clarified.

6. **Optimus Head as a Gift (Low Signal):** A post shared a video of an Optimus head being given as a gift. While attention-grabbing, this contains no substantive product, capability, or manufacturing data.

7. **SpaceX "SpaceXAI" Trademark (Tangential):** SpaceX filed a trademark for "SpaceXAI" covering satellite-based data center services, orbital computing infrastructure, cloud computing, and AI SaaS. This is a SpaceX — not Tesla — development, but is worth flagging for investors who track Elon Musk's broader ecosystem and any potential future interplay between xAI, SpaceX compute infrastructure, and Tesla's AI training needs.

---

## Signal Strength: **Mildly Bullish** — FSD V14.3 is demonstrating meaningful safety improvements (weather detection, hand signal recognition, European performance), and Tesla's UK energy bundle reflects a maturing cross-product strategy, but no major robotaxi fleet, Optimus, or financial data points emerged today.

2026-05-11.title: Weekly Tesla Brief (May 4 – May 10, 2026)
2026-05-11.body:
## Unsupervised Robotaxi Fleet

| City | Now | 7D | 30D |
|:-----|----:|---:|----:|
| Austin | 28 | +7 | +18 |
| Houston | 6 | 0 | +6 |
| Dallas | 5 | 0 | +5 |
| **Total** | **39** | +7 | +29 |

Source: [RobotaxiTracker.com](https://robotaxitracker.com/)

---

## Brief

- FSD 14.3.2 rolling wide on HW4; navigation regression confirmed in real-world review.
- Cybercab FMVSS-compliant; production ~20 units/day begun in April at Giga Texas.
- Tesla Semi high-volume Nevada line live; 430+ units ordered in one week at ACT Expo.
- Model S/X discontinued; Fremont converting to Optimus production this summer.
- 45X tax credit lost — ~$400M/year — due to new PFE rules on imported CATL cells.
- EU FSD bloc vote missed May 5; next window June 30; Belgium fast-tracking independently.
- Cybertruck PCS2 board failures widespread across tens of thousands of VINs.

## Autonomous Driving

- **FSD 14.3.2 is a split verdict.** Vehicle control — merging, lane selection, pedestrian handling — described as "exceptional" with edge cases increasingly rare. But navigation regressed: one reviewer's vehicle looped a bank parking lot entrance three times before entering, behavior confirmed as new. Verdict: "The navigation has absolutely gotten worse." The build reached ~50–60% of the HW4 consumer fleet by mid-week; full rollout expected within one to two weeks.

- **FSD 14.3's architectural significance.** The update rewrote the AI compiler and runtime using MLRI, targeting ~36 guaranteed inference cycles per second and producing an estimated reaction time of ~0.2 seconds — versus the ~1.5-second human standard. The rewrite also established a reinforcement learning pipeline enabling rapid field-issue fine-tuning from real robotaxi incidents. Per Tesla's Q1 earnings call, Ashok confirmed the robotaxi fleet runs a variant of the 14.3 series likely ahead of the consumer build.

- **EU FSD: no May 5 vote; June 30 is the next window.** Dutch regulator RDW presented 18 months and 1 million miles of FSD data to all 27 EU member states at a Brussels TCMV meeting; regulators raised objections around speed limits, wildlife hazards, icy roads, and the "Full Self-Driving" name. Bhakdi assigns 30–50% probability to a bloc-wide pass; his base case is rejection followed by individual-country approvals. Belgium's Flemish minister formally requested Tesla's dossier and instructed her administration to explore rapid homologation. Denmark's authority publicly contradicted a Reuters report claiming skepticism, stating it had issued no official position.

- **NHTSA is running a concurrent Engineering Analysis on ~3.2 million Tesla vehicles**, the stage typically preceding a recall, focused on FSD camera failures in sun glare and fog and potential underreporting of related crashes. This runs in parallel with the 2026 Model Y becoming the first vehicle to pass all eight NHTSA NCAP ADAS evaluations, including four new criteria added for MY2026.

- **Consumer unsupervised FSD targeted Q4 2026 or Q1 2027.** Elon on the Q1 earnings call suggested FSD version 15 — described as featuring a model ~10x larger than the current small model — may be needed before truly scaled unsupervised consumer deployment.

## Robotaxi

- **Cybercab confirmed FMVSS-compliant from day one** per Tesla's head of engineering. This eliminates the NHTSA 2,500-vehicle annual exemption cap as a ceiling risk for the purpose-built driverless vehicle — production ramp at Giga Texas is now constrained by manufacturing, not regulation. Production began in April 2026 at approximately 20 units/day, with ~40–50 units documented near the factory.

- **Unsupervised expansion: Dallas and Houston are 100% driverless.** Both cities launched directly into unsupervised service with no prior ride-hail supervised phase. Austin's remaining supervised vehicles are expected to convert within approximately 10 days. Per Brian Wang, the Texas triangle could reach 300+ unsupervised vehicles by end of June. The operational binding constraint is now software orchestration (pickup/drop-off behavior, remote ops frequency) rather than safety performance.

- **Paid robotaxi miles tripled quarter-over-quarter**: ~1.7 million miles in Q1 2026, up from ~610,000 in Q4 2025. Farzad projects Q2 could exceed 4 million and Q3 could approach 10 million paid miles.

- **Five additional city launches committed for H1 2026:** Phoenix, Miami, Orlando, Tampa, and Las Vegas. Field response specialist hiring is active in Las Vegas and Doral, Florida — the same pre-launch role Tesla staffed ahead of Dallas and Houston. California unsupervised service is unlikely before 2027; Tesla has not applied for a CPUC AV permit and faces a 6–9 month processing window once it does.

- **California AV traffic law takes effect July 1, 2026.** Law enforcement may issue citations directly to AV manufacturers; accumulated violations can restrict or suspend driverless operating licenses. A separate 50,000-mile pre-commercial safety test is required.

## Optimus

- **Model S/X production discontinued; Fremont line converting to Optimus manufacturing.** The factory conversion is a deliberate reallocation of production capacity — a formal signal Tesla has transitioned its strategic identity from car company to physical AI company. Fremont targets 1M units/year; Giga Texas targets 10M units/year. V3 production is set to begin summer 2026; 2027–2028 targets are 100,000–300,000 units across both facilities at a cost target of $20,000–$25,000/unit.

- **Optimus reveal expected within 90 days per Bhakdi**, who describes it as a major soft catalyst. Tesla has maintained a communications blackout on Optimus citing competitive intelligence concerns — Elon cited frame-by-frame copying by rivals. A "paused production line to retool for faster assembly" news item was read as active development signal, not a setback.

- **Optimus supply chain does not yet exist.** Elon on the Q3 earnings call: "With humanoid robots, there is no supply chain." Tesla is building actuators, sensors, hands, and forearms internally; Elon described the hand and forearm as "more difficult than the entire rest of the robot." The Etherloop (Ethernet-based time-division multiplexing developed for Cybercab) will apply directly to Optimus limb control architecture.

- **AI5 chip is a hard prerequisite for meaningful Optimus production**, per Phil Biceel. AI5 delivers 2,500 TOPS and 144 GB memory — up to 40x system-level improvement over HW4. Elon's roadmap: AI4 achieves safety far beyond human levels; AI5 makes cars "almost perfect"; AI6 targets Optimus and data centers.

## Tesla Semi

- **High-volume production line is live at Giga Nevada.** The first unit came off the dedicated facility on April 29; the 1.7 million sq ft Sparks plant is designed for 50,000 trucks/year. Analyst 2026 delivery estimates range from 5,000 to 15,000 units. CARB regulatory filings confirmed specs: 822 kWh (Long Range) and 548 kWh (Standard Range), both NCMA/4680 chemistry; LR achieves 500 miles at 82,000 lb GCW.

- **430+ units ordered at ACT Expo.** Watt EV: 370 units (~$100M), first 50 in 2026. Big F Transport: 40 units after a single demo. NA Container Freight Lines: 20 units, first operating 2027. Semi pricing is 25–35% below competing electric Class 8 trucks ($400K–$500K range); official pricing confirmed at $290,000 LR / $260,000 SR.

- **New charging suite removes depot infrastructure barrier.** Mega Charger: 1.2 MW, 60% in 30 minutes, ~$188,000 per two-post setup, 66 planned locations across 15 states. Base Charger: 125 kW, 60% overnight, ~$40,000 installed for two units, daisy-chainable on a single breaker. Jordan (The Limiting Factor): "I'm no longer concerned that the charging network will be the rate-limiting factor for semi production."

- **Incentives make economics compelling.** Washington State WEZI program: up to $175,000 rebate, reducing the LR Semi to ~$115,000. California HVIP: $120,000–$330,000 per truck with $100M+ available. Tesla Semi captured 965 of 1,067 California clean truck voucher applications between January 2025 and February 2026.

## Energy

- **Tesla loses ~$400M/year 45X tax credit in 2026.** IRS Notice 2026-15 introduced Prohibited Foreign Entity rules; Tesla's use of imported CATL cells at the Lathrop Megapack factory immediately exceeds the PFE allowance, eliminating the $10/kWh module assembly credit. Nevada LFP factory expected to restore eligibility — but ~99% of LFP cathode supply is China-based, creating a substantial compliance hurdle even after the domestic line opens.

- **Q1 2026 energy gross margin of ~39% included non-recurring tariff benefits.** Management flagged the record margin reflected "tariff recognitions"; Benchmark's Iola Hughes describes the most likely explanation as an overpayment during tariff turbulence — not a recurring benefit.

- **Giga-scale project pipeline accelerating sharply.** Q1 2026 saw 11 projects over 1 GWh come online; the full-year 2026 pipeline stands at 122 projects, versus 50 in all of 2025 and 17 in 2024. Australia became the second-largest global market with over 8 GWh installed in Q1 alone. Ex-China markets grew ~112% year-over-year in Q1.

- **Chinese competition intensifying.** BYD took top global energy storage shipment rank in 2025. Chinese competitors deploy systems in China at under $100/kWh versus Tesla's ~$190–$200/kWh — a structural gap in unprotected markets. Hughes: "Tesla's potentially lagging some of what we see from the Chinese players." Powin, previously the third-largest US integrator, declared bankruptcy.

## Electric Vehicles

- **Record April China deliveries: 79,478 units, +36% YoY** — best April ever for China operations. South Korea posted a record 13,190 units, outselling BMW and Mercedes combined. Germany posted its best April ever. Model Y confirmed as the world's best-selling EV in March 2026; Tesla passed BYD in Q1 2026 overall.

- **Canada Model 3 RWD (Giga Shanghai) priced at ~CAD $39,990 (~USD $29,000)** — enabled by Canada's quota mechanism allowing ~49,000 Chinese-built vehicles at 6% import tariff in 2026. Delivery estimates slipped from June to October on strong order intake; Chinese EV brands have no Canadian sales infrastructure to compete for the quota this year.

- **New five-tier Model Y lease starting at $459/month.** Tesla reclaims vehicles at lease-end (~30,000–40,000 miles) and redeploys them into the robotaxi fleet — a model generating margin twice regardless of robotaxi readiness at return. Model Y L mule spotted in the US with an unveil possible within 60 days; deliveries projected ~October 2026 at ~$55,000–$60,000.

- **Cybertruck Frost Blue and Model 3 Marine Blue launched.** Model S/X Signature Edition delivery event — originally scheduled May 12 — postponed with no new date announced.

## Financials

- **Tesla guided to negative free cash flow for the remainder of 2026.** Capital commitments include Terafab ($55B upfront, $119B total), xAI's Colossus 2 supercomputer ($18B in chips), and the Optimus supply chain buildout. Terafab is jointly owned by Tesla, xAI, SpaceX, and Intel; a Grimes County public hearing is scheduled for early June 2026.

- **FSD Europe perpetual purchase ends May 21, 2026** across UK, Germany, France, Italy, Belgium, Switzerland, Denmark, and other markets — shifting to subscription-only and converting one-time revenue to recurring ARR.

- **Bhakdi DCF: ~$600/share intrinsic value for 2026**, explicitly conditioned on 10,000 robotaxis deployed by year-end. He pushed original model timelines back 12–18 months from earlier projections. Stock up ~11% on the week, closing above its 200-day moving average (~$402–$404).

## Market & Competition

- **xAI dissolved; folded into SpaceX as "SpaceX AI."** Colossus 1 (~220,000 Nvidia GPUs, ~300 MW) leased to Anthropic for inference; Colossus 2 remains dedicated to Grok training. Larry Goldberg estimates the combined SpaceX entity could show ~$20B in profit in its first year. SpaceX–Tesla merger speculation is at ~70% on Polymarket; Sawyer Merritt characterized it as "purely speculation" with no confirmed timeline.

- **Goldman Sachs: autonomous trucking is a $560B market by 2035**, larger than the $415B robotaxi market. Autonomous truck cost per mile projected to fall from $8.56 today to ~$2.30 by 2035, with crossover versus human-driven trucks around 2028.

- **Waymo projected to lose ~$5B in 2026 — roughly $100 per ride** across ~52 million annual rides. Morgan Stanley pegs Tesla's robotaxi cost per mile at ~$0.81 versus Waymo's ~$1.36–$1.43. Multiple analysts argue Waymo must abandon its LiDAR/HD-mapping architecture entirely to reach viable unit economics.

- **BYD April 2026 passenger EV sales: ~314,000 units, -15.7% YoY** — eighth consecutive month of domestic China decline. Domestic rivals Xiaomi, Leap Motor, and Zeekr posted new monthly highs.

## Bear Case of the Week

- **FSD 14.3.2 navigation confirmed regressing.** A real-world review found the vehicle looping a bank parking lot entrance three times — behavior a passenger confirmed "didn't used to" happen. The reviewer's verdict: "The navigation has absolutely gotten worse." This is a concrete regression, not a framing complaint, in a build that has reached ~50–60% of the HW4 consumer fleet.

- **NHTSA Engineering Analysis covers ~3.2 million Tesla vehicles**, the stage typically preceding a recall, specifically focused on FSD's camera system failing in sun glare and fog and potential underreporting of related crashes. Running concurrently with the positive NCAP result — the duality is a material regulatory risk.

- **4680 "8L" pack quietly substituted in European Model Y without disclosure.** The swap cuts WLTP range 52 km (−8%) versus the LG 5M pack it replaced in the same Premium Long Range RWD trim, with slower charging (155 kW curve already declining at 31% SOC, ranked worst in the current EU lineup). Consumer backlash triggered cancellations in France and Norway. South Korean cathode supplier L&F confirmed the scale of 4680 commercial disappointment: a $2.9B Tesla contract written down to $7,386 (−99.9%), citing "change in supply quantity."

- **Cybertruck PCS2 board failures widespread.** Failures documented across a wide VIN range with concentration between VINs 25,000–35,000; the board manages AC charging, Supercharging, and PowerShare. Charge rate drops silently from 48A to 24A with no driver alert. Out-of-warranty repair cost was $4,000–$7,000 before Tesla offered a goodwill rate of ~$1,000; parts are backordered 4–8 weeks. Per Craig (Red Review): "There needs to be a recall on this part." 2024–2025 trucks are covered only by the standard 4-year/50,000-mile warranty, which many high-mileage owners have already exceeded.

- **45X credit loss of ~$400M/year is effective immediately in 2026** due to PFE rules triggered by CATL cell imports at Lathrop. The Nevada LFP line that could restore eligibility faces a further obstacle: ~99% of LFP cathode supply is currently China-based, and cathode accounts for ~40% of cell cost — meaning domestic manufacturing alone does not resolve the compliance gap.

- **Tesla guided to negative free cash flow for the remainder of 2026** while simultaneously absorbing Terafab ($55B upfront), Colossus 2 ($18B in chips), and the Optimus supply chain — with Q1's record energy gross margin

2026-05-11.title: The 5 Questions Every Tesla Investor Is Asking Now
2026-05-11.body:
This video features host "brighterwithherbert" interviewing Larry Goldberg, a serial entrepreneur and active venture capital investor, to address the five key questions Tesla investors are asking. The conversation covers Tesla's auto sales rebound, the robotaxi rollout, the SpaceX IPO as a major catalyst, and the biggest underpriced catalyst for Tesla stock. Larry's core thesis is that Tesla stock will surpass its all-time high this year, driven primarily by a successful SpaceX IPO rather than any specific robotaxi fleet milestone.

## Electric Vehicles
1. **Auto Sales Rebound Is Real But Modest:** Larry characterizes Tesla's auto business as a mature, legacy business undergoing modest growth rather than explosive expansion. He expects new form factors (such as an enlarged Model Y in the US), continued evolution of the Cybertruck, and new models tied to the robotaxi fleet and a "robo van." He does not view the auto business as Tesla's growth engine, but sees it as a stable, cash-flow-generating foundation that underpins the robotaxi business.

2. **Strong Regional Sales Data Cited:** The host highlights specific April sales data: China up 36% (described as its highest ever), Denmark up 102%, Sweden up 111%, and France up 112% in volume of Tesla car sales. Larry acknowledges the rebound is real and timely, coinciding with FSD rollout and the early stages of robotaxi scaling.

3. **Full Self-Driving as a Demand Driver:** Both the host and Larry agree that FSD is already becoming a demand driver for vehicle sales, even without significant marketing or advertising. Larry argues that once broader awareness of FSD's capabilities spreads — as it is beginning to do in Europe — a massive shift in consumer demand will follow. Larry frames the shift as Tesla no longer selling cars but selling self-driving capability, with the car model being a secondary choice.

4. **FSD's Competitive Advantage Is Time-Limited:** Larry notes that FSD is currently roughly three to four years ahead of the market, but cautions that this advantage will erode over that same timeframe. He therefore argues Tesla's true long-term business is robotaxi, not FSD itself, which he sees as years — potentially a decade — ahead of competitors as a business model.

## Robotaxi
1. **No Magic Fleet Number for Stock Movement:** Larry pushes back on the idea that a specific unsupervised robotaxi fleet size — whether 500, 1,000, or surpassing Waymo's scale of roughly 3,000 vehicles — will trigger a stock re-rating. He argues there is instead a singular "magic moment" of public realization, similar to the moment during Tesla's production hell when registration data began moving despite widespread skepticism. The precipitating fact of that moment is unpredictable and cannot be engineered by hitting a particular milestone number.

2. **Robotaxi Scaling Not Expected to Be Complete This Year:** Larry explicitly states he does not believe robotaxi will be "scaled" by end of 2026, contrary to some investor expectations. He anticipates continuous and ongoing progress but cautions against expecting a fully scaled network within the year. The host references a current figure of approximately 38 unsupervised robotaxis, and Larry suggests the fleet may be in the range of 100 to 200 by the time the SpaceX IPO occurs.

3. **Unsupervised Personal Use as an Underpriced Catalyst:** The host references a Piper Sandler thesis that unsupervised personal use — the ability for existing Tesla owners to use their personal vehicles in a fully driverless capacity — is the biggest catalyst not yet priced into the stock. Larry acknowledges Piper Sandler's deep market knowledge on this point but personally ranks the SpaceX IPO as a larger near-term catalyst.

## Humanoid Bots
1. **Optimus Expected to Show Meaningful Capability by Q3–Q4 2026:** Larry states he expects Optimus to "really roll out" and demonstrate genuine capability by the third or fourth quarter of 2026, describing it as one of several simultaneous catalysts — alongside robotaxi progress and the SpaceX IPO — that could drive Tesla's stock higher this year.

## Market & Competition
1. **SpaceX IPO as the Single Biggest Tesla Stock Catalyst of 2026:** Larry identifies a successful SpaceX IPO — which he expects in June 2026 — as the single most important catalyst for Tesla stock this year. He outlines three reasons: (1) a successful IPO will reawaken public perception of Elon Musk as a visionary, moving past the political environment that damaged his image; (2) it will help investors understand how Tesla and SpaceX work together as complementary businesses; and (3) it will validate Elon's credibility on robotaxi promises, since SpaceX's success proves his ability to deliver on audacious claims. Larry estimates Tesla stock could move 30–40% on the back of a successful SpaceX IPO.

2. **SpaceX Valuation and IPO Dynamics:** Larry discusses SpaceX's IPO pricing expectations, suggesting an offering at approximately $1.75 trillion with a successful outcome defined as the stock rising to $2 trillion by end of day. He notes SpaceX was valued at roughly $800 billion just months ago, and that the Anthropic deal has materially changed the valuation picture. He expects a staggered lockup period, likely as long as six months, meaning any Tesla-SpaceX merger announcement or exploration would not come until after the lockup ends — likely after the end of 2026.

3. **Tesla-SpaceX Merger Discussion:** Larry believes a Tesla-SpaceX merger announcement is possible but will not occur around the time of the IPO or during the lockup period. He speculates that discussions, if happening at all, would be extremely private. He describes a potential merger announcement as "extraordinarily positive" for Tesla stock and expects it would be a landmark event, though he aligns with the view that it would be locked in step with SpaceX's post-IPO trajectory.

4. **Anthropic Deal as a Proxy Signal:** Both the host and Larry point to Tesla's stock rising approximately $10 following SpaceX's deal with Anthropic — a deal with no direct Tesla connection — as evidence that investor instincts, not spreadsheet analysis, drive stock movements. Larry uses this as an analogy: if a tangential SpaceX deal moved Tesla $10, a successful SpaceX IPO could move it $50.

5. **Tesla Stock Expected to Surpass All-Time High in 2026:** Larry states his expectation that Tesla stock will surpass its all-time high this year, closely tied to SpaceX IPO progress. He notes the prior all-time high was reached at the time of Tesla's S&P 500 inclusion, which he characterizes as "artificial," and anticipates the next high will be more fundamentally driven by the confluence of events — auto rebound, FSD adoption, robotaxi progress, Optimus rollout, and the SpaceX IPO.

Notable quotes and data:
- China Tesla sales up 36% in April (described as highest ever)
- Denmark up 102%, Sweden up 111%, France up 112% in Tesla vehicle sales
- Current unsupervised robotaxi fleet referenced at approximately 38 vehicles (host's figure)
- Larry estimates 100–200 unsupervised robotaxis possible by SpaceX IPO in June 2026
- Waymo referenced at ~3,000 vehicles as a potential benchmark some investors cite
- Larry: FSD is "only three to four years ahead of the market"
- Larry: Tesla's robotaxi business model is "maybe 10 years ahead of the marketplace"
- Larry's Tesla stock move estimate on successful SpaceX IPO: "30%, maybe even 40%"
- SpaceX IPO expected in June 2026; IPO target valuation ~$1.75 trillion, success = reaching ~$2 trillion
- SpaceX valued at ~$800 billion "months ago"
- Tesla stock rose ~$10 following SpaceX-Anthropic deal announcement
- Larry: "I'm expecting [Tesla stock past all-time high] this year, very close in line with the IPO progress"
- Piper Sandler cited as flagging unsupervised personal use as the biggest underpriced catalyst
- Larry on Optimus: expects it to "really roll out" by Q3–Q4 2026
- Larry on Tesla-SpaceX merger: "extraordinarily positive" but not before lockup period ends

2026-05-11.title: Tesla’s Global FSD Signals Are Accelerating
2026-05-11.body:
This video from "brighterwithherbert" features host Herbert and guest Jeff Lutz — a multi-decade supply chain executive and chief quality officer, now CEO of a high-tech manufacturing consulting firm — reviewing a range of Tesla signals from the weekend, including new FSD technology demonstrations, regulatory progress in Europe and China, robotaxi fleet expansion commentary, and strong Giga Shanghai export data. The core thesis is that Tesla's FSD technology is accelerating globally across software capability, safety features, international regulatory approvals, and fleet deployment, while competition remains far behind.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Tesla hiring "code hardening" robotaxi software engineers:** Tesla posted a job listing for robotaxi software engineers focused on "code hardening," with miles per intervention explicitly named as the primary KPI. The job description states: "Miles per intervention is a key metric we look at to measure this and our primary focus is keeping the number as high as possible while robotaxi expands globally." Jeff Lutz noted that the KPIs are crystal clear and that a secondary metric is likely a bug identification and closure rate. He also suggested that much of the front-end development work that went into architecting FSD is now moving to Optimus.

2. **Tesla Vision enables airbag deployment up to 70 milliseconds earlier:** Tesla and Elon Musk posted about a new capability where Tesla Vision cameras detect unavoidable collisions and can deploy airbags up to 70 milliseconds earlier than traditional impact-sensor-only systems. Elon described this as coming "for free on all new cars" via a software update. The system uses cameras around the vehicle to identify when contact will be made and how severe a crash will be, passing that information to the airbag controller to supplement existing impact sensors. Jeff Lutz praised the feature while noting the importance of thorough stress testing for false-positive triggering across Tesla's fleet of approximately 8–9 million vehicles.

3. **Neural net photon reconstruction gives Tesla cameras superhuman night and glare vision:** Elon shared images contrasting human-perceived vision (showing extreme glare) with Tesla AI's photon count reconstruction of the same scene, which was dramatically clearer. Herbert and Jeff discussed how Tesla's real-time inference on in-vehicle AI supercomputers allows the camera system to see substantially better than a human driver, particularly at dawn, dusk, and in low-light conditions. Jeff noted this is Tesla's core system-level architectural advantage — not simply having "eight sets of eyes" but having AI-augmented vision exceeding human capability.

4. **Coast-to-coast FSD drive completed — 2,800 miles, zero interventions, under 50 hours:** Zach Black (Model 3) and teammates Dan Berkeland and Aaron completed a New York City to Los Angeles drive on FSD version 14.3.2 with zero human interventions, covering 2,800 miles in under 50 hours. They beat the previous record set by David Moss by 8.5 hours. Tesla officially reposted this achievement. Jeff Lutz emphasized that this milestone — long promised and long delayed — is now becoming a regular occurrence, and that no competing vehicle can offer anything comparable.

5. **NHTSA: Tesla Model Y is first vehicle to pass new advanced driver assistance system tests:** NHTSA announced that the 2026 Tesla Model Y (manufactured on or after November 2025) is the first vehicle to successfully meet criteria for four newly integrated advanced safety tests: pedestrian automatic emergency braking, lane-keeping assistance, blind spot warning, and blind spot intervention. Herbert noted this creates positive headlines for Tesla and NHTSA together and sets a high bar for the industry.

6. **FSD regulatory progress in Ireland and Belgium; Denmark clarifies Reuters report:** Tesla is currently in talks with Irish government authorities regarding approval of FSD supervised — a new country engaging with Tesla following the Dutch RDW presentation weeks earlier. In Belgium, a local director named Anek Ditter announced she is pushing to fast-forward the analysis of Tesla FSD in Belgium, though authorities there want to conduct additional limited-scale testing before homologation to account for differences between the Belgian and Dutch road systems. Separately, the Danish road traffic authority pushed back against a Reuters article, clarifying it had not expressed criticism or skepticism about Tesla FSD supervised and had not expressed positive or negative opinions about approval.

7. **China FSD employee beta reportedly underway on version 14.3.2:** An unverified rumor (attributed to "Ry") circulating on social media claims Tesla China has begun pushing a full-featured FSD version 14.x internally to employees in China, with employees asked to sign NDAs. The beta allegedly began late April/early May, runs version 14.3.2 (the latest), and involves approximately 1,000 hardware-equipped employee vehicles. Tesla China is also actively hiring many autopilot test engineers. Herbert speculated this internal beta may be timed ahead of potential regulatory approval coinciding with Elon Musk's visit to China with President Trump. Jeff Lutz cautioned that product development milestones would not be built around a trip that was itself rescheduled from late March.

8. **Chinese auto industry insider acknowledges gap vs. Tesla FSD:** Wang Yao, deputy chief engineer of the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers, stated in an interview that despite Chinese social media claiming domestic brands' autonomous driving surpasses Tesla's, technical professionals should honestly acknowledge certain gaps. Herbert and Jeff framed this as a signal of why Chinese regulators may have been hesitant to approve Tesla FSD — concern that Tesla's technology is superior to domestic competition.

## Robotaxi

1. **Robotaxi fleet growth pace defended statistically; scale of "volume deployment" unknown:** Jeff Lutz pushed back against social media skeptics dismissing near-term robotaxi scale, arguing that most people lack the statistical training to appreciate what incremental fleet growth means. He cited the example of going from approximately 22 to 33 to 35 unsupervised vehicles within a 7–10 day span as statistically meaningful, particularly if it represents a ~50% fleet increase. He emphasized, however, that neither Tesla nor outside observers truly know what Elon meant by "volume deployment" — whether hundreds of thousands is the threshold — and that uncertainty cuts both ways. He noted Tesla likely uses internal probabilistic models to monitor incident probability by geography as the fleet expands.

2. **Austin robotaxi transition from supervised to unsupervised ongoing:** Herbert noted that Tesla appears to be systematically moving supervised robotaxi drivers in Austin into unsupervised operation, replacing supervised rides with driverless ones as the technology is validated. He described this as the observable path of fleet maturation being watched in real time.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Giga Shanghai posts highest exports since October 2022:** Data reported by Roland Percher showed Tesla exported 53,000 Model 3s and Model Ys from China in April 2026 — the highest export figure from Giga Shanghai since October 2022, representing 80% year-over-year growth and 5.7% quarter-over-quarter growth vs. January 2026. Jeff Lutz noted that high exports from Shanghai are favorable for Tesla's margins since domestic China pricing is highly competitive with low margins, while EU, Asian, South Korean, and Japanese export markets carry higher margins.

2. **Tesla China domestic sales: 26,000 units in April, Model Y third bestselling car:** Tesla recorded 26,000 domestic sales in China in April with a 1.9% overall market share. The Model Y was the third bestselling car in China, with the sales mix approximately 89% Model Y and 11% Model 3. BEV penetration in China hit a new record of 41.8%, with Tesla holding 4.5% of that BEV segment. April domestic sales were approximately 10% below April 2025 levels but up approximately 40% compared to January 2026.

## Market & Competition

1. **Elon Musk and tech CEOs joining Trump's China visit; trade implications discussed:** Elon Musk is reportedly joining President Trump on a visit to China, alongside Tim Cook, Meta's CEO, Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon, BlackRock CEO Larry Fink, and Visa and Mastercard CEOs. Tesla China SVP Grace Tao posted optimistically about US-China mutual prosperity ahead of the visit. Jeff Lutz discussed concerns about the trip potentially opening US markets to Chinese auto manufacturers, but argued that any Chinese companies building in the US would face high US labor rates, supply chain constraints, and labor availability challenges that would make profitability extremely difficult — dismissing the idea of $10,000 EVs built domestically by Chinese firms. He also noted that US manufacturing job growth has been negative for the past 14 months despite manufacturing-friendly policy rhetoric.

2. **Competition cannot match Tesla's coast-to-coast FSD capability:** Jeff Lutz noted that no competitor — naming Nvidia's Alpamayo vehicle as an example — has demonstrated anything approaching Tesla's coast-to-coast intervention-free driving capability, with competitors limited to short YouTube clips on specific streets. He argued Tesla may have been late reaching this milestone, but no other automaker has closed the gap, and no other car can be purchased today that offers hands-free point-to-point driving.

Notable quotes and data:
- Tesla robotaxi job posting: *"Miles per intervention is a key metric we look at to measure this and our primary focus is keeping the number as high as possible while robotaxi expands globally."*
- Tesla Vision airbag feature: *"With the vision system, we're looking at up to 70 milliseconds earlier airbag deployment decision. But that can be the difference between a serious injury and walking away from the incident."*
- Elon Musk on Tesla Vision: *"Tesla AI Vision deploys airbags before impact, which greatly reduces risk of injury or death. This comes for free on all new cars."*
- Wang Yao (China Association of Automobile Manufacturers): *"While Chinese companies are indeed doing a very good job, we should also honestly acknowledge some of the gaps."*
- Coast-to-coast FSD drive: 2,800 miles, zero interventions, under 50 hours, on FSD version 14.3.2
- Giga Shanghai exports April 2026: 53,000 units — highest since October 2022, +80% year-over-year
- China BEV penetration: new record of 41.8%
- Tesla China April domestic sales: 26,000 units, 1.9% market share
- Unsupervised robotaxi fleet growth: reportedly went from ~22 to ~33 to ~35 in a 7–10 day window (per Jeff Lutz's commentary)
- Tesla fleet size referenced: approximately 8–9 million vehicles eligible for Vision airbag software update
- China FSD employee beta rumor: ~1,000 employee vehicles, version 14.3.2, NDAs signed, started late April/early May 2026
- NHTSA: 2026 Tesla Model Y (manufactured on or after November 2025) is first vehicle to pass four new ADAS safety tests

2026-05-11.title: Tesla's Robotaxi Path Just Got Clearer
2026-05-11.body:
This video features a multi-person discussion on the Tesla Tesla investment research platform, focused on the significance of the FSD 14.3 software release and its implications for scaling unsupervised robotaxi operations. The hosts — including Cern Basher and at least two other commentators — argue that 14.3's improvements, particularly around reinforcement learning, vision encoding, and self-recovery from edge cases, represent a meaningful step toward robotaxi scalability rather than a headline model size increase. The core thesis is that operational robustness and data pipeline optimization matter more than raw parameter counts for autonomous driving progress.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD 14.3 improvements centered on reinforcement learning:** The panelists explain that the majority of new features in FSD 14.3 — including pothole avoidance, animal avoidance, and improved school zone handling — fall under the category of reinforcement learning use cases. Rather than a dramatic architectural overhaul, the release represents a broad application of RL training to a wide range of real-world scenarios that previously caused difficulty for the system.

2. **Improved vision encoder as a key infrastructure upgrade:** One panelist highlights the improved vision encoder in 14.3 as an underappreciated but critical component. The vision encoder sets up raw data for the neural network to process, and optimizing it means the system can ingest more data at a higher rate. The argument is that maximizing the data pipeline to the limits of the available hardware is essential groundwork before any model scaling (e.g., a 10x parameter increase) can be meaningful.

3. **Skepticism toward "10x model improvement" framing:** The discussion includes pointed criticism of the public framing around large model parameter increases. One panelist argues that increasing parameters by 10x without first optimizing input data quality and runtime efficiency would be pointless — and potentially impossible on existing hardware. The comment is directed partly at Elon Musk for advertising such metrics without context, which the panelist says misleads the public about what actually drives better driving outcomes.

4. **Self-recovery from mistakes as a critical robotaxi capability:** A panelist emphasizes that FSD 14.3's ability to recover from difficult situations without driver intervention — reducing unnecessary disengagements — is especially important for unsupervised robotaxi deployment. In a robotaxi scenario with no human behind the wheel, the vehicle must resolve edge cases (e.g., a tree blocking a road) entirely on its own or escalate to a remote operations center. The goal is to minimize such escalations to only truly critical situations, so the system can scale to thousands of vehicles without an unmanageable operations burden.

5. **Hardware 3 vehicles predicted to never run unsupervised robotaxi:** One panelist states a clear prediction that Hardware 3 vehicles will not run unsupervised in the robotaxi network or in a customer unsupervised scenario. This is framed as a personal prediction, not a Tesla statement, but the panelist expresses confidence in it. The implication is that unsupervised FSD capability — whether for robotaxi or personal vehicles — will be limited to Hardware 4 (and presumably the Cybercab platform).

## Robotaxi

1. **Robotaxi scaling prioritized over customer unsupervised FSD:** The group reaches consensus that Tesla's internal focus is overwhelmingly on making robotaxi scale, rather than on enabling customer-owned vehicles to run unsupervised. While the panelists acknowledge that robotaxi and customer unsupervised are technically similar problems, they believe Tesla has a separate and currently lower-priority list of items specific to the customer unsupervised use case. Robotaxi revenue generation is seen as the primary near-term goal.

2. **Business risk logic favors robotaxi-first sequencing:** One panelist argues that from a business risk perspective, it makes more sense to first scale robotaxi, generate substantial revenue and cash flow, and then release customer unsupervised FSD. The reasoning is that Tesla will inevitably face lawsuits from unavoidable accidents — a point Elon Musk himself acknowledged in a post cited during the discussion, where he said autonomous vehicles will likely avoid 90% of accidents but the remaining 10% are unavoidable and will result in litigation. Having strong cash flow from robotaxi operations would provide a financial buffer for those legal costs.

3. **Operations center scalability as a design constraint:** The panelists discuss how the robotaxi operations center model must be engineered with scale in mind from the outset. If the current fleet of vehicles requires frequent intervention for everyday problems, multiplying the fleet by 1,000x, 2,000x, or 5,000x would make the operations center unmanageable. The implication is that FSD 14.3's improvements in self-recovery and edge case handling are directly aimed at reducing the ratio of operational interventions per vehicle-mile, which is a prerequisite for economically viable large-scale robotaxi deployment.

Notable quotes and data:
- Elon Musk posted that autonomous vehicles will "probably end up avoiding 90% of accidents and saving millions of lives," but the remaining 10% are unavoidable and Tesla will be sued for them.
- One panelist predicts Hardware 3 vehicles will never run unsupervised in the robotaxi network — stated as a personal prediction, not a Tesla commitment.
- FSD 14.3 features cited: pothole avoidance, animal avoidance, improved school zone handling, improved vision encoder, self-recovery from edge cases without driver intervention.
- The group agrees: 14.3's improvements increase safety and will enable Tesla to scale unsupervised robotaxi, initially scoped to Austin geography.
- Robotaxi is characterized as priority one; customer unsupervised FSD on personal vehicles is priority two.

2026-05-11.title: Tesla China retail sales fall 10% in April despite reports of 36% surge
2026-05-11.body:
Tesla's actual retail sales in China fell 10% year-over-year in April to 25,956 vehicles, per China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) final data — contradicting widespread media reports of a 36% surge that were based on wholesale/export figures from Giga Shanghai.

## Electric Vehicles
1. **Wholesale vs. retail discrepancy:** Giga Shanghai produced and shipped 79,478 vehicles in April, which generated the "36% surge" headlines. However, 53,522 of those were exports — up 80% year-over-year and the second-highest monthly export total in Giga Shanghai's history. Stripping out exports leaves just 25,956 domestic retail units, down 9.66% from 28,731 in April 2025.

2. **Sequential and cumulative declines:** April retail sales fell 53.7% from March's 56,107 units, though part of that drop reflects seasonal end-of-quarter dynamics. For January–April 2026, cumulative retail sales totaled 138,754 vehicles, down 15% year-over-year. This follows a full-year 2025 retail decline of roughly 5% and a Q1 2026 crash of 16%.

3. **Market share at recent lows:** Tesla captured 3.06% of China's overall NEV retail market in April — its lowest share since November 2025. In the pure BEV segment, share was 4.48%, also a new low since November 2025.

4. **Financing policy change:** Tesla canceled a seven-year low-interest loan option in China in May 2026, retaining only a zero-interest plan for up to five years. The article notes promotional financing has not reversed the demand trend so far.

## Market & Competition
5. **Export surge masks domestic weakness:** In the first four months of 2026, Tesla exported 154,122 vehicles from Shanghai — a 127% surge year-over-year — while domestic retail dropped 15% over the same period. Export destinations include South Korea, Europe, Australia, and Canada (which recently resumed accepting Chinese-made Teslas).

6. **Chinese competitors outpacing Tesla domestically:** In April, BYD posted wholesale volume of 321,123 NEVs (though down 15.5% year-over-year, its eighth consecutive YoY decline). Li Auto delivered 34,085 vehicles, Xpeng delivered 31,011, and NIO delivered 29,356 — up 23% year-over-year. All three exceeded Tesla's domestic China retail figure of 25,956.

## Editorial Stance
Author Fred Lambert argues that reporting Giga Shanghai's wholesale output as "Tesla China sales" is misleading, since roughly two-thirds of production is now exported. He contends the retail figure is the relevant metric for assessing Tesla's competitive position in the world's largest EV market, which he characterizes as genuinely declining.

Notable quotes and data:
- April 2026 China retail sales: 25,956 units (-9.66% YoY)
- Giga Shanghai wholesale output: 79,478 units (+36% YoY)
- April exports from Shanghai: 53,522 units (+80% YoY; +81% vs. March)
- Jan–Apr 2026 exports: 154,122 (+127% YoY)
- Jan–Apr 2026 domestic retail: 138,754 (-15% YoY)
- Tesla NEV market share in China (April): 3.06% (lowest since Nov 2025)
- Tesla BEV segment share (April): 4.48% (lowest since Nov 2025)
- Sequential drop from March to April retail: -53.7%

2026-05-11.title: Nobody Sees What Amazon Just Did to Tesla
2026-05-11.body:
This video argues that Amazon's newly announced Amazon Supply Chain Services (ASCS) — an end-to-end logistics platform opened to any business — is the single most important macro event for Tesla's long-term thesis. The host, Farzad, draws a direct parallel to AWS, contending that ASCS will require massive scaling of autonomous trucks, delivery vans, and humanoid warehouse robots, and that Tesla is uniquely positioned to supply all three categories. The core argument is that Tesla is effectively the "Nvidia of physical AI hardware" — the picks-and-shovels supplier for Amazon's ambition to become the AWS of the physical world.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Tesla Semi as the critical truck supplier:** Farzad identifies Tesla as the only U.S. truck OEM with a high-volume, vertically integrated electric semi factory with autonomous capability that rolled its first truck off the high-production line in April 2026. The Sparks, Nevada semi factory is designed for 50,000 trucks per year. Standard range starts at $260,000 with ~350 miles of range; long range is $290,000 with ~500 miles. The Megacharger can restore 60% charge in 30 minutes. Existing or pending customers include PepsiCo, Frito-Lay, Walmart, Cisco, Anheuser-Busch, UPS, DHL, JB Hunt, and SAIA. In California's clean truck voucher program, Tesla Semi received 965 of the Class 8 applications, while Daimler, Paccar, and Volvo combined received under 100.

2. **Cybercab and Robo Van as autonomous delivery platforms:** The Cybercab began production at Giga Texas in Q1 2026, is built with FSD only in mind (self-driving by design), and has a full-volume target of 2 million units per year. Tesla also revealed a "Robo Van" at its "We Robot" event in October 2024 — described as a 20-passenger autonomous van form factor with no confirmed production date. Farzad envisions the Robo Van as an obvious autonomous delivery vehicle, potentially paired with an Optimus unit handling last-step parcel delivery.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus production timeline and scale targets:** Tesla's Optimus humanoid robot is targeted to begin production at Fremont in late July or August 2026 on the converted Model S and X line, though Farzad explicitly expects this to be late. The Fremont target is a 1 million units per year run rate by late 2026, more likely sliding into 2027–2028. The Giga Texas Optimus factory is targeted at 10 million units per year. The end-goal price target is $20,000–$30,000 per unit.

2. **Optimus unit economics vs. human labor:** Using a $25,000 unit cost, a 3-year useful life, and ~7,000 productive hours per year (21,000 lifetime hours), the hardware cost alone comes to roughly $1.20/hour. Adding energy at ~$0.10–$0.15/hour and maintenance at ~$0.20–$0.30/hour yields a fully loaded cost of roughly $1.50–$2.00/hour. This compares to $25–$35/hour fully loaded for a U.S. warehouse worker — a 90%+ labor cost reduction per unit at scale.

3. **Amazon as potential anchor Optimus customer:** Amazon already operates over 1 million robots (up from 750,000 the prior year) across 300+ fulfillment centers. Farzad argues Amazon's warehouses are the largest concentrated humanoid market on Earth, and that at $20,000–$30,000 per unit, Amazon could absorb hundreds of thousands of Optimus units without straining its capex budget. He flags this as a "generational signal" event if Tesla announces even a pilot Optimus deployment in an Amazon fulfillment center.

4. **Competitive humanoid landscape — Tesla not currently leading deployments:** Farzad acknowledges Tesla is not currently in the lead on real-world humanoid deployments. Boston Dynamics has its Atlas robot deployed inside Hyundai's Meta Plant in Georgia, with all 2026 fleet capacity committed to Hyundai and Google DeepMind. Apptronik (the Apollo robot company) just raised $520 million and has GXO Logistics as a customer. Figure has BMW Spartanburg. Agility Robotics has subscription humanoid leasing models already operating in warehouses. Tesla has the more integrated stack and manufacturing edge if it executes, but has the most catching up to do on actual deployment.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD as the unifying software platform across Tesla's physical AI stack:** Farzad emphasizes that Tesla Semi runs FSD hardware, Cybercab is FSD-only by design, and Optimus shares the same neural net architecture as FSD. He frames this as one software stack powering the entire physical labor pipeline — trucks, vans, and humanoid robots — that Amazon would need to scale ASCS globally. He describes this as "the picks and shovels play of the decade."

## Market & Competition

1. **Amazon Supply Chain Services — the AWS of the physical world:** Amazon announced ASCS, bundling freight (ocean, air, ground, rail), distribution and fulfillment, parcel shipping (2–5 day, 7 days/week), and AI-powered inventory forecasting into a single platform available to any business. Launch customers include Procter & Gamble, 3M, Lands' End, American Eagle, and Aerie. Amazon's logistics infrastructure includes ~1,200 facilities globally, 350+ full-scale fulfillment centers, 40,000+ owned semi-trucks, 390,000+ delivery service partner drivers, 100+ aircraft, 80,000+ trailers, and 30,000 Rivian electric vans (committed to 100,000 by 2030). The global logistics market ASCS is entering is $9.37 trillion, projected to grow to $13 trillion by 2035. A 1% market capture equals $130 billion in revenue.

2. **Immediate market reaction to ASCS announcement:** FedEx had its worst single-day stock performance in over a year. UPS dropped 10%. GXO Logistics dropped 13%. CH Robinson dropped 9%. Farzad calls these moves likely an overreaction on the day but directionally correct.

3. **AWS analogy and SaaS multiple re-rating thesis:** AWS grew from zero in 2006 to $108 billion in revenue by 2024 and generated nearly $40 billion in income in 2024, representing ~50% of Amazon's total profit on only 15–18% of revenue. In Q1 2026, AWS reaccelerated to 28% year-over-year growth, the fastest in 15 quarters. Farzad argues ASCS, unlike AWS, is launching into a $9.37 trillion existing market with infrastructure already built — it doesn't need to create the category. He also argues Wall Street assigns higher multiples to recurring infrastructure-style revenue, so ASCS could justify more market cap than equivalent FedEx revenue even at the same dollar level.

4. **Key risks:** On Amazon: FedEx and UPS have decades of customs relationships, international air rights, regulatory expertise, and political leverage (Teamsters at UPS). Antitrust and FTC scrutiny is a real risk given Amazon already faces self-preferencing investigations and would now see competitors' full distribution data. On Tesla: Elon Musk has missed virtually every Optimus production deadline since 2021 and nearly every major timeline, and competitors are already deployed in real warehouses while Tesla is not.

Notable quotes and data:
- AWS: $108B revenue and ~$40B income in 2024; ~50% of Amazon's total profit on 15–18% of revenue; 28% YoY growth in Q1 2026, fastest in 15 quarters
- Global logistics market: $9.37 trillion today, projected $13 trillion by 2035; 1% capture = $130 billion
- Amazon robots: 1,000,000+ deployed across 300+ fulfillment centers (up from 750,000 the prior year — 250,000 added in under one year)
- Amazon workforce: ~1.56 million employees, second-largest U.S. employer behind Walmart
- Tesla Semi: Sparks, Nevada factory designed for 50,000 trucks/year; standard range $260K/350mi, long range $290K/500mi; 965 of 1,067 California Class 8 clean truck voucher applications
- Cybercab: Production started Giga Texas Q1 2026; full-volume target 2 million units/year
- Optimus target price: $20,000–$30,000/unit; Fremont target ~1M units/year run rate by late 2026 (likely 2027–28); Giga Texas target 10M units/year
- Optimus fully loaded cost: ~$1.50–$2.00/hour vs. $25–$35/hour for U.S. warehouse worker (~90%+ reduction)
- Apptronik raised $520M; Boston Dynamics 2026 fleet fully committed to Hyundai and Google DeepMind
- Amazon Rivian vans: 30,000 currently, committed to 100,000 by 2030

2026-05-11.title: FSD Crash Probe (Not Tesla!) | Ireland FSD Just Dropped? | S/X Era Over? | LEAK?!
2026-05-11.body:
This is a Monday morning news roundup from FutureAzA host Brian, covering a broad range of Tesla and EV industry stories from May 11, 2026. The video touches on the end of Model S/X production, Tesla's FSD regulatory engagement in Ireland, a competitor AV crash investigation, battery technology comparisons, and a range of market and competitive developments. The tone is conversational and editorial, blending news summaries with commentary and audience Q&A.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **End of the Model S and X Era:** Tesla has produced its last Model S and Model X at the factory, marking 14 years of history for the Model S and 11 for the Model X. The final vehicles were signed by factory workers in a graffiti-style tribute. However, with just 72 hours' notice, Tesla delayed the planned final delivery event, which Brian suggests may be because production was not actually fully complete — citing leaked footage reportedly showing a worker installing the final brake booster.

2. **Giga Shanghai Best April Ever:** Giga Shanghai recorded its best-ever April, producing 79,000 cars, putting it on pace for approximately one million vehicles per year from the 10-million-square-foot factory. This marked the sixth consecutive month of growth as the factory continues to rebound.

3. **Model 3 Global Sales Strength:** Despite narratives about the Model 3's decline, Brian notes it was the second best-selling EV in the world in March, and Canada has now been added to its strong markets, with tens of thousands expected to be sold there.

4. **Tesla Semi Battery Capacity Published:** California regulators published the Tesla Semi's official battery capacity — 822 kWh for the long-range variant and 548 kWh for the standard range. Brian downplays the significance of battery size alone, emphasizing range as the key metric. He notes stacking incentives in California, Oregon, Washington, New Jersey, New York, and other states on top of an already competitively priced vehicle could make the Semi significantly more attractive.

5. **Tesla Semi Appearing on European Websites:** The Tesla Semi is now appearing on Tesla's websites in Europe, including the UK, though only the standard (short) range version is listed so far.

6. **Model Y Tops New NCAP ADAS Test:** A Model Y manufactured on or after November 12th, 2025 became the first vehicle to pass a new NCAP ADAS test covering pedestrian automatic emergency braking, lane keeping assistance, blind spot warning, and blind spot intervention. As of two days before the video, no other automaker had passed more than three of the four criteria, leaving Tesla ahead by at least 33% on those safety metrics.

7. **Tesla Owner Loyalty Remains Strong:** Despite brand controversies, Tesla maintains high owner loyalty — 63.6% among Asian households and 61.9% among Hispanic households, down from the 80%+ of early adopter days but still notably strong.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Tesla Engages Irish Authorities on FSD Approval:** Ireland's Department of Transportation confirmed in a statement to RTÉ News that Tesla is currently engaging with Irish authorities, including the Irish approval body, regarding their FSD system. The department noted that negotiations will continue on both national and EU levels but that no timeline for EU approval can be provided. Brian notes that EU-level approval would unlock Ireland as well.

2. **Unusual Volume of NHTSA Tesla Complaints:** Brian relays a secondhand account from someone with a contact at NHTSA, who noted Tesla was receiving more complaints than there were units of the relevant car sold — suggesting organized bad-faith complaint filing intended to obstruct Tesla's regulatory progress, rather than legitimate consumer grievances.

## Robotaxi

1. **Competitor AV Company Under NHTSA Investigation:** A Tesla robotaxi rival (not named in the transcript but described as operating in Dallas and Austin, developing since 2017, and available on Uber) is under NHTSA investigation following 16 accidents involving its automated driving system, resulting in one minor injury and property damage. Alleged ADS failures included changing lanes into the path of other vehicles, failing to respond to vehicles entering the lane, and striking partially obstructed stationary objects. Brian notes the headline required putting Tesla's name in it to generate clicks, despite Tesla not being the subject.

2. **Customer-Owned Vehicles Entering the Taxi Fleet:** In Q&A, Brian was asked when customer-owned vehicles would enter the robotaxi fleet, calling it "the trillion dollar question" with no current answer. He added that a step change in Cybercab deployment is not expected in April or May 2026, but that it is "definitely" coming in 2026 with no roadblocks having appeared — quite the opposite.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Piper Sandler Says Optimus Is Free at Current Valuations:** Piper Sandler published an update arguing that at $400 per share, investors are effectively getting Optimus for free — meaning their valuation model has not yet assigned any value to Optimus. Brian is skeptical, questioning how they arrived at a trillion-dollar valuation without counting Optimus, and noting that Piper Sandler says they will begin incorporating Optimus into valuation models once revenue arrives.

## Energy

1. **New CATL Sun WODA LFP Battery:** A new LFP battery from CATL called the Sun WODA features a 62.5 kWh capacity (fully usable), ultra-fast 3C charging enabling 10–80% charge in 15 minutes (versus 25 minutes previously), and a 0–62 mph time of 5.2 seconds (versus 6.1 seconds). Brian frames this as evidence that LFP batteries have already addressed most of what solid-state batteries were hoped to solve — lower cost, faster charging, and fire resistance — making solid-state less urgently necessary.

2. **4680 Battery Falls Short on Energy Density:** Citing analyst Yash Bajaj, Brian notes that Tesla's 4680 battery achieves 244 Wh/kg versus 269 Wh/kg for the 2170 cells — approximately 8% lower energy density. In real-world charging, 15 minutes of charging delivers 27 kWh. Brian acknowledges the 4680 likely offers cost advantages but concedes it underperforms on energy density metrics relative to 2170s.

3. **Wind and Solar Already Cheaper Than Fossil Fuels:** New gas capacity costs $70–85 per MWh, new coal costs approximately $100 per MWh, while wind and solar cost $54–82 per MWh — already cheaper unsubsidized.

## Market & Competition

1. **China Investigates EV "Battery Locking" Claims — Then Debunks Them:** Chinese state media reported that EVs rated for 500 km of range were being reduced to under 300 km via over-the-air battery management updates. Multiple automakers including BYD, Tesla, NIO, Xpeng, Zeekr, GAC, and Li Auto denied the claims. BYD threatened legal action. Brian characterizes the story as having snowballed from a vague regulatory inquiry into unfounded accusations, drawing a parallel to the NHTSA complaint manipulation story.

2. **European Automakers Selling Factories to Chinese Partners:** Stellantis announced it is considering selling an underutilized factory in Spain to its Chinese joint venture partner Leap Motors. Brian argues this doesn't merely "risk" strengthening Chinese automakers — it guarantees it. He notes European factories are operating at roughly half capacity and face structural competitive pressure from Chinese EV makers' technical advancement and low production costs. The observation is that steep import tariffs are being bypassed by Chinese firms simply building locally.

3. **Tesla–Intel Semiconductor Partnership:** Elon Musk toured Intel's semiconductor fab in Hillsboro ahead of a reported Tesla and SpaceX partnership with Intel. Wedbush published commentary calling it both a "compelling opportunity" and issuing warnings about the gap between announced plans and actual execution, noting the path contains significant risks.

4. **XAI / SpaceX Merger and Anthropic Deal:** Anthropic announced it is renting server space from XAI data centers. The merged company of SpaceX and XAI is expected to be named "SpaceX AAI." Brian notes this as an interesting revenue model for the combined entity.

5. **Tesla Recall of 218,000 Vehicles:** Tesla issued a recall of over 218,000 vehicles in the US, which Brian characterizes as a non-event — the issue was a backup camera glitch resolved over the air.

Notable quotes and data:
- Giga Shanghai: 79,000 cars in April 2026 — best April ever; sixth consecutive month of growth; ~1 million/year run rate
- Tesla Semi battery capacity (per California regulators): 822 kWh long range, 548 kWh standard range
- 4680 energy density: 244 Wh/kg vs. 2170 at 269 Wh/kg (~8% lower)
- 4680 real-world: 27 kWh delivered in 15 minutes of charging
- Sun WODA LFP: 62.5 kWh, 3C charging, 10–80% in 15 minutes, 0–62 mph in 5.2 seconds
- Tesla owner loyalty: 63.6% Asian households, 61.9% Hispanic households
- Wind/solar: $54–82/MWh unsubsidized; new gas $70–85/MWh; new coal ~$100/MWh
- Model S history: 14 years; Model X history: 11 years
- Competitor AV (not Tesla): 16 accidents under NHTSA investigation, operating in Dallas and Austin
- Piper Sandler: "At $400/share, investors can buy Optimus for free in terms of valuation"
- Cybercab step-change deployment: "Not in April, not in May — definitely in 2026"
- Tesla stock at time of recording: ~$440/share; 52-week high $498
- Brian's comment on Cybercab timeline: "No roadblocks have appeared. Quite the opposite."

2026-05-11.title: If You Own Tesla Stock Don't Make These Mistakes & The Next Big Stock About to Break Out!
2026-05-11.body:
This video from the "investingagainstthegrain" channel covers a range of investing topics centered on Tesla's recent breakout above $400, with the host (Nick) warning long-term Tesla investors against selling covered calls prematurely at what he believes may be the beginning of a major autonomous driving thesis inflection point. He also addresses macro risks from the Iran-U.S. peace deal breakdown, cautions investors on Micron and SanDisk's commodity-driven valuations, and identifies Nvidia, Palantir, and Meta as additional actionable opportunities.

2026-05-11.title: Why Tesla Stock Is EXPLODING - And What Happens NEXT
2026-05-11.body:
Jo Bhakdi delivers a live stream covering his near-term Tesla price thesis, options trading strategy, and outlook on the robotaxi ramp. The core argument is that Tesla's stock returning to its all-time high of ~$490 is a technically and fundamentally driven inevitability — not a repricing event — given that both the broader market and Tesla's fundamental position are stronger now than they were when the stock last hit that level in December. He also reviews Pioneer Alpha's recent performance and introduces a new bond product structure for qualified investors.

## Market & Competition

1. **Tesla's technical path back to all-time highs:** Bhakdi argues that Tesla hit an all-time high of $490 on December 16th, then slid through Q1, and is now in what he describes as its strongest 33% up-run in a very long time, having bounced from a May 6th low of $385. His reasoning is purely mechanical: the broader market is at or above its prior all-time highs, and Tesla is objectively stronger as a company than it was in December, therefore the stock has a technical forcing function back to $490. He explicitly frames $490 as the near-term minimum target, not a ceiling, and says it could be reached as early as the current week or the following week.

2. **Caution above $490 until robotaxi scales:** Bhakdi strongly cautions against extrapolating the move to $500, $550, or $600. He argues that everything above $490 is, in his words, "complete randomness and arbitrary" until robotaxi proves itself at scale. He references the RobotaxiTracker.com data, noting that the unsupervised fleet stands at 39 vehicles, and contrasts this with Waymo's approximately 3,000 vehicles, arguing that cold-blooded institutional investors will dismiss the current robotaxi numbers as insignificant. He says the forcing function for a true repricing — one that would justify much higher prices — would require robotaxi scaling to hundreds of vehicles, not dozens.

3. **Waymo comparison as institutional benchmark:** Bhakdi explicitly invokes Waymo's ~3,000-vehicle fleet as the frame of reference that institutional investors will use when evaluating Tesla's robotaxi progress. He suggests that until Tesla's unsupervised robotaxi count becomes meaningfully large by that standard, the market will not re-rate Tesla above its prior all-time high on robotaxi fundamentals alone.

## Robotaxi

1. **Unsupervised fleet size and growth trajectory:** Bhakdi references the RobotaxiTracker.com data showing 39 unsupervised robotaxi vehicles currently operational. He acknowledges the exponential growth trend visible on the tracker chart but emphasizes that the absolute number remains too small to move institutional sentiment. He frames this as exciting for believers but insufficient for a fundamental repricing.

2. **Cybercab as the key catalyst:** Bhakdi states that "Cybercab is live" and that Tesla is now beginning to scale unsupervised operations, albeit delayed from earlier expectations. He characterizes the current phase as fine-tuning for convenience rather than safety — suggesting that safety is largely solved, and the remaining work is reducing the share of rides that are annoying or inconvenient to customers (e.g., getting stuck at intersections), bringing that error rate from perhaps 5–10 per 100 rides down toward 0.1 per 100.

3. **Slow growth in unsupervised numbers:** In response to a viewer question about slow growth in unsupervised FSD numbers over the prior few days, Bhakdi says he is not concerned, characterizes it as normal early-stage growth on a very low base, and notes that Pioneer Alpha is building out more sophisticated robotaxi margin and growth models that he hopes to share soon, possibly as early as the following week.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Safety vs. convenience as the current frontier:** Bhakdi expresses confidence that Tesla has effectively solved the safety dimension of Full Self-Driving, citing visible data as his basis for that belief (echoing Elon Musk's own statements). He frames the current challenge as a convenience and reliability problem — reducing the frequency of non-dangerous but frustrating ride failures — rather than a life-safety issue.

## Financials

1. **Pioneer Alpha performance:** Bhakdi reports that his Pioneer Alpha portfolio was up 22% last week, compared to Tesla's 9.6% gain, representing approximately 12% alpha over Tesla. Year-to-date, the portfolio is up 36%, which he says outperforms NASDAQ, S&P, MSCI, TSLL, Tesla itself (by 41%), ARK's ARKQ (outperformed by ~20%), and ARK's ARKK (outperformed by ~34%). He attributes this largely to a disciplined short-put strategy on Tesla executed with high conviction during the recent run-up.

2. **Pioneer Reserve bond products:** Bhakdi describes three bond products now available through the Pioneer Reserve Luxembourg securitization vehicle, all drawing on the same underlying Pioneer Alpha portfolio. The first, "Tesla Plus 50," charges no fees up to Tesla's benchmark return and captures 50% of alpha above that. The second, "Growth 45," targets up to 45% annualized return with a maximum bond payout of 200% of principal, designed for lower volatility. The third, "Income 12," pays 1% per month (3% quarterly) of principal plus up to 100% additional gain at maturity. He says the first close is expected in May and that the products are available to qualified investors in Europe, Canada, the UK, Switzerland, and the United States.

3. **Options strategy detail — short puts:** Bhakdi walks through his preferred instrument in detail: selling at-the-money short puts with weekly expiration. Using the current stock price of roughly $445 and a May 15th expiration as an example, he notes the 445-strike put was trading at approximately $9.50–$9.65 per share ($950–$965 per contract). He explains that this strategy profits if Tesla goes up, sideways, or even down modestly (to roughly $435 in his example), and only loses if Tesla falls significantly — which he describes as the rare scenario requiring aggressive risk management and immediate position reduction regardless of conviction level.
