2026-05-27.title: Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX merger would be Musk’s 4th billion-dollar self-deal
2026-05-27.body:
Electrek reports that Elon Musk is reportedly considering merging Tesla and SpaceX, framing it as the fourth in a pattern of billion-dollar self-dealing transactions between companies Musk controls. The article argues this would be the largest such deal yet, raising serious fiduciary concerns for Tesla shareholders.

## Market & Competition
1. **SpaceX IPO context and merger odds:** SpaceX filed its S-1 on May 20 and is expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under ticker SPCX on June 12, targeting a valuation of up to $1.75 trillion and raising approximately $75 billion — described as the largest IPO in history. Tesla's market cap currently sits around $1.6 trillion. Wedbush analyst Dan Ives puts merger odds at "80 to 90 percent" by early 2027; Kalshi prediction markets assign only 33% odds before May 2027. A combined entity could exceed $3 trillion in market cap. SpaceX reported revenue of $18.7 billion and a net loss of $4.9 billion ahead of the IPO.

2. **Pattern of self-dealing transactions:** The article catalogs three prior billion-dollar transactions: (1) Tesla's 2016 acquisition of SolarCity for $2.6 billion in stock, where Musk chaired both boards; other Tesla directors settled related litigation for $60 million. (2) Musk's $44 billion Twitter acquisition in 2022, which Fidelity later marked down ~65%; by October 2024 the platform was valued at roughly $9–10 billion. In March 2025, xAI acquired X for $33 billion ($45 billion including $12 billion in debt). (3) Tesla disclosed a $2 billion investment in Musk's xAI in January 2026; shortly after, SpaceX acquired xAI in a deal valued at approximately $250 billion. Musk subsequently admitted xAI was "not built right."

3. **Structural conflict of interest:** Musk holds approximately 20% of Tesla's equity but controls 85.1% of SpaceX's voting power through a super-voting share class. The article argues this asymmetry means Musk effectively negotiates merger terms with himself, with Tesla shareholders absorbing disproportionate risk. Tesla shareholders are already suing Musk for breach of fiduciary duty over the xAI investment.

## Editorial Stance
Author Fred Lambert argues this potential merger represents the "logical culmination" of Musk using Tesla as a "piggy bank" for private ventures, contending that Musk's playbook — shuffling assets between entities he controls to stamp higher valuations on combinations — benefits his private holdings at Tesla shareholders' expense. Lambert is skeptical of Dan Ives' pro-merger thesis and notes Ives "has been extremely wrong in predicting Tesla's progress in robotics."

Notable quotes and data:
- SpaceX IPO target valuation: up to $1.75 trillion; raise: ~$75 billion; expected trading date: June 12 under ticker SPCX
- SpaceX financials: $18.7 billion revenue, $4.9 billion net loss
- Tesla market cap: ~$1.6 trillion; combined entity projected at $3+ trillion
- Musk's Tesla equity: ~20%; SpaceX voting control: 85.1%
- Dan Ives merger probability: "80 to 90 percent" by early 2027
- Kalshi merger odds: 33% before May 2027
- SolarCity deal: $2.6 billion (2016); director settlement: $60 million
- Twitter acquisition: $44 billion (2022); platform value by Oct. 2024: ~$9–10 billion
- xAI/X deal: $33 billion ($45 billion including debt), March 2025
- Tesla's xAI investment: $2 billion (disclosed January 2026)
- SpaceX acquisition of xAI: ~$250 billion
- Dan Ives claim: autonomous robotics could add "$1 to $2 trillion" to combined market cap

2026-05-27.title: The Electric Car Explosion Nobody Saw Coming
2026-05-27.body:
This video is a lighthearted, comedic review by Brian (FutureAzA) and Mark (The Tesla Life) of Top Gear's list of 44 most exciting upcoming electric vehicles. The hosts work through the list car by car, offering quick reactions, design critiques, and skepticism about whether many of the featured vehicles will ever reach production in their rendered form. The core thesis, stated at the outset, is that the EV market has matured dramatically — where 10–15 years ago affordable options barely existed, today there is a wide and growing global selection, even if many are not yet available in North America.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **EV market maturity framing:** The hosts open by noting that while a decade or more ago it was genuinely true that affordable EVs were scarce, today there is a broad and expanding global selection. The caveat is that many of the most interesting options are not yet available in preferred markets, colors, or brands — but the variety is real and growing.

2. **Peugeot E208 GTI (No. 1 on Top Gear's list):** Shown only as a rendering, the car is noted as having 276 horsepower. The hosts are skeptical of render-only reveals and note that many vehicles on the list claim up to 300 miles of range on the European test cycle, which they address more fully later.

3. **European vs. EPA range cycles explained:** When discussing the Mercedes C-Class electric's claimed 473-mile range (on the CLTC Chinese cycle), the hosts clarify that non-EPA range figures are not inherently dishonest — CLTC is calibrated for slower, more congested Chinese urban driving, and WLTP is calibrated for typical European driving conditions. They argue these figures reflect real-world expectations for their respective markets.

4. **Hyundai Ioniq 3:** Noted as claiming 305 miles of range on the European cycle. The hosts caution that charging from 10–80% would reduce usable range by roughly a third, and that real-world figures would be lower still. They suggest it could be competitive if priced well, given the popularity of small SUVs.

5. **Hyundai Staria Electric:** Highlighted as significant because it fills a gap — an electric minivan segment largely absent in North America. Mark notes Hyundai also has a smaller van (the PV4 or PV5) coming to Canada later in the year (i.e., later in 2026). The hosts confirm the Staria is not made in China, with production across Korea and two final assembly plants elsewhere.

6. **BYD Denza 79 GT:** The hosts are genuinely enthusiastic about this vehicle, citing 952 brake horsepower, crab-walk capability, and instant charging. Already on sale in China and heading to Europe. They discuss its fastback/shooting brake design and note its camera-based side mirrors, confirming that Europe has permitted camera mirrors for years.

7. **Rivian R2 (No. 16):** The hosts express surprise it ranks so low given that manufacturing has already begun and the vehicle has been seen publicly. They drove it previously and found the slightly smaller size appealing, noting it could be a strong fit for both European and North American markets. They flag that it lacks even a cramped third row. Rivian will be present at the Michigan summer meetup offering test drives (of other models, not the R2).

8. **Volkswagen ID Polo / ID2 / ID Golf:** The hosts call it an early winner on nostalgia alone, noting it closely resembles a Golf. No pricing or specs confirmed yet, but they believe the heritage branding will drive strong sales.

9. **Polestar 2 Gen 2 and Polestar 4 Estate:** The Polestar 4 estate variant appears to add a rear window absent from the standard model. On Polestar generally, the hosts note that US pricing has been too high relative to perceived brand value — "it's hard to charge Mercedes pricing without the Mercedes logo."

10. **Jaguar concept:** The hosts are harshly critical of Jaguar's strategy, noting the brand has had nothing to sell for over a year and a half to two years while running brand-image advertising. They question what Jaguar dealerships have been doing during this period. Despite this, Top Gear apparently gave the prototype a drive and called it "a proper Jag of the highest order."

11. **Render quality and concept skepticism:** A running theme throughout is that a significant portion of the 44 vehicles are either pure CGI renders, early-stage concepts, or designs the hosts believe will look substantially different in production. Several entries (BMW hydrogen, Bentley Urban SUV, Ford Universal EV, Alpine A3, and others) receive particular mockery for appearing to be low-quality renders or outright placeholder images.

## Market & Competition

1. **China-origin vehicles expanding to Europe:** Multiple vehicles on the list — including the BYD Denza 79 GT and MG Cyber Stir Coupe — are already on sale in China and are now moving into European markets. The hosts note that Chinese manufacturing enables lower price points and that MG's heritage as a non-premium brand means the Cyber Stir coupe does not need to be expensive.

2. **Stellantis/Jeep credibility gap:** The hosts express skepticism about the Jeep Recon, citing Stellantis's track record of announced products that underdeliver. They predict the Jeep Recon will likely be "an overpriced, oversized pavement princess" given its apparent weight and cost trajectory.

3. **Toyota/Subaru partnership noted:** The Subaru E Outback is identified as still being a Toyota platform cousin, with the hosts noting that the latest generation of Toyota EVs has meaningfully improved in horsepower, efficiency, and range for the 2027 model year.

Notable quotes and data:
- Mercedes C-Class electric: up to 473 miles of range (CLTC Chinese cycle)
- Hyundai Ioniq 3: 305 miles claimed range (European cycle); hosts estimate ~200 miles usable at 10–80% charge
- BYD Denza 79 GT: 952 brake horsepower, crab-walk, instant charging, already on sale in China
- Honda Super N: under £20,000, 95 brake horsepower
- GV60 Magma (Genesis/Hyundai): described as having "600-something" horsepower
- Jaguar has had no production car to sell for "over a year and a half, maybe two" years (as of mid-2026)
- Polestar 4 Estate and Polestar 2 Gen 2 both appearing on the list
- Rivian R2: manufacturing confirmed underway; no third row; to be represented at Michigan summer meetup
- Hyundai PV4/PV5 van: coming to Canada later in 2026
- Brian mentions recently driving a Jeep Wagon S with 1,000 horsepower and roughly three metric tons curb weight
- "If you've got a car that small, you want to go for the cute aesthetic rather than the angry aesthetic. If you made it angry, people would call it a Chihuahua."
- European camera mirrors: confirmed legal in Germany and presumed across broader Europe

2026-05-27.title: Why Elon Just Unlocked MASSIVE New Cash Flow for SpaceX AI
2026-05-27.body:
This video from Jo Bhakdi's "Pioneer Lands" channel (cross-posted to jobhakdi) argues that Elon Musk has made a strategically brilliant move by pursuing a partnership and acquisition option with Cursor — the AI coding assistant — combining it with Grok's LLM capabilities and SpaceX's Colossus compute infrastructure to potentially leapfrog Anthropic in the AGI/enterprise AI race. Bhakdi's core thesis is that the key differentiator in AI is not raw model intelligence ("IQ") but the "scaffolding" — the organizational framework, prompt architecture, and agent management layer around the LLM — and that Cursor possesses the world's best scaffolding, making the combination with Grok and SpaceX compute a potential "holy trinity." The video is primarily a strategic analysis of the AGI landscape and SpaceX's positioning, with implications for Tesla investors given the overlap of Elon Musk's entities.

## Market & Competition

1. **AGI capability threshold imminent:** Bhakdi argues that economic AGI — defined as the ability to replace approximately 95–99% of mid-level and higher-level white collar jobs (lawyers, accountants, doctors' intellectual work, etc.) — is now within 3–6 months of being reached as of the video's publish date (May 2026). He states he originally predicted this would be completed by 2027 when he made that call in January 2025, but believes he overestimated the timeline.

2. **Anthropic's explosive growth as benchmark:** Bhakdi highlights Anthropic as currently running at a $45 billion annualized revenue run rate and doubling that run rate every six weeks. He uses Sweden's GDP as a reference point, arguing Anthropic will exceed Swedish GDP in revenue terms by end of 2026 if this trajectory holds. He positions Anthropic and OpenAI as the clear leaders in the AGI space, with Grok materially behind both.

3. **The scaffolding thesis — why Anthropic beats OpenAI and Grok:** Bhakdi's central analytical insight is that raw LLM intelligence ("IQ") is less important than the scaffolding — the hidden prompt systems, agent organization architecture, and cultural/operational structure wrapped around the model. He argues Anthropic likely does not have the best raw LLM (suggesting OpenAI or Grok may have stronger base models) but wins because its scaffolding is superior. He uses Claude Design vs. Claude Code as an internal example: same underlying model, dramatically different performance, entirely due to different scaffolding.

4. **Cursor's unique position — best scaffolding, no LLM:** Bhakdi describes Cursor as having the paradoxically weakest raw AI position (no proprietary LLM, relying on third-party models) but demonstrating through benchmark results that Composer 2.5 — now using Grok — approximates or matches OpenAI's and Anthropic's best models (including Opus and high-tier ChatGPT). He interprets this as proof that Cursor's scaffolding framework is the most advanced in the world, since it achieves near-parity results with a lower-IQ model (Kimi) than competitors use.

5. **The Elon/SpaceX-Cursor deal structure:** Bhakdi describes the deal as SpaceX paying $10 billion as a call option on Cursor, with a requirement to exercise the option within 60 days of Cursor's IPO — which Bhakdi estimates will be by approximately August 2026 — at an acquisition price of $60 billion. He characterizes $60 billion as "peanuts" relative to SpaceX's projected ~$2 trillion valuation.

6. **Anthropic's existing SpaceX compute deal and its vulnerability:** Bhakdi notes that Anthropic is currently paying $1.5 billion per month to SpaceX for compute access on Colossus. He states this deal has a short notice/cancellation period (approximately 60 days) and suggests SpaceX could terminate it if the Grok + Cursor combination proves able to displace Anthropic's product offering — creating a strategic optionality where SpaceX both profits from Anthropic today and is positioned to replace it.

7. **Cursor's enterprise deployment moat:** A key component of Bhakdi's thesis is that Cursor already has deep penetration across Fortune 500 companies — he states he believes Cursor is present in all or nearly all Fortune 500 companies — with existing account managers and a standing deployment infrastructure. He argues this gives SpaceX AI not just a sales channel but an already-installed enterprise footprint for deploying "digital human" (white collar AI replacement) products at scale.

8. **Grok's weakness acknowledged:** Bhakdi is direct in criticizing Grok/xAI's product capabilities, stating they have "no product team," are "bad at product," and have a poor scaffolding/harness layer. He frames Elon's Cursor move as a self-aware acknowledgment of this weakness and a smart solution — acquiring rather than trying to build the scaffolding capability internally.

## Financials

1. **SpaceX revenue trajectory from AI:** Bhakdi projects that the Anthropic compute deal alone — at $1.5 billion per month — has effectively doubled SpaceX's near-term revenue outlook and is now comparable in size to Starlink revenue. He then argues the larger opportunity is SpaceX AI's own "digital human" enterprise product (positioned as a direct Anthropic competitor), projecting tens of billions in revenue in 2027 and hundreds of billions in 2028, which he describes as "completely unrecognized" by the market.

2. **SpaceX valuation context:** Bhakdi references SpaceX's current or near-term valuation range as approximately $1.5–2 trillion, with his prediction being that it reaches roughly $2 trillion before experiencing a pullback, then continuing higher.

3. **Orbital AI compute as long-term infrastructure:** Bhakdi references his November 2025 video as the first coverage of SpaceX's orbital AI satellite business, arguing that orbital AI compute will replace terrestrial AI buildout at scale before 2030. He notes Elon has promised to present the AI satellite concept soon. He frames this as the third leg of the "holy trinity" alongside Cursor's scaffolding and Grok's LLM.

Notable quotes and data:
- "Anthropic is now at a $45 billion revenue run rate and they are doubling [every six weeks]."
- "Anthropic alone will be larger than the Swedish GDP by end of this year."
- "[SpaceX has] a call option that he needs to use within 60 days after IPO, which is probably by August. By August he has to pull the trigger and buy Cursor for $60 billion."
- "Anthropic is paying $1.5 billion per month to SpaceX for compute for Colossus."
- Composer 2.5 (using Grok) is described as "beating OPUS and ChatGPT" and "approximating max and extra high ChatGPT and Opus 4.7."
- "Tens of billions next year [2027] and hundreds of billions in 2028" — projected SpaceX AI revenue.
- "The bare compute lease out... within a week doubled SpaceX's outlook because it's now as big as Starlink, just the Anthropic deal."
- Bhakdi's January 2025 prediction: economic AGI completed by 2027; revised May 2026 estimate: within 6 months (by end of 2026).
- White collar labor replacement TAM cited as "$30 to $40 trillion."

2026-05-27.title: 600kW ChargePoint Express Solo - Powered by Eaton
2026-05-27.body:
This video features Armen Pashnovski from Munro Live interviewing representatives from Eaton (Sai Murhari, Global EVCI Product Manager) and ChargePoint (Erdog, Product Marketing) at ACT Expo 2026 in Las Vegas. The segment focuses on a newly announced joint product — the ChargePoint Express Solo — a 600 kW standalone DC fast charger, and the broader partnership between Eaton's power distribution expertise and ChargePoint's EV charging platform to address EV infrastructure bottlenecks.

## Electric Vehicles
1. **ChargePoint Express Solo — Fastest Standalone Charger on the Market:** The ChargePoint Express Solo is described as the fastest charging standalone solution currently available, capable of delivering up to 600 kW of output at the system level. It can charge two vehicles simultaneously at up to 300 kW per port, and can also function as a cabinet to distribute power to a side dispenser, supporting up to four ports charging simultaneously (averaging 150 kW each). The product was announced just prior to the show and is a brand-new market entry.

2. **Current EV Charging Speed Benchmarks:** The fastest-charging EV currently for sale in North America is cited as the Lucid Gravity, which was observed charging at 400 kW during testing at ChargePoint's facilities. In a theoretical scenario sustaining that power level, it could charge from 20% to 80% in approximately 15 minutes. No production EV currently on the North American market is capable of utilizing the full 600 kW output of the Express Solo.

3. **Cable Theft Prevention — Dual-Layer Security System:** ChargePoint and Eaton have developed a two-level cable theft deterrent system. The first layer consists of cut-resistant cables with embedded high-tensile metal invisible to the user. The second layer is an alarm system called "ChargePoint Protect," which triggers simultaneous alarms and flashing alerts across all chargers at a site when any single cable is cut, and notifies authorities — deterring further theft attempts.

## Energy
1. **Grid Infrastructure Bottleneck:** Eaton's representative emphasized that the existing grid infrastructure is not ready to support high-power charging installations like the 600 kW Express Solo. In approximately 99% of cases, installing such a charger would require a service upgrade, potentially including a new transformer and switchboard. This is a core problem the Eaton–ChargePoint partnership aims to address end-to-end for site owners.

2. **Direct DC Bus Integration with Battery Storage:** A technically distinctive feature of the Express Solo is its internal DC bus architecture, which allows battery storage to be integrated directly into the charger without a separate AC inverter. This reduces capital expenditure, lowers total cost of ownership, and optimizes physical footprint compared to conventional setups where battery storage requires its own inverter stack.

3. **Energy Arbitrage and Battery Storage Trends:** The representatives discussed using co-located battery storage as a practical solution for sites that cannot support 600 kW from the grid alone — charging batteries overnight at low utility rates and discharging during peak demand hours. They noted that in 2025, the U.S. added approximately 19 GW of battery storage capacity, representing roughly 30% growth over the prior year, signaling an accelerating trend toward on-site energy resilience.

4. **Prefabricated Skid Solution for Simplified Deployment:** Eaton is developing a prefabricated, pre-wired skid product that bundles a four-port charging hub, the Express Solo charger, a PowerLink dispenser, and a switchboard into a single deliverable unit. This is designed to eliminate the complexity of piecemeal procurement and installation for site operators. Eaton's Power Distribution Experience Center in Pittsburgh (described as "Disney World for engineers") will serve as a live demo site.

5. **Deployment Timeline:** ChargePoint expects the Express Solo to be available in the field by the end of 2026. One unit is already installed at ChargePoint's headquarters for ongoing testing, and an installation at Eaton's headquarters is planned.

Notable quotes and data:
- 600 kW total output — ChargePoint Express Solo (system level)
- Up to 300 kW per port (two-port simultaneous charging)
- Up to four ports supported when used as a cabinet/dispenser hub (averaging 150 kW each)
- Lucid Gravity observed at 400 kW charging rate during ChargePoint testing
- Theoretical 20–80% charge in ~15 minutes for the Lucid Gravity at sustained 400 kW
- ~99% of existing sites would require infrastructure upgrades (new transformer/switchboard) to support 600 kW
- U.S. added ~19 GW of battery storage capacity in 2025, ~30% more than the prior year
- "Engineers joke that it's Disney World for engineers" — describing Eaton's Pittsburgh Power Distribution Experience Center
- Expected field deployment: by end of 2026

2026-05-27.title: Tesla Reveals Major New Roadster Update
2026-05-27.body:
This episode of The Tesla Space covers three main stories: the long-awaited Tesla Roadster's production plans finally crystallizing around Giga Texas, the Boring Company's shift toward centralized remote tunneling operations, and Tesla's accelerating Full Self-Driving rollout across Europe. The episode's core thesis is that Tesla's most ambitious and delayed projects — the Roadster, FSD in Europe — are moving from speculation into concrete execution, while the Boring Company is quietly transforming itself from a construction contractor into an automation company.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Tesla Roadster confirmed for Giga Texas production:** Tesla VP of Vehicle Engineering Lars Morvi and chief designer Franz von Holleshausen confirmed on the Ride the Lightning podcast that the next-generation Roadster will be built at Tesla headquarters in Giga Texas. Morvi stated: "We can say it's going to be built in Texas. We've made first plans on that and you start to see a lot of things start to unfold in the next months." The video frames this as a meaningful milestone — allocating production space implies tooling, engineering validation, and factory planning are converging around a real vehicle program, not just a concept.

2. **Roadster's production location history and Tesla's strategic shift to Texas:** When the Roadster was first unveiled, Tesla planned to build it in Fremont. During the Q2 2020 earnings call, Elon Musk said the Roadster would make sense as a California-built product. That has since changed, with Tesla increasingly concentrating its newest and most ambitious programs — Cybercab, Optimus, Terafab, and now the Roadster — around Giga Texas. The video notes the symbolic fit: SpaceX's Starship is built in Texas, and the Roadster is described as a Tesla/SpaceX collaboration confirmed by Elon Musk in 2024.

3. **Original Roadster specs and the delay problem:** The Roadster was first unveiled in November 2017 at Tesla's semi-event, with specs that seemed near-impossible at the time: 0–60 mph in 1.9 seconds, 0–100 in 4.2 seconds, a quarter-mile in 8.8 seconds, over 620 miles of range, and a top speed exceeding 250 mph. Originally targeting 2020 deliveries, the car never launched. The video argues that the industry has since caught up — Tesla's own Model S Plaid (launched 2021) matched the 1.9-second 0–60 claim, and competitors like Lucid, Porsche, Rimac, and Xiaomi's SU7 Ultra (claimed 1.98 seconds at a fraction of the Roadster's expected price) have reached similar or better figures. Simply matching the original specs would no longer be revolutionary in 2026.

4. **Roadster's evolved identity — the last great driver's car:** Elon Musk has repeatedly hinted at a far more extreme version of the Roadster than originally planned. In 2018 he mentioned an optional SpaceX package using small cold gas thrusters (similar to those used on the Falcon 9 for stabilization during re-entry) to enhance acceleration, braking, and cornering. He has also claimed the car could hit 0–60 in under 1 second, and stated: "There will never be another car like this, if you could even call it a car." Most significantly, during Tesla's Q1 2026 earnings call, Musk said: "Over time, it's going to make sense for our whole lineup to be autonomous vehicles of different sizes. Long-term, the only manually driven car will be the new Tesla Roadster." This reframes the Roadster as not just the fastest car in the world, but potentially the last great manually driven car before full autonomy arrives.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD Supervised approved in Lithuania — second EU country:** Tesla received regulatory approval to deploy FSD Supervised in Lithuania, making it the second European country to activate the system after the Netherlands. Lithuania used the EU's mutual recognition framework to leverage the Dutch approval rather than starting from scratch, completing its own process in under 40 days. By contrast, the Dutch Vehicle Authority had spent more than 18 months evaluating the system using 1.12 million miles of European driving data. Tesla had been quietly preparing behind the scenes — opening FSD ride-along experiences at its Vilnius showroom in late April and hiring FSD vehicle operators in Lithuania and eight other European countries around the same time.

2. **Greece poised to be the third EU country:** The Greek Secretary General of Transport has publicly stated that Greece intends to adopt FSD Supervised using the same Dutch mutual recognition framework as part of an upcoming transportation bill. Greece had hoped to be the second European country to approve it but was narrowly beaten by Lithuania. The video identifies a clear pattern: Tesla is building country-by-country momentum using mutual recognition rules already embedded in the European regulatory system, rather than waiting for a slow continent-wide process.

3. **European FSD mileage milestones and safety data:** Tesla Europe announced that drivers in the Netherlands and Lithuania have collectively logged more than 12.5 million miles (20 million kilometers) with FSD Supervised active. That milestone was reached less than three days after the same markets crossed 9.3 million miles (15 million kilometers) — meaning roughly 3 million miles were added in under 72 hours. Dutch Tesla owners alone surpassed 6.2 million miles in under a month after launch. Tesla also reported that when FSD Supervised is active, the probability of a collision per kilometer driven is up to seven times lower compared to manual driving.

Notable quotes and data:
- Lars Morvi: "We can say it's going to be built in Texas. We've made first plans on that and you start to see a lot of things start to unfold in the next months."
- Elon Musk (Q1 2026 earnings call): "Over time, it's going to make sense for our whole lineup to be autonomous vehicles of different sizes. Long-term, the only manually driven car will be the new Tesla Roadster."
- Elon Musk on the Roadster: "There will never be another car like this, if you could even call it a car."
- Roadster original specs (2017 reveal): 0–60 mph in 1.9 sec, 0–100 in 4.2 sec, quarter-mile in 8.8 sec, 620+ miles range, 250+ mph top speed.
- FSD Supervised collision probability: up to 7x lower per km vs. manual driving.
- Netherlands FSD evaluation: 18+ months using 1.12 million miles of European driving data.
- Lithuania approval timeline: under 40 days via mutual recognition framework.
- Combined Netherlands + Lithuania FSD miles: 12.5 million miles (20 million km).
- Dutch owners alone: 6.2 million miles in under one month post-launch.
- Vegas Loop full vision: ~68 miles of tunnels, 100+ stations.
- Boring Company tunnel permit timeline: up to 6 months per permit currently.
- Clark County Commissioner Jib Gibson: "The project is now ready to explode."

2026-05-28.title: Tesla Just Dropped Huge Cybercab And Roadster Updates
2026-05-28.body:
This video from brighterwithherbert features host Herbert and guest Brian White (of the FutureAzA YouTube channel) discussing a range of Tesla news updates, including new technology spotted on Cybercab test vehicles, Roadster development progress, China market developments, and Supercharger expansion. The core thesis is that multiple converging signals — Cybercab hardware refinements, FSD rebranding in China, and infrastructure buildout — reinforce Tesla's long-term autonomous and energy business thesis.

## Robotaxi

1. **Cybercabs Spotted with Starlink Mini Units in Austin:** Multiple Cybercab units were spotted driving in tandem around Austin with Starlink Mini satellite dishes bolted to the rear hatch. Brian White explains that while Cybercabs are known to use 5G as their primary connectivity, Starlink Mini would serve as a redundant backup communication system — critical for scenarios involving cellular dead zones, tower outages, or large-scale fleet coordination. He also raises the possibility that for a fleet eventually reaching one million vehicles, Tesla would want independence from any single carrier like AT&T, and that Starlink could be used to offload heavy data tasks (such as overnight software updates) invisibly and cost-effectively.

2. **Cybercab Confirmed at 165 Wh/Mile Efficiency:** Lars Morvy (Tesla's VP of Vehicle Engineering) confirmed in an interview on the Ride the Lightning podcast that the Cybercab has a certified efficiency of 165 Wh per mile, making it the most efficient vehicle Tesla has ever produced. Brian White noted that when he spoke with Tesla engineers, they indicated 5.5 miles per kilowatt hour is what they are "allowed to say," implying real-world performance is even better. He attributed this to a virtuous cycle of weight reduction, aerodynamic optimization (no mirrors, sleek profile), and right-sized motors — potentially using new rare-earth-free motor designs. He contrasted this with competitors, noting that Cybercab's efficiency means less time needed for charging compared to rivals like Waymo.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Next-Gen Roadster Confirmed for Giga Texas, Alpha Prototypes Testing:** Tesla executives confirmed the next-generation Roadster will be manufactured at Giga Texas. Alpha prototypes are already in testing. Lars Morvy described it as the first time Tesla has designed a motor with a "pure performance mentality." Joe Tegtmeyer also confirmed the Roadster's Texas home and highlighted that Giga Texas is becoming ground zero for Tesla's most important products — including the Model Y, Cybertruck, Cybercab, Optimus, Cortex data centers, and a SpaceX chip fab. Brian White expressed a "hope against hope" that the now-sold-out X Takeover event on October 10th could serve as the Roadster's reveal, given the new test track being built at Giga Texas and the proximity of the delivery center.

2. **New Test Track Under Construction at Giga Texas:** A new video shows Tesla building a large test track at Giga Texas. While the general purpose is vehicle testing, speculation points to the Roadster as a likely use case. Brian noted that having an on-site test track is standard for major automakers and suggested it could also be used for owner events near the delivery center.

## Market & Competition

1. **China Issues 154,000 NEV License Plate Quotas Targeting BEV Buyers:** The Chinese government introduced 154,000 new NEV license plate quotas exclusively for battery electric vehicles (not hybrids or range-extended EVs), with 119,000 reserved for families and 35,000 for individuals. The family eligibility cutoff score hit a historic low of 36 points, meaning younger, tech-savvy, middle-class urban families are now qualifying for plates. Brian White provided context on China's urban congestion-management system, explaining that license plates in major cities like Beijing are lottery-based and can cost thousands of dollars — but EV plates were historically easier to obtain as an incentive. One analyst cited in the video estimates Tesla could gain approximately 23,000 new sales if it captures roughly 15% of this quota allocation, given that Model Y and Model 3 buyers represent the exact target demographic.

2. **Tesla Rebranding FSD in China to "Tesla Assisted Driving":** Tesla China has renamed its supervised FSD offering to "Tesla Assisted Driving" in the Chinese owner's manual. Three tiers are visible: Tesla Assisted Driving, Enhanced Assisted Driving, and Basic Assisted Driving. Brian White and Herbert interpreted this as semantics rather than a capability downgrade — a signal that Tesla is preparing for a broader FSD rollout in China. Herbert noted that Tesla previously launched FSD in China in a very limited form (with restricted data usage) to satisfy the requirement for a locally sequestered data center, and that the hiring activity around that data center suggests a nationwide expansion is now possible.

3. **Optimus in China: ~80% Probability Discussed:** Herbert and Brian discussed the possibility of Tesla building an Optimus factory in China and selling Optimus robots there. Brian explained that China may require the same data-sequestration model used for FSD — local training data centers, no data in or out — before permitting a bipedal robot with indoor mobility. Herbert put the probability of China allowing Tesla to sell Optimus and build a factory there at approximately 80%, citing the FSD data center precedent as the blueprint.

4. **Ferrari's New Electric Flagship Criticized for Inefficiency:** As a contrast to Cybercab's efficiency, the hosts briefly discussed Ferrari's new electric flagship (referred to colloquially as "Lucy Goosey"), noting it carries a battery larger than a Cybertruck but delivers less range than a Cybertruck — requiring 800V architecture and 365 kW charging just to compensate for its inefficiency.

## Energy

1. **Tesla Supercharger Card Now Available to Non-Tesla Owners in China via WeChat:** Tesla China announced that non-Tesla EV owners can now use Tesla Superchargers by paying via WeChat prepaid cards — eliminating the need to download the Tesla app. Brian White characterized this as a frictionless payment expansion. The video cited a projection that adding just two non-Tesla charging sessions per stall daily across 1,000 open stations (averaging 10 stalls each) would generate approximately 600,000 kWh of additional daily energy sales, translating to roughly $45 million USD in annual revenue.

2. **Tesla Oasis Sets Record at 164 Stalls, Solar + Megapack Powered:** Tesla Oasis in Lost Hills, California — the world's largest charging station with 164 stalls — peaked at 112 simultaneous cars charging on Memorial Day weekend. The station is powered entirely by solar and Megapacks, with only a minimal grid connection retained as an emergency backup. Brian White explained this architecture avoided the prohibitively expensive cost of upgrading transmission lines and transformers back to a substation. He noted the station was intentionally overbuilt so it would not reach capacity even on peak holiday weekends for years to come. He discussed the economics of replicating this model: ground-mount solar (as used at Lost Hills) is the cheapest option; canopies are most expensive but justified in high-electricity-cost states like California or at premium retail locations.

3. **Tesla Superchargers Expanding Globally:** Tesla charging announced its first Supercharger stations in Colombia, continuing Latin American expansion. Additionally, Volvo announced that starting in Q4 2026, Volvo EV drivers will be able to access more than 20,000 Supercharger stations across 29 European countries directly through the Volvo cars app.

4. **Tesla Asia Megapack Factory — Two-Year Buildout Milestone:** Photos shared from Tesla Asia showed a Megapack factory that went from groundbreaking to operational in exactly two years (as of May 23rd). Discussion followed about whether a future Optimus factory in China could follow a similar rapid buildout trajectory.

Notable quotes and data:
- Cybercab efficiency: **165 Wh per mile** — confirmed by Lars Morvy; Brian White says engineers told him "5.5 miles per kWh is what we're allowed to say," implying real-world performance is better
- China NEV quota: **154,000 plates** (119,000 family, 35,000 individual), exclusively for BEVs
- Estimated Tesla China sales from quota: **~23,000 vehicles** if Tesla captures ~15% of allocation
- WeChat Supercharger revenue projection: **~$45M USD annually** from 2 extra non-Tesla sessions/stall/day across 1,000 stations at 10 stalls each
- Tesla Oasis, Lost Hills CA: **164 stalls**, world's largest charging station, **peaked at 112 cars** on Memorial Day; powered by solar + Megapacks
- Volvo EV access to Tesla Superchargers: **20,000+ stations** across **29 European countries**, starting **Q4 2026**
- Brian White (FutureAzA): "If you have a Waymo versus a Cybercab, but the Cybercab doesn't have to go into supercharging maybe two or three hours a day less than the Waymo does — you've just become more car, less cars needed to be out there servicing."
- On Starlink Mini: "If for some reason the entire fleet were to be getting too high where it's going to incur additional costs, they could determine should we shift some of the load to Starlink... entirely invisible to you and I and impossible to every one of their competitors."

2026-05-28.title: Tesla’s Rivals Keep Copying The Vision-Only Strategy
2026-05-28.body:
This video from brighterwithherbert features host Herbert and guest Brian White (of the FutureAzA YouTube channel) reviewing a series of competitive moves in the autonomous driving and EV space, including updates on Stellantis, Mercedes, Xiaomi, Waymo, and Pony AI. The central thesis is that Tesla's vision-only, neural-net-first approach is increasingly being validated as competitors either pivot toward it (Xiaomi/Xpeng) or continue struggling with lidar-dependent systems. The discussion also covers Tesla's European sales recovery and the unit economics challenges facing robotaxi competitors.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Tesla Europe Sales Rebound Continues:** New car registrations for Tesla vehicles across the European Union, UK, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland jumped 46.5% year-over-year last month (April 2026), totaling 10,654 units. In the EU alone, sales grew over 67% from a year earlier. This marks the third consecutive month of growth, following an improvement of over 84% in March 2026 and nearly 12% in February 2026. Brian White contextualizes this as a return to pre-refresh levels rather than a new high, noting Tesla is holding steady with the same core lineup despite intensifying competition and lower-priced alternatives.

2. **FSD Europe Approval Has Not Yet Impacted Sales:** Brian White argues that FSD approval in Lithuania and the Netherlands has had essentially no measurable effect on sales yet — perhaps five units out of roughly 10,000. He reasons that awareness is low, the product is only in very limited hands, and customers won't purchase until FSD is approved in their specific country and clearly available today.

3. **Xiaomi YU7 Standard Edition Launches at $33,000:** Xiaomi released a new standard trim of the YU7 — a vehicle frequently positioned as a Model Y competitor — priced at approximately $33,000. Brian White notes Xiaomi is losing roughly $5,000 per car, which structurally limits their ability to scale since selling more vehicles only deepens losses. He explains Xiaomi did not build its first car (the SU7) in-house but contracted a state-run manufacturer, then subsequently purchased that factory. He views it as a strong first effort but one still exhibiting early-production quirks.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Xiaomi/Xpeng Vision-Only Pivot Validates Tesla's Approach:** Xpeng CEO He Xiaopeng publicly stated the company is "absolutely adamant" they no longer need lidar, even though he acknowledged it is good technology. Brian White notes this declaration was first made in July 2024, after which lidar on existing Xpeng vehicles was deprecated and is now purely ornamental. He positions Xpeng as the current leader in end-to-end neural net autonomous driving in China, ahead of competitors still relying on Huawei's lidar-based platform. He argues that Huawei functions as the "Intel Inside" of FSD in China but has not yet fully adopted neural net approaches due to AI chip export restrictions.

2. **Stellantis Announces $70 Billion EV and Autonomy Plan with Wave AI:** Stellantis announced a €60 billion strategic plan to build 29 new EVs by 2030, with nine priced under €30,000, on a dedicated EV architecture. Their partner Wave AI announced it will bring the Wave AI driver to Stellantis's auto-drive platform, promising hands-free, door-to-door supervised automated driving across urban streets and highways, launching in 2028. Brian White acknowledges the plan has real strategic necessity — EU regulations require all-electric vehicles by 2035 — but remains skeptical Wave AI is the best partner and notes the system is still lidar-based.

3. **Mercedes Plans Automated Driving Rollout in Germany by End of 2026:** Mercedes announced plans to deploy a point-to-point automated driving system (not highway-only) in selected German cities by the end of 2026, with nationwide rollout planned for 2027. The hosts speculate it may involve Nvidia's Alpamayo platform but note that platform was only recently announced and could not realistically be integrated into production vehicles in under a year. Brian White gives roughly 10% odds this timeline is met, calling it structurally implausible for a company as large as Mercedes to execute that quickly, and notes Mercedes previously abandoned its Level 3 highway system after minimal consumer adoption.

4. **Waymo Pauses Atlanta Service Over Flooded Road Incidents:** A gold-painted Waymo driverless vehicle was spotted in Los Angeles, which the hosts note visually echoes Tesla's Cybercab. More significantly, Waymo paused service in Atlanta after vehicles repeatedly drove into flooded areas — a software recall was issued. Brian White provides context: Waymo first over-corrected by stopping for any puddle, then pushed an update to drive through them, leading to the current problem. He contrasts this with Tesla's FSD, which he says uses neural net reasoning to assess whether another vehicle's behavior in similar conditions makes the path safe.

## Robotaxi

1. **Pony AI Raises Fleet Target to 3,500 Vehicles by End of 2026:** Pony AI announced it is raising its robotaxi fleet target to 3,500 vehicles by the end of 2026 — an increase of 500 — after reporting stronger-than-expected Q1 2026 revenue of $34 million against an average estimate of $21 million. The company now expects full-year robotaxi revenue to grow 3.5 times its 2025 level. However, Pony AI reported a net loss of $58 million against that $34 million revenue, meaning they are losing nearly twice what they earn. The hosts note their fares would need to be roughly 300% higher to break even, though some costs won't scale linearly.

2. **Robotaxi Unit Economics Remain Deeply Challenged Across the Industry:** The hosts highlight systemic profitability problems across robotaxi operators. Waymo is losing approximately $5 billion per year and roughly $100 per ride. Pony AI's losses suggest fares are underpriced by approximately 70% relative to break-even. Brian White argues these are structural problems requiring fundamental fixes, not incremental fare increases, and that scale will only partially help since some costs (compute, vehicles) don't fall proportionally.

## Market & Competition

1. **Lidar vs. Vision-Only Debate Continues to Favor Vision:** The hosts argue that every lidar-first company is underperforming Tesla in autonomous driving capability. Waymo's Atlanta flood incident is cited as an example of lidar's inability to substitute for genuine intelligence and neural net reasoning. Brian White contends that FSD supervised today is "vastly safer than a human driving," citing distractions like phone use as a persistent human problem, and argues the industry is moving toward vision-centric end-to-end systems pioneered by Tesla and now being adopted by Xpeng in China.

2. **China AV Market Faces Regulatory Headwinds:** The hosts reference a prior incident in China where widespread outages of BYD robotaxis caused major traffic disruptions, prompting regulators to freeze new permits for high-level self-driving vehicles. This backdrop makes Pony AI's fleet expansion ambitions more challenging even as their revenues improve.

Notable quotes and data:
- Tesla Europe registrations: +46.5% YoY in April 2026; 10,654 units across EU, UK, and four other markets
- EU-only Tesla sales: +67% YoY in April 2026
- Month-over-month growth trend: +84% in March 2026, +12% in February 2026
- Xiaomi YU7 Standard Edition: ~$33,000; losing ~$5,000 per unit
- Stellantis plan: €60 billion, 29 new EVs by 2030, 9 under €30,000, autonomy partnership with Wave AI launching 2028
- Pony AI Q1 2026 revenue: $34 million (vs. $21 million average estimate); net loss: $58 million
- Pony AI full-year 2026 robotaxi revenue target: 3.5x their 2025 level
- Pony AI fleet target: 3,500 vehicles by end of 2026
- Waymo losses: ~$5 billion/year; ~$100 per ride
- Brian White on Alpamayo/Mercedes timeline: "10% odds" of deployment by end of 2026
- Brian White on Xpeng lidar deprecation: "It's ornamental. It's decorative."
- On Waymo flood issue: "This is the Michael Scott navigation."

2026-05-28.title: Tesla’s own AI trainers don’t trust ‘Full Self-Driving’ or its safety stats, Reuters finds
2026-05-28.body:
A Reuters investigation, based on interviews with nine former Tesla data labelers, a former self-driving engineer, and 11 traffic-safety researchers, finds that Tesla's FSD safety statistics are methodologically flawed and that the company's own AI trainers overwhelmingly distrust the technology.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **Safety statistics inflated by a factor of three:** Tesla executives — including CEO Elon Musk, CFO Vaibhav Taneja, and Board Chair Robyn Denholm — have repeatedly claimed FSD is up to 10 times safer than human drivers, with Musk displaying a chart at a November shareholder meeting claiming "85% less crashes." Reuters found that Tesla compared airbag-deployment crashes in its own fleet against federal data that includes all crashes requiring a tow truck — a far less severe threshold. University of Michigan researcher Marco Benedetti performed the correct apples-to-apples comparison (airbag crashes vs. airbag crashes) and found the result dropped from "10x safer" to roughly three times farther between crashes. That figure itself remains unreliable due to the age gap between Tesla's fleet (4.1 years average) and the overall U.S. fleet (12.8 years). Ten of 11 traffic-safety researchers who reviewed the methodology told Reuters it amounted to misleading marketing.

2. **Tesla's own data labelers don't trust FSD:** Seven of the nine former data labelers told Reuters they wouldn't trust FSD to drive them. One said he wouldn't ride in a Tesla robotaxi "if you fucking paid me." A veteran self-driving engineer who reviewed Tesla crash data for years called the company's safety claims "bullshit" and said: "Definitely, don't trust Elon on this." Labelers described routinely seeing FSD fail to yield to emergency vehicles, give motorcyclists adequate space, brake on freeway off-ramps, and avoid construction zones. A specialized "trauma team" in Palo Alto reviewed near-misses with pedestrians, including clips of FSD-piloted vehicles nearly hitting children and failing to recognize pedestrians in crosswalks. FSD was also reported regularly exceeding speed limits by 20–30 mph after Tesla introduced a "Mad Max" aggressive driving mode, with one reported instance of 60 mph in a 25-mph zone.

3. **NHTSA scrutiny and legal exposure:** NHTSA currently has four active investigations into FSD and Autopilot, including a probe into dozens of cases where FSD ran red lights or turned into oncoming traffic, and a review of whether Tesla's 2023 Autopilot recall was sufficient. Tesla was also hit with a $243 million verdict after an Autopilot crash in Florida killed a 22-year-old woman. Despite Musk's November statement that Tesla would soon allow drivers to text while using FSD, the feature has not been enabled six months later; Tesla's own FSD website continues to state the system requires active driver supervision.

## Robotaxi

1. **Extensive pre-launch mapping contradicts Musk's "no HD maps" claim:** Reuters found that Tesla conducted weeks of intensive nightly testing and mapping at the Warner Bros. studio lot before the October 2024 Cybercab unveiling, and similarly mapped Austin's limited robotaxi zone extensively before its June 2025 launch — annotating curbs, traffic lights, road signs, and road markings. The Utah data-labeling staff doubled to approximately 300 workers in the six months before the Austin launch. This directly contradicts Musk's repeated claim that Tesla's approach does not require the "laborious local mapping" used by rivals like Waymo. One former employee described the Austin zone: "You can't get creative outside of that."

2. **Unsupervised fleet remains very small:** Nearly a year after the Austin launch, Tesla still operates only about 20 unsupervised robotaxis there within a limited and carefully mapped zone. Some vehicles still carry human safety monitors in the front seat. The Reuters findings explain the scaling difficulty: the labor-intensive, zone-specific mapping and annotation process is extremely hard to replicate broadly.

## Editorial Stance
Author Fred Lambert states the Reuters findings confirm what Electrek has long documented — that Tesla's safety claims don't hold up — and calls the statistical methodology choice (using a metric that inflated safety claims 3x despite access to correct data) deliberate rather than accidental. Lambert also flags a new complacency risk: as FSD improves on HW4 hardware, drivers are becoming less attentive, making the remaining edge-case failures more dangerous, and argues Tesla is not doing enough to address this.

Notable quotes and data:
- "It's like saying: 'My jet airplane is faster than your World War II bomber.' Yeah, so, what's your point?" — Carnegie Mellon professor Phil Koopman
- "Definitely, don't trust Elon on this." — former Tesla self-driving engineer
- One labeler: he wouldn't ride in a Tesla robotaxi "if you fucking paid me"
- Tesla fleet average age: 4.1 years vs. U.S. fleet average: 12.8 years
- Safety claim inflation factor: ~3x, per University of Michigan researcher Marco Benedetti's corrected comparison
- Austin unsupervised robotaxi count: ~20 vehicles, per Reuters
- Utah labeling staff pre-Austin launch: ~300 workers (doubled in six months)
- Tesla $243 million verdict in Florida Autopilot wrongful death case
- NHTSA: 4 active FSD/Autopilot investigations currently open

2026-05-28.title: Why Tesla's Robotaxi Rollout Stalled / Many Are Wrong About Elon's Voting Percentage ⚡️
2026-05-28.body:
This episode of "Electrified," hosted by Dillon Loomis, covers the current state of Tesla's robotaxi rollout and why fleet growth has stalled, along with a detailed breakdown of Elon Musk's actual real-world voting power at Tesla versus the commonly cited beneficial ownership figure. The video also touches on Megapack 3 deployments in Europe, EU EV sales data, Optimus factory construction progress, FSD updates, and several SpaceX-related developments.

## Robotaxi

1. **Fleet Growth Has Stalled Since Mid-May:** According to the third-party tracker (RobotaxiTracker.com), fleet growth effectively paused in all three Texas cities around May 9th. Of the 26 active vehicles tracked over the past 30 days, 21 are unsupervised, and just under 80% of rides over the past 7 days have been unsupervised. A photo shared by a community member shows 13 Cybercabs parked in Dallas that "appear to be asleep for now," suggesting they are on-site but not yet deployed.

2. **Houston Depot Activity Suggests Preparation:** A community observer named Aron noted that many Model Y vehicles at the Houston robotaxi depot have their hazard lights on, speculating they may be undergoing retrofits (possibly for a rear washer camera). Some of these Model Ys are launch edition vehicles not available for sale. Separately, employees were observed removing carpeting and parts from trunks. Last week, all Model 3s, Cybertrucks, and non-robotaxi vehicles were removed from the lot, leaving only Cybercabs and Model Ys. Dillon interprets this as Tesla being in "all hands on deck" mode preparing Cybercabs for imminent deployment.

3. **Cybercab Production Timeline and Deployment Thesis:** Tesla announced the first Cybercab off the production line at Giga Texas on February 17th, with a broader production announcement on April 23rd. The pause in Model Y fleet expansion appears to coincide with the arrival of Cybercabs in Austin, Dallas, and Houston. Dillon's personal expectation is approximately 30 Cybercabs in Austin and 10–15 each in Dallas and Houston over the coming weeks. He believes serious scale will wait until a future FSD version (referred to as V15), expected later in 2025.

4. **Five New Cities Must Launch Within 33 Days:** Tesla's own slide deck commits to launching robotaxi service in five new cities, and as of the video's date, that deadline is approximately 33 days away. Dillon emphasizes that commitments in Tesla's official slide deck should carry significantly more weight than off-the-cuff comments Elon makes in interviews. He believes Tesla is hyperfocused on meeting these city-launch milestones and does not want to face the backlash of missing them.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD 14.3 Mixed Performance:** Dillon reports that FSD version 14.3 demonstrated impressive supervised FSD behavior in a complex traffic scene in the Netherlands. However, it also showed a concerning parking failure where the vehicle would have driven into a shopping cart stall without human intervention. Dillon has also experienced some phantom braking on 14.3 in limited testing. He emphasizes that the most significant aspect of 14.3 is Tesla's rewrite of the compiler and runtime from the ground up, positioning it as a foundational building block for future releases rather than a polished end product.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus Factory Steel Structure Goes Up:** Joe Tegtmeyer reported that the first steel structure has been erected at the construction site for an Optimus factory with a stated capacity of 10 million units per year, and that the second phase of land reclamation is underway. A screenshot was shared showing the first steel going up at the site.

## Energy

1. **Megapack 3 Heading to Belgium:** Tesla's newest Megapack 3 will be deployed in one of Europe's most significant battery storage projects, with Belgian company Spy installing 180 units on the site of a former power plant. Installation and grid connection work is scheduled to begin in November 2025, with testing and commissioning expected to be completed by end of 2027. The project will have a storage capacity of several hundred megawatt hours and a total project value exceeding $116 million. This will be one of the first large-scale Megapack 3 deployments in Europe.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Tesla EU Sales Up 45.8% Year-to-Date:** New ACA data through April shows Tesla sold 89,429 vehicles in the EU, EFTA, and UK year-to-date, up from 61,343 in the same period last year — a 45.8% increase. Tesla's overall market share rose from 1.4% to 1.9%. Dillon cautions that comparisons are distorted because Q1 and Q2 of last year saw Tesla transitioning to the refreshed Model Y and Model 3. He hopes a broader supervised FSD rollout later in the year will accelerate momentum further.

2. **Chinese Automakers Outpacing Tesla in Europe:** BYD sold over 101,000 vehicles in EU/EFTA/UK markets in the first four months of the year, up nearly 144% year-over-year, exceeding Tesla's volume. Chery Auto also outsold Tesla in this period with sales growth of 338% year-over-year. Dillon notes that lower price points and more available models contribute to these figures, but flags the Chinese automaker surge as a significant storyline. Hybrids continue to dominate EU consumer preference at 38.2% market share versus full BEVs at 19.7%.

## Market & Competition

1. **Elon's Real-World Voting Power Is 11%, Not 20%:** Dillon provides a detailed breakdown of the difference between Elon Musk's SEC-reported beneficial ownership and his actual real-world voting power. The 13G/A filing shows approximately 717 million shares classified as beneficial ownership (~20.3%), but this includes 303 million unexercised options from the 2018 compensation award that do not currently carry voting rights. Elon's actual real-world voting power today is based only on the ~413 million shares he fully owns in a revocable trust, divided by Tesla's actual outstanding share count of approximately 3.75 billion — yielding an 11% real-world voting percentage.

2. **Options Exercise Window Opens Path to 17.6%:** Per a new implementation agreement following the Delaware court case, Elon's window to exercise the 303 million 2018 award options runs from May 21st through August 15th of this year. If Elon doesn't exercise them himself, Tesla will exercise them on his behalf. Once exercised, those shares will be added to both the numerator and denominator: 717 million divided by approximately 4.059 billion outstanding shares would give Elon a 17.6% real-world voting stake. The tax event for those shares is expected to be pushed to 2028 when shares vest, not at the time of exercise, with a 5-year holding period extending through 2033.

3. **2025 Award and Path to 28.1%:** The newer 2025 compensation award covers approximately 423 million shares already included in Tesla's outstanding share count. These shares are currently subject to a voting proxy given to Tesla's secretary, voted proportionately to other shareholders — meaning Elon has no voting control over them now. The award has 12 tranches, each worth approximately 35 million shares. As Elon earns each tranche by hitting market cap and operational milestones (implying Tesla reaching approximately an $8.5 trillion market cap for full vesting), voting rights transfer to him. If all tranches are earned, Elon's total voting control would reach approximately 28.1% — near or above his stated goal of 25%, estimated to occur around tranches 8 or 9.

4. **SpaceX Merger Speculation:** Peter Diamandis, a friend of Elon Musk and early SpaceX investor, stated that a post-IPO merger between SpaceX and Tesla is "inevitable" and a question of timing, primarily because Elon would want to consolidate voting power across his companies. Elon currently holds 85.1% voting control at SpaceX (prior to IPO filing). The FTSE Russell indices announced fast-entry enhancements allowing qualifying IPOs to join relevant indices just 5 days after IPO, changes Dillon notes were largely put in place for SpaceX, enabling more forced institutional buying shortly after listing.

5. **Rivian R2 Launch June 9th:** Rivian announced the R2 will launch on June 9th with order invites, first customer deliveries, and demo drives beginning. Dillon characterizes the R2's success or failure as likely a make-or-break moment for Rivian.
